audits.st: not reported

audits.st: National and international guidelines: fracture risk assessment with clinical factors and BMD to guide bone agent use and bone protection advice for patients on ADT
audits.f: 4.9% were already known to the osteoporosis service, but none had been referred for bone health assessment when ADT started.
audits.c: Joint urology-osteoporosis guideline and management pathway for bone health assessment on ADT, with patient information, signposting and bone agent initiation by a trained team.

audits.t: E012 An audit examining specialist referral for osteoporosis treatment for rheumatoid arthritis patients using new NOGG (National Osteoporosis Guideline Group) Guidelines 2022
audits.st: NOGG 2022 guidance on specialist referral based on FRAX and other risk factors
audits.f: Mean major osteoporotic fracture risk 15.6 and hip fracture risk 4.7 over 10 years; 31.6% had previous fracture; 26.3% on steroids (10.5% high dose); 5% had received parenteral treatment. A significant number would need specialist referral under NOGG 2022 (number not given).

audits.t: P001 An audit to assess whether patients who had a delayed or missed denosumab dose during the covid-19 pandemic came to any harm or suffered a subsequent fracture
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 34/166 (21%) did not receive denosumab on time; 21/166 (12.6%) delayed and 13/166 (7.8%) missed; 8/166 (4.8%) sustained a fracture, 6 of whom had a delayed or missed dose during Covid-19.

audits.t: E051 Audit of the management of patients over 75 with osteoporotic fragility fractures in primary care
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: NICE guidance on anti-resorptive or anabolic treatment after osteoporotic fragility fracture
audits.f: 51% not on any fracture prevention medication (reasons explained in 40%); 39% taking bisphosphonates; 10% prescribed but not taking oral bisphosphonates.
audits.c: Dedicated clinics (telephone or face to face) to discuss management and start medication
audits.r2: 49% started on medication; 9% refused; 17% deemed inappropriate; 25% had died or left the practice.

audits.t: P058 Anabolic treatment of osteoporosis: an audit on safety events from a teaching hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Teriparatide (n=24): 17 (70%) had a documented post-teriparatide plan, 2 adverse events, no fractures after cessation. Romosozumab (n=26): 7 adverse events including heart failure and hypocalcaemia, no fractures after cessation. All met NICE criteria.

audits.t: E050 Parathyroidectomy vs pharmacological strategies in the management of bone health in patients with primary hyperparathyroidism: a service improvement audit
audits.tp: Bone health management in primary hyperparathyroidism
audits.st: NICE NG132 (2019): parathyroidectomy as definitive treatment, cinacalcet if surgery inappropriate
audits.f: Parathyroidectomy in 21 (32.8%); cinacalcet 10 (15.6%); alendronic acid 37 (68.5%), denosumab 24 (37.5%), zoledronic acid 10 (18.5%), risedronate 2 (3.7%); fragility fractures in 41 (64%).

audits.t: E051 Diagnosis and monitoring of Paget’s disease of bone: an audit across hospital departments in secondary care
audits.tp: Paget's disease of bone investigation and treatment
audits.st: Paget's Association, ECTS and IOF clinical guideline (February 2019)
audits.f: Targeted X-ray or CT in 127/143 (88.8%); bone scan in 38.4% (68.3% rheumatology v 22.6% other departments); ALP available in all rheumatology and 88.7% of other patients; bisphosphonates in 36.1% (73.3% rheumatology v 9.4% other).

audits.t: Independent sector and peri‐operative cardiac arrest as reported to the 7th National Audit Project of the Royal College of Anaesthetists
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 174/442 (39%) independent hospitals participated; preparedness survey response 23 (13%); activity survey (1912 responses) suggested suboptimal compliance with monitoring recommendations; 17 cardiac arrest reports (2% of NAP7).

audits.t: Data quality audit of a clinical quality registry: a generic framework and case study of the Australian and New Zealand Hip Fracture Registry.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Literature-derived benchmarks for data agreement and completeness (very high if ≥95%, high 90–94%, moderate 80–84%)
audits.f: Overall data agreement 82.3% (7111/8639 items), moderate; overall data completeness 95.6% (8258/8639), very high. Lowest agreement for ED departure time (27.0%) and time of surgery (33.1%).

audits.t: THROMBOPROPHYLAXIS FOR AMBULATORY PATIENTS WITH IMMOBILISED LOWER LIMB TRAUMA: A CLOSED AUDIT LOOP
audits.st: NICE recommendation for VTE risk assessment in lower limb immobilisation, RCEM GEMNet guidance and local policy
audits.f: 20/62 (32%) had a documented VTE risk assessment; none received thromboprophylaxis per local policy.
audits.c: Pathway redesigned to GEMNet guidance, local education and launch, electronic discharge prompt/block and orthopaedic engagement.
audits.r2: 54/58 (93.1%) had a documented risk assessment; 25/58 (43%) high risk and prescribed thromboprophylaxis.

audits.t: Introduction of clerking pro forma for surgical spinal patients at the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust (London): an audit cycle.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons documentation guidelines (GMC/NICE)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Standardised clerking pro forma for surgical spinal patients.
audits.r2: Pro forma significantly improved documentation in admission clerking (no figures given in abstract).

audits.t: Vitamin D deficiency in a high secure forensic psychiatry hospital: A clinical audit and service evaluation
audits.st: Local trust guideline: vitamin D checked within one month of admission and then three-monthly, with dosing by level
audits.f: 76.4% checked within one month of admission; 66.7% checked in last 3 months; 21.4% correct dose, 22.9% under-dosed, 14.3% over-dosed, 41.4% no dose when indicated

audits.t: An audit cycle of physical health monitoring and record keeping of long term in-patients at male and female psychiatric rehabilitation wards using QI approach
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: NICE guidelines, RCPsych report on physical health in mental health and Cygnet Health Care physical health policy
audits.f: Physical assessment within 24 hours 98%; monthly physical health reviews 62%; annual Health Improvement Profile 30%; high-dose antipsychotic monitoring 10%; ECG/bloods for antipsychotic monitoring 64%.
audits.c: QI approach with 4 PDSA cycles: MDT strategies to improve engagement with monthly physical health clinics, care plan points, diary reminders for bloods and ECGs, MDT and patient health education, and a designated support staff member for observations and physical health files.
audits.r2: Overall compliance 92%; high-dose antipsychotic monitoring 100%; monthly physical health clinics 88%; annual HIP 75%; annual antipsychotic monitoring/bloods/ECG 95%.

audits.t: Improving the Identification, Assessment and Management of Osteoporosis and Fragility Fracture Risk on a Later Life Psychiatry Ward: A Complete Audit Cycle
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: NICE and National Osteoporosis Guideline Group guidance on identification, assessment and management of fragility fracture risk
audits.f: FRAX calculated in 8/16 (50%) without known osteoporosis; FRAX communicated to GP in 2/8 (25%)
audits.c: Fracture risk scoring added to structured ward round template and osteoporosis information posters displayed
audits.r2: FRAX calculated in 15/17 (88%); FRAX communicated to GP in 11/15 (73%); BMD measured in 1/10 (10%) intermediate-risk patients

audits.t: Identification and Management of Hyperprolactinaemia in Patients With Intellectual Disabilities Who Are Prescribed Antipsychotic Medication: A Retrospective Audit
audits.st: Prolactin measured in the last 12 months for patients on antipsychotics and elevated results managed per current guidelines
audits.f: 39 (52.0%) had prolactin measured in the last 12 months; 16 (41.0%) of these were elevated; 81.3% of elevated results discussed and treatment considered.

audits.t: Re-Audit of the Assessment and Prevention of Risk of Fragility/Osteoporotic Fractures by Community Physicians in at Risk Old-Age Female Patients Admitted to Central Norfolk Older Adult Inpatient Unit at the Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: NICE guidelines (2012): fracture risk assessment with FRAX or QFracture for women aged 65 and over
audits.f: 0% had documented FRAX/QFracture assessment or DEXA; only 19% on bone-protecting medication despite over 90% intermediate or high risk

audits.t: When Psychosis is Not Psychosis: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Delirium Misdiagnosis Across Hospital Departments
audits.st: CAM-ICU delirium screening before psychiatry referral
audits.f: 82/130 (63%) referrals for suspected psychosis were delirium; CAM-ICU use 0%; mean time to delirium management 22 hours.
audits.c: Four-week CAM-ICU training: didactic sessions (Medicine, Surgery), bedside demonstrations (ICU, Orthopaedics), and quick-reference materials with brief ward teaching (Obstetrics and Gynaecology).
audits.r2: Misdiagnosis fell to 39/126 (31%); CAM-ICU uptake 56%; mean time to delirium management 11 hours.

audits.t: DELIVERING SUSTAINABLE CHANGE OF POSTOPERATIVE CARE DOCUMENTATION PRACTICES IN SPINAL SURGERY THROUGH QUALITY IMPROVEMENT FRAMEWORKS
audits.st: MDT consensus of 15 essential criteria for complete post-operative care documentation (no published standard)
audits.f: Baseline: >75% compliance in 4 criteria and <50% compliance in 10 of 15 criteria.
audits.c: Post-operative care template based on the 15 criteria embedded in existing IT software as a non-overwriting suffix needing two mouse clicks; later template update after a usage questionnaire.

audits.t: A VIRTUAL FRACTURE CLINIC AUDIT: ARE WALES MATCHING THE OUTCOMES IN ENGLAND?
audits.tp: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
audits.st: Appropriate VFC referrals, compared with established VFCs in England
audits.f: Inappropriate referrals for soft tissue knee and shoulder injuries 15.1% (n=50).
audits.r2: Average 19% improvement in referral quality; inappropriate soft tissue referrals 4.5% (n=15); fracture clinic appointments rose by 8% to 74.4% (n=247).

audits.t: A RETROSPECTIVE ANALYSIS OF THE DEFINITIVE MANAGEMENT OF OPEN TALUS FRACTURES, COMPARING ORIF AND TIBIOCALCANEAL FUSIONS, AT A MAJOR TRAUMA CENTRE: COHORT STUDY AND AUDIT OF BOAST 4 GUIDELINES
audits.st: BOAST 4 guidelines (open fractures)
audits.f: BOAST compliance result not reported; FUSION vs ORIF showed no significant difference in EQ-5D-5L (P = 0.13), FAAM-ADL (P = 0.20), FAAM-Sport (P = 0.34), infection (P = 0.55), surgical time (P = 0.91) or time to weight bearing (P = 0.39).

audits.t: A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT INVESTIGATING THE MDT CARE PROVIDED FOR FRAGILITY NON-HIP FEMORAL FRACTURES WITHIN A MAJOR TRAUMA CENTRE
audits.tp: Non-hip femoral fracture care in older patients
audits.st: NHFD key performance indicators: orthogeriatric review within 72 hours, surgery within 36 hours, post-operative weight bearing, confusion assessment, discharge home
audits.f: Orthogeriatric review within 72 hours 84%; surgery within 36 hours 32% (over 36 hours in 92% of peri-prosthetic fractures); 37% not advised to fully weight bear; confusion assessment 84%; 61% discharged to prior place of living.

audits.t: INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE ACCURACY OF UK NATIONAL HIP FRACTURE DATABASE INTRAOPERATIVE DATA: A CLOSED LOOP AUDIT WITH POSITIVE RESULTS
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Completion of NHFD V13.0 theatre collection sheet by the operating surgeon >80%, with improved accuracy
audits.f: 56% (n=14) had a completed V13.0 form; of these 21% (n=3) were 100% accurate.
audits.c: Results presented with education on V13.0 at the monthly trust audit meeting, and a sticker added to the hip fracture pre-operative checklist (time of admission and reason for delay).
audits.r2: 81% (n=25) had a completed form; accuracy increased to 56% (n=14).

audits.t: COMPLIANCE WITH THE SUSPECTED CAUDA EQUINA SYNDROME (CES) PATHWAY IN BETSI CADWALADR UNIVERSITY HEALTH BOARD (BCUHB) WEST: A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT AGAINST NATIONAL STANDARDS
audits.tp: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
audits.st: SBNS/BASS guidelines for urgent MRI in suspected cauda equina syndrome
audits.f: 99% scanned in compliance with SBNS/BASS standards; CES found on imaging in 18%.

audits.t: STANDARDIZATION OF URINARY CATHETERIZATION GUIDELINES TO REDUCE PAEDIATRIC PERIOPERATIVE URINARY TRACT INFECTION RATES: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE
audits.st: ACS NSQIP-Paediatric UTI rates; project aim of a 30% reduction in paediatric perioperative UTIs within 1 year
audits.f: Institution's paediatric UTI rate had an odds ratio of 1.9x compared with the predicted rate (NSQIP 'Needs Improvement'); audits of catheterisation practice identified areas for improvement.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary working group; 'permissive list' of procedures for which catheters may be required; standardised early catheter removal except urological procedures; education on insertion and maintenance; standardised equipment and technique; electronic medical record order sets as a forcing function.
audits.r2: 47% reduction in perioperative UTI rate by project completion; 96% adherence to the 'permissive lists'; NSQIP-Paediatric status improved from 'Needs Improvement' to 'Exemplary'.

audits.t: IMPROVING STANDARDS OF LONG LEG ALIGNMENT RADIOGRAPHS AT A UK DISTRICT GENERAL HOSPITAL: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
audits.st: Locally defined standard: blocks under the shorter limb where there is clear leg length discrepancy, equal pelvic height and patella facing forwards
audits.f: 116/243 (48%) performed with patella facing forwards; of 110 patients needing blocks, none had them used.

audits.t: THE CHILDREN'S URGENT REDUCTION OF FOREARM FRACTURES IN THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT (CURFFED) PROJECT: A NATIONAL PROSPECTIVE TRAINEE-LED COLLABORATIVE AUDIT OF PRACTICE AND PERCEIVED BARRIERS TO CHANGE
audits.tp: Paediatric buckle and forearm fracture management
audits.st: BOAST standards for the early management of the paediatric forearm fracture
audits.f: Overall compliance with BOAST standards 63%; of 577 eligible for ED manipulation, 424 (73%) managed in ED and 89 (21%) needed later theatre manipulation; IV sedation in 28% (n=120).

audits.t: Scottish Open Fractures of Tibia (SOFT) audit; a multi-centre retrospective review of ortho-plastic management of tibial shaft fractures at major trauma centres (MTCs) in Scotland.
audits.st: BOAST guidelines for open fractures
audits.f: Complete compliance with BOAST guidelines documented in 8.8% of cases.

audits.t: THE PAEDIATRIC ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT (ACL) NATIONAL AUDIT STUDY (PANA)
audits.st: BOAST guideline for paediatric ACL injuries
audits.f: 65% of centres used acute knee pathways; 68% locally collaborative imaging pathways; 59% radiological growth monitoring; 30% reported functional outcomes; fewer than 50% reported re-rupture rates; 74% followed rehabilitation protocols.

audits.t: THE ABERDEEN EXPERIENCE OF LEAN AND GREEN WARD-BASED CARPAL TUNNEL SURGERY: A SAFETY AND EFFICIENCY AUDIT
audits.st: BSSH out-of-theatre guidelines
audits.f: Full compliance with BSSH safety standards on ward-based lists (n=40); infection 2% (3/150) theatre vs 1.6% (2/129) DOSA (p=0.95).

audits.t: Unmet foot health needs in people with Systemic Sclerosis: an audit of foot health care provision
audits.tp: Foot health care in systemic sclerosis
audits.st: UK PRCA/ARMA standards of care: all people with systemic sclerosis should receive at least basic foot health information, and those with foot problems should have access to self-management advice and care
audits.f: Only 35/91 (39%) reported receiving foot health information; 49/91 (54%) had previous access to foot care and 38 (42%) were receiving foot care currently; 54 (59%) had current foot problems.

audits.t: Clinical photography in a high risk foot clinic: a quality audit
audits.tp: Clinical photography in foot ulcer monitoring
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 731 charts had a photograph; 623 (85%) of good quality. Probe to bone completed 99%, antibiotic 97%, offloading device 81%, Texas classification 76%.

audits.t: Management of shoulder dystocia: a re-audit
audits.st: Clinical Negligence Scheme for Trusts (CNST) minimum documentation standards for shoulder dystocia
audits.f: All areas 100% documented; brachial plexus injury rate 6.7%.
audits.r2: Documentation declined: only 65% recorded manoeuvres, timing and stage of delivery; 41% recorded staff attending and time of arrival; sequence of manoeuvres and who performed them not routinely recorded. Brachial plexus injury rate 15.8%.

audits.t: A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT OF PAIN MANAGEMENT IN PATIENTS PRESENTING WITH HIP FRACTURE
audits.tp: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block
audits.st: Agency for Clinical Innovation (ACI) hip fracture minimum standard 2: pain management
audits.f: Hourly pain scores on presentation in 82%; nerve blocks used in 35% in ED; 18% reported severe post-operative pain; neuropathic analgesia used in 14%; inappropriate NSAID use in 10%.

audits.t: 91 Mrs Bad Bones: Impact of COVID-19 on Secondary Prevention of Fragility Fractures
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pre-lockdown vs lockdown: orthogeriatric review 88% to 0%; vitamin D/calcium 81.6% to 58.0% (p = 0.0156); bone-sparing medication 60.7% to 18.2% (p = 0.0037); DEXA requests 40.1% to 3.6% (p = 0.0027).
audits.c: Introduction of the 'MRS BAD BONES' mnemonic for secondary fracture prevention.
audits.r2: Vitamin D/calcium 85.7% (p = 0.0034); bone-sparing medication 72.4% (p = 0.0002); DEXA requests 60%; orthogeriatric review 38%.

audits.t: P18 An audit on the delivery of Bristol Royal Children's Hospital paediatric orthopaedic services in response to BOAST COVID-19 guidance
audits.st: BOAST COVID-19 standards (management of patients with urgent orthopaedic conditions and trauma during the coronavirus pandemic)
audits.f: Patient-initiated follow-up 16% in acute fracture clinic and 12% in fracture follow-up clinic.
audits.c: Pandemic service changes including a virtual fracture clinic, patient-initiated follow-up, reduced radiography and cancellation of elective operating.
audits.r2: Acute fracture clinic and follow-up bookings reduced by 40% and 48%; patient-initiated follow-up rose to 75% and 35%; only 17% and 39% needed radiographs.

audits.t: 989 Improving the Completion of Hospital Anticipatory Care Plans in Orthopaedic Trauma Wards During The COVID-19 Pandemic
audits.st: All patients admitted acutely should have a Hospital Anticipatory Care Plan (HACP) completed within 24 hours
audits.f: 37/50 (74%) had HACPs completed; 18/37 (49%) completed within 24 hours; median time to completion 45.3 hours (range 0.4-275.1 hours)
audits.c: Staff teaching sessions and dissemination of infographic posters

audits.t: P3 A closed loop audit on pre-operative anaemia in major elective orthopaedic surgery
audits.st: International consensus statement on perioperative anaemia: treat Hb <130 before elective surgery
audits.f: 38% underwent arthroplasty with Hb <130; 14% with Hb <120; 11% of anaemias appropriately investigated; 7% had attempted treatment.
audits.c: Results presented at clinical governance meeting; departmental action plans for early identification and treatment of anaemia to Hb 130, delaying operations where necessary.
audits.r2: 21% operated with Hb <130 (p = 0.036); 0% with Hb <120; 80% of anaemias appropriately investigated (p < 0.001); attempted treatment 20% (p = 0.279).

audits.t: P16 An audit of elderly patients with a femoral fracture: is the quality of care received by patients affected by where in the femur the fracture occurs?
audits.tp: Non-hip femoral fracture care in older patients
audits.st: BOAST/NICE: surgery within 36 hours, orthogeriatric assessment within 72 hours, documented ceiling of treatment, falls risk assessment, bone health review, nutritional assessment, physiotherapy review
audits.f: Versus neck of femur fractures: surgery within 36 hours 63.9% vs 66%; orthogeriatric assessment within 72 hours 32.6% vs 91.9%; falls risk 76.7% vs 99.6%; bone health 41.9% vs 99.7%; nutrition 55.8% vs 99.6%; physiotherapy 97.7% vs 98.9%.
audits.c: Planned proforma for all femoral fractures and presentation to orthogeriatric, bone health and physiotherapy teams, with re-audit.

audits.t: 441 Management of Intracapsular Hip Fractures During Unprecedented COVID Times In A DGH
audits.tp: Total hip replacement for intracapsular hip fracture
audits.st: NICE hip fracture guideline eligibility criteria for THR vs hemiarthroplasty; BOA COVID-19 guidance on management of urgent orthopaedic conditions and trauma
audits.f: THR compliance dropped during the peak COVID months from 35% to 21.4%; Kings Mill THR compliance 27.3% vs national 18.3%; 54.5% of eligible patients were operated on by THR-performing consultants but received hemiarthroplasty.
audits.c: Planned introduction of a new table in the clerking booklet to identify THR-eligible patients, with re-audit.

audits.t: Prevention and Management of Falls in Older Adults admitted to Woodlands Hospital, an inpatient Old Age Psychiatric Unit
audits.st: NICE guidelines on the management of falls in older people
audits.f: 100% had individualised interventions; 97.3% had falls risk assessment on admission; 60.3% checked for signs of fracture; 78.3% had physical examination within 12 hours; 75% had neurological observations.

audits.t: From Register to Electronic Medical Records: A Data-Quality Audit in a Bangladeshi Orthopaedic Outpatient Department
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality

audits.f: Completeness: sex 98.6%, age 98.7%, occupation 94.9%; 0.5% unparsable dates; 131 duplicate serial numbers (3.2%) and seven complete-row duplicates; age mismatch 0.2%.

audits.t: Prospective Audit of Hand-Scrubbing Practices in an Orthopedic Operating Theatre in a Regional Headquarter Hospital of Northern Pakistan

audits.r2: Scrub duration 90%, coverage 88%, antiseptic use 93%, drying 87%, overall aseptic protocol 95%; all improvements statistically significant

audits.t: Clinical audit of surgical waste reduction in an equine theatre
audits.st: not reported

audits.r2: Mean total waste mass lower than in the other periods; offensive waste percentage reduced further; domestic waste percentage higher than period 1

audits.t: Improving Administration of Fascia-iliaca Blocks for Patients With a Fractured Neck of Femur by Clinical Audit
audits.tp: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block
audits.st: Administration of fascia iliaca compartment block to hip fracture patients
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Results presented at departmental and mortality meetings; teaching sessions for doctors; encouraged use of the neck of femur proforma to document FICB or a valid reason for omission.
audits.r2: Statistically significant increase in patients receiving fascia iliaca block (p value not given in abstract).

audits.t: Use of abbreviations in consent forms for orthopaedic patients: A quality improvement project
audits.st: GMC, Royal College of Surgeons Glasgow and British Orthopaedic Association guidance on consent
audits.f: Abbreviations used in 54% of consent forms.

audits.t: PAIN-AGE, a Controlled Before/After Study Assessing an Audit and Feedback Perioperative Pain Management Intervention in Older Patients with Hip Fracture.

audits.t: A Closed-Loop Audit of Thrombo-Embolic Deterrent Stocking Use in an Orthopaedic Ward.

audits.t: Clinical effectiveness of high tibial osteotomy for osteoarthritis of the knee.

audits.t: Reduction of nosocomial pressure ulcers in patients with hip fractures: a quality improvement program.

audits.t: Quality of post-anesthetic care in a hospital without a Post-Anesthetic Care Unit. A clinical audit.

audits.t: The effect of a fracture protocol on hospital prescriptions after minimal trauma fractured neck of the femur: a retrospective audit.

audits.t: A clinical audit of patients on an orthopaedic waiting list for greater than two years.

audits.r2: Bone-sparing agent 84.0% (42/50) aged 50–74 and 70.5% (222/316) aged ≥75 (p<0.001). Fragility fracture recorded 14% (25/178) aged 50–74 (p=0.168) and 2.3% (199/8702) aged ≥75 (p<0.001).

audits.r2: Gentamicin for IDC insertion fell to 4/205 (2%).

audits.t: Reducing mortality from hip fractures: a systematic quality improvement programme.

audits.f: 39.6% operated within 36 hours (2010); best practice tariff attainment 28% (2010); 30-day mortality 7.8%

audits.t: Cambridge Polytrauma Pathway: Are we making appropriately guided decisions?

audits.f: 8 patients received definitive orthopaedic intervention out-of-hours; other baseline figures not reported.

audits.r2: Significant improvement in recording of lactate and fibrinogen on admission (p<0.000, p=0.015) and preoperatively (p=0.003, p=0.030). Time to CT unchanged (p=0.536), median 0.53h (IQR 0.48-0.75). Out-of-hours definitive orthopaedic intervention fell from 8 to zero (p=0.195).

audits.t: The Introduction of a Multidisciplinary Hip Fracture Pathway to Optimise Patient Care and Reduce Mortality: A Prospective Audit of 161 Patients.

audits.t: Making the weekend work: a local quality improvement project to establish and improve the quality of weekend handover.

audits.f: Baseline (247 handovers over nine weeks): patient name 99%, hospital number 94%, admission reason 91%, other categories 12% to 84% (date of birth 54%, location 84%, frequency of review 70%, TTO 12%); only admission reason met its standard.

audits.r2: Sustainability re-audit of intranet tool (201 handovers, new cohort of doctors): patient name 100%, hospital number 98%, date of birth 85%; five of 10 categories met their standard (patient name, location, consultant, admission reason, frequency of review); all except TTO were above 50%.

audits.t: Addressing Hand Hygiene Compliance in a Low-Resource Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: a Quality Improvement Project.

audits.t: Injury coding in a national trauma registry: a one-year validation audit in a level 1 trauma centre.

audits.f: 582 AIS codes in the registry vs 766 in the reference standard.
