audits.tp: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
audits.st: BOAST COVID-19 guidance points 7–10: removable casts/splints in 100%; index fracture clinic appointments 100% virtually screened; follow-up by phone/video in 100%; follow-up radiographs for union in 0% (exceptions if documented)
audits.f: 100% removable casts; 96% virtually assessed or approved for face-to-face (197 VFC, 18 approved, 8 no approval); 97% virtual follow-up or documented reason (6/223, 2.7% without); 0.4% inappropriate radiographs for union.
audits.c: All patients required a consultant-level senior opinion (trauma meeting, on-call consultant or VFC) before a face-to-face appointment, from 11 May 2020; email reminder to use virtual clinics.
audits.r2: 100% removable casts; 99% virtually assessed or consultant-approved (130 VFC, 14 approved, 1 unapproved); 100% virtual follow-up or documented reason; 0.7% inappropriate radiographs for union.

audits.t: Compliance with antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines in surgery: Results of a targeted audit in a large-scale region-based French hospital network.
audits.st: French national antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines (use, agent, timing within 60 minutes before incision, initial dose, additional doses)
audits.f: Overall antibiotic prophylaxis compliance 64%; correct agent 93%; correct initial dose 97.4%; given within 60 minutes before incision in 77.6%.

audits.t: Adequacy of clinical information in X-ray referrals for traumatic ankle injury with reference to the Ottawa Ankle Rules-a retrospective clinical audit.
audits.tp: Ottawa rules and radiograph request appropriateness
audits.st: Ottawa Ankle Rules criteria documented on adult ankle X-ray referrals
audits.f: 163/262 referrals met Ottawa Ankle Rules criteria; 99 of 262 (38%) did not. Compliance by profession: physiotherapists 77.3%, nurses 65.4%, consultants 61.5%, registrars/MOs/interns 54.8%. Overall sensitivity 0.59 and specificity 0.37.

audits.t: The National Hip Fracture Database is only as good as the data we feed it - significant inaccuracy demonstrated and how to improve it.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Accuracy of NHFD entries for operation, implant polarity and cementation
audits.f: Inaccuracies in 20.5% of 3972 data entries.
audits.c: Introduction of a hip fracture clinical data administrator in each centre.
audits.r2: Inaccuracies reduced to 5.2% of 559 data entries.

audits.t: National Metrics Improved Timeliness of Antibiotic Administration for Open Extremity Fractures.
audits.st: American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Improvement Program best-practice guidelines: antibiotic order and administration within 1 hour
audits.f: Baseline period; figures not given in abstract.
audits.c: First, institutional awareness and education of departments; second, tracking of antibiotic order and administration times with quarterly audits following new guidelines.
audits.r2: Antibiotic order within 1 hour and administration within 1 hour both significantly improved after the second initiative, as did median arrival-to-order and arrival-to-administration times (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Secondary Prevention of Hip Fragility Fractures During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Service Evaluation of "MRS BAD BONES".
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: UHCW trust guidelines (in line with NICE) for secondary fragility fracture prevention: vitamin D/calcium supplementation, bone-sparing medication, DEXA scan for eligible patients, bone blood tests including PTH
audits.f: Pre-lockdown baseline: orthogeriatric review 88% (44/50); vitamin D/calcium 40/49 (81.6%); bone-sparing medication 17/28 (60.7%); DEXA requested 9/22 (40.1%); PTH measured 5 (10%). Post-lockdown (n=50, before intervention): orthogeriatric review 0%; vitamin D/calcium 29/50 (58.0%, P=.02); bone-sparing medication 4/22 (18.2%, P=.004); DEXA 1/28 (3.6%, P=.003).
audits.c: Audit results presented at the monthly T&O quality improvement meeting and the 'MRS BAD BONES' mnemonic disseminated to junior doctors, advanced nurse practitioners and medical students
audits.r2: Vitamin D/calcium 42/49 (85.7%, P=.003 vs post-lockdown); bone-sparing medication 21/29 (72.4%, P<.001); DEXA requested 12/21 (60.0%, P<.001); orthogeriatric review 38% (19/50).

audits.t: The acute management of ankle fractures (Augment) study: A prospective trainee led national collaborative audit of the Boast 12 guidelines.
audits.st: BOAST 12 (BOA/BOFAS) standards for ankle fractures: documentation, imaging, management and follow-up
audits.f: Overall BOAST 12 compliance 41.7%; neurovascular documentation 40.7%; VTE assessment 61.5%.

audits.t: Getting it right first time (GIRFT): A closed loop study of hip arthroplasty documentation in a trauma and orthopaedic department.
audits.st: GIRFT, British Hip Society and BOA July 2019 total hip arthroplasty best practice guidance (24 documentation criteria)
audits.f: Handwritten notes scored an average of 12/24 (50%); compliance ranged 0%-100% across criteria, e.g. protection of critical structures 15%, leg length/neurovascular status 20%, intraoperative complications 5%; 80% legible
audits.c: Pre-populated GIRFT-compliant online hip arthroplasty operative note proforma in the local 'Trackcare' electronic system, typed notes
audits.r2: Typed notes with the computerised proforma scored an average of 22/24 (92%) (p<0.05); compliance 80%-100% across criteria; 15 of 24 criteria significantly improved; 100% legible

audits.t: Open lower limb fractures in the UK trauma system: A multicentre prospective audit of current practice.
audits.st: BOA and BAPRAS standards for trauma (open fractures)
audits.f: Antibiotics within 1 hour 41.7%; splint in ED 74.4%; documented orthoplastic plan 85.8%; debridement within 12 hours for high-energy injuries 41.7%

audits.t: The fiscal impact of repeat imaging in a pediatric orthopedic clinic.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 77 (11%) new patients did not bring previous X-rays, generating reimaging charges of $33,326 (30%-50% of total visit charges).

audits.t: Pre-operative resuscitation discussion with patients undergoing fractured neck of femur repair: a service evaluation and discussion of current standards.
audits.tp: Resuscitation discussion before hip fracture surgery
audits.st: ReSPECT form completed before operation and countersigned by a consultant
audits.f: ReSPECT form completion 23%; consultant signed 41%.

audits.t: Digital radiography reject analysis of examinations with multiple rejects: an Australian emergency imaging department clinical audit.
audits.st: No established reject rate guideline stated; ALARA principle
audits.f: Overall reject rate 10.3% (1,193/11,596) and multiple reject rate 1.3% (147). Highest multiple reject rates among frequent projections: horizontal beam knee 32/380 (8.4%) and horizontal beam hip 17/182 (9.3%).

audits.t: Revolutionising rapid recovery: a quality improvement project in hip and knee replacement.
audits.st: Local SMART aim: 90% of cases mobilising on day 0 and length of stay reduced by 1 day within 1 year, with increased throughput
audits.f: Mean length of stay 3.6 days for both total hip and total knee replacement; Model Hospital median length of stay 4.2 days (hips, 41st nationally) and 3.9 days (knees, 34th).
audits.c: Multidisciplinary Rapid Recovery Group with parallel PDSA cycles: ropivacaine local infiltration protocol, oxycodone MR, preprinted drug charts, Taurus frames and nurse-led mobilisation, stopping routine MSU and TED stockings, and a ring-fenced elective ward.
audits.r2: Mean length of stay fell to 2.4 days for hips and 2.0 days for knees (p<0.0001); all patients mobilised on day 0 in the most recent 3 months; predicted yearly throughput 560 vs 480.

audits.t: Do we achieve the Montgomery standard for consent in orthopaedic surgery?
audits.st: Montgomery v Lanarkshire Health Board (2015) standard for informed consent
audits.f: Specific patient risks documented 50%; procedure-specific risks 42%; alternative options 48%; written information 14%.
audits.c: Results presented to clinicians and a teaching session on expected consent standards.
audits.r2: Specific patient risks 60%; procedure-specific risks 76%; alternative options 66%; written information 8%.

audits.t: Perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis in spinal surgery.
audits.st: North American Spine Society (NASS) 2013 guideline on perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis: preoperative dose, redosing as needed, discontinuation within 24 hours for uncomplicated non-instrumented surgery
audits.f: All patients received a correct preoperative first-generation cephalosporin dose, but IV antibiotics continued 1–6 days followed by oral antibiotics until suture removal (up to two weeks) in all patients, with mixed agents; SSI 1 case (1.85%).
audits.c: New local surgical antibiotic prophylaxis protocol (first-generation cephalosporin 30–60 minutes before incision, redose after 3 hours, stop at 24 hours) agreed in discussion sessions and disseminated by pamphlet and theatre poster.
audits.r2: All patients received preoperative first-generation cephalosporin continued for only 24 hours postoperatively and were discharged on day 2; no SSI.

audits.t: Retrospective Review of Perioperative Multimodal Analgesia for Orthopedic Patients in a Veterans Affairs Setting.
audits.st: American Pain Society guideline recommendations for perioperative multimodal analgesia (at least two medication classes)
audits.f: Perioperative multimodal analgesia used in 85%; 87% discharged on multimodal analgesia.
audits.c: Evidence-based multimodal perioperative quick-order menu developed (no re-audit reported).

audits.t: Crossing quartiles: Improving time to theatre for patients with hip fractures in a large UK district general hospital; A quality improvement report.
audits.st: Hip fracture Best Practice Tariff: surgery within 36 hours of admission (National Hip Fracture Database)
audits.f: Surgery within 36 hours 54%; mean time to surgery 43.68 hours; BPT achieved in 45.7%; trust ranked 152/160 for time to surgery.
audits.c: Anaesthetic 'hot week' introduced in January 2018: the same anaesthetist covers hip fracture lists, attends trauma meeting, liaises with orthopaedic and orthogeriatric teams and advises on medical optimisation.
audits.r2: Surgery within 36 hours 87.5%; mean time to surgery 25.11 hours; BPT achieved in 84%; ranking rose to 20th for time to surgery and 18th for BPT.

audits.t: Clinical Audit as a Quality Improvement Tool in Measurements of Lying and Standing Blood Pressure for Elderly Patients Admitted With a Hip Fracture.
audits.st: NICE guidelines on falls in older people: lying and standing blood pressure measurement; RCP FFAP guidance on LSBP procedure
audits.f: LSBP measured in 16 (32%); correctly documented in 12/16 (75%).
audits.c: Results presented at geriatric medicine mortality meeting with root cause analysis; flyers and posters on wards, teaching sessions for ward staff on LSBP measurement and recording on POET, and aide-memoires placed around wards.
audits.r2: LSBP measured in 45 (83.3%) (p < 0.0001); correctly documented in 45 (100%) (p = 0.0035).

audits.t: Optimizing orthopedic trauma care delivery during the COVID-19 pandemic. A closed-loop audit of implementing a virtual fracture clinic and fast-track pathway in a Dutch level 2 trauma center.
audits.tp: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
audits.st: Predefined standards from national coronavirus outpatient guidelines and local consensus: (1) all eligible ED trauma patients referred for VFC review; (2) all patients contacted after VFC review; (3) patient-initiated follow-up by default where possible; (4) follow-up by telephone or video where possible. Target 100% for standard 1.
audits.f: 162/184 (88.0%) referred for VFC review; 98.1% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.9%, not reached); 29/162 (17.9%) discharged 'virtually'; 137/291 (45.0%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 95 minutes vs 131 minutes at baseline (p<0.001).
audits.c: After an evaluation meeting, ED staff were invited to attend VFC review for direct feedback, presentations explaining the workflow were held, posters were put up in the ED, and a patient information leaflet asking patients to call if not contacted by 15:00 the next workday was introduced.
audits.r2: 302/305 (98.4%) referred for VFC review; 99.0% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.0%, not reached); 41/302 (13.6%) discharged 'virtually'; 179/436 (41.1%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 98 minutes (−33 minutes vs baseline, p=0.001); time to review 47 minutes (p<0.001); time for review 35 minutes vs 45 minutes (p=0.019).

audits.t: Fascia Iliaca Compartment Block for Hip Fractures: Improving Clinical Practice by Audit.
audits.tp: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block
audits.st: NICE hip fracture guidance and BOAST fragility fracture analgesia guidance; local decision that all hip fracture patients receive FICB on presentation unless contraindicated
audits.f: FICB administered in 45 (24.5%); mean post-FICB pain score 4 (NRS)
audits.c: Results discussed at departmental and Trust mortality meetings, one-to-one teaching on loss-of-resistance FICB for ED and T&O junior doctors, and enforcing completion of the hip fracture clinical proforma with FICB sign-off or documented contraindication
audits.r2: FICB administered in 94 (44.3%) (p<0.00001); mean post-FICB pain score 3.6 (p<0.0011)

audits.t: Introduction of an enhanced recovery programme for total shoulder arthroplasty: report of a novel pathway.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pre-enhanced recovery: mean LOS 2.38 nights, median 2 nights, single night stay rate 40.2%; complication rate 9.9%.
audits.c: Enhanced recovery programme via PDSA cycles: MDT-led preoperative class with OT home assessment, new patient information booklet and DVD, standardised anaesthetic/analgesic protocol with carbohydrate and gabapentin loading, and a physiotherapy protocol with sling for comfort only and early safe-zone mobilisation.
audits.r2: Matched enhanced recovery cohort: mean LOS 1.89 nights (median 2), single night stay rate 49.2%; 15 fewer bed nights; complication rate 7%; OSS and Constant scores similar at 3 and 12 months.

audits.t: Use of abbreviations in consent forms for orthopaedic surgery: A pilot study.
audits.st: GMC, RCS Glasgow and BOA consent guidance; no abbreviations on consent forms
audits.f: Abbreviations in 189/350 (54%) forms; mostly by registrars (74%); DVT and PE commonest.
audits.c: Results presented at M&M meeting, email to all staff, reminder sticker attached to consent forms and poster in areas where consent is taken.

audits.t: Improving Secondary Bone Protection Prescription in Patients Admitted With a Femoral Neck Fracture.
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians National Hip Fracture Database: all patients with hip fracture assessed for and managed with a secondary bone-protection plan (100% gold standard); SMART aim of an additional 40% per year
audits.f: 13.9% (n=11) assessed for bone protection; 1.3% (n=1) prescribed a bisphosphonate and 10.1% (n=8) other bone protection; 86.1% (n=68) neither assessed nor prescribed.
audits.c: PDSA 1 awareness poster (January 2019); PDSA 2 education session for clerking and ward doctors added to induction (March 2019); PDSA 3 MDT meeting with responsibility charting, giving assessment and prescribing to the care of the elderly team (April 2019).
audits.r2: 100% (n=50) of patients assessed or placed on a bone-protection plan.

audits.t: Improving the Quality of Medical Documentation in Orthopedic Surgical Notes Using the Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR) Score.
audits.st: Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR), based on Royal College of Surgeons guidance on medical record keeping (no target stated)
audits.f: Mean total STAR score 94.3 ± 1.6.
audits.c: Annual teaching of practitioners on documentation using slides based on Royal College of Surgeons of England recommendations, with periodic (annual) re-auditing.

audits.t: Results From an All Wales Trainee Led Collaborative Prospective Audit on Management of Ankle Fractures.
audits.st: BOAST guideline on management of ankle fractures (documentation, imaging including CT for posterior malleolus, weight-bearing X-rays, early weight-bearing)
audits.f: Documentation: mechanism 94.4%, skin 71.3%, neurovascular status 80.1%, comorbidities 81%, alcohol 34.3%, smoking 41.7%. Mortice view 75.9%. CT for posterior malleolus fracture 15/31 (48.38%) operative and 0/9 non-operative. Weight-bearing X-ray in non-operative group 22/106 (20.8%). Early weight-bearing 63/106 (59.43%) non-operative and 11/110 (10%) operative.

audits.t: Informed Written Consent for Orthopaedic Trauma in the Emergency Setting at a Tertiary Referral Centre: A Closed-Loop Audit.
audits.st: American Association of Orthopaedic Surgeons 'Orthopaedic Surgical Consent' standards (name, DOB, board number, procedure without abbreviation, side/site stated); no target stated
audits.f: Name, DOB and board number 100%. No abbreviations 79 (74.5%). Side/site 81 (76.4%) (the abstract wording says 'without correctly stating' but the comparison treats this as compliance). Abbreviation and side/site both failing in 13 (12.3%).
audits.c: A single 90-minute virtual education session for all trauma and orthopaedic staff on consent standards, sharing cycle 1 results.
audits.r2: Name, DOB and board number 100%. No abbreviations 37 (92.5%, p=0.02). Side/site correctly stated 39 (97.5%, p=0.0015). No form had both failures (0% vs 12.3%, p=0.02).

audits.t: Patients Lacking the Capacity to Consent to Hip Fracture Surgery May Be Undergoing Major Operations Without Their Next of Kin Being Involved in Best-Interests Decisions: A Quality Improvement Report.
audits.st: Mental Capacity Act 2005 best-interests process; documented attempt to contact next of kin before surgery and completion of NoK section of Consent Form Four
audits.f: Documented attempt to contact NoK 80% (24/30); NoK section of Consent Form Four completed 30% (10/30).
audits.c: Feedback presentation at trauma meeting and email to orthopaedic team.
audits.r2: Documented attempt to contact NoK 100% (28/28), p<0.05; NoK section completed 64.3% (18/28), p<0.05.

audits.t: A retrospective analysis of the definitive management of open talus fractures at a major trauma centre, comparing ORIF to FUSION: cohort study and audit of BOAST 4 guidelines.
audits.st: BOAST 4 guidelines for open fractures (e.g. prophylactic antibiotics within one hour of injury, definitive soft tissue coverage within 72 h, orthoplastic involvement, debridement); no target stated
audits.f: 15 open talus fractures in 14 patients. 100% had orthoplastic involvement, initial saline-soaked gauze and occlusive film dressing, functional recovery and rehabilitation advice, and recorded debridement; 60% had debridement using fasciotomy lines. Only 27% received prophylactic antibiotics within one hour of injury and only 27% achieved definitive soft tissue coverage within 72 h (mean 9.7 days in the 7 needing coverage).

audits.t: Compliance With the Cauda Equina Pathway: Results of a Closed-Loop Audit.
audits.tp: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
audits.st: Local standard operating procedure for acute back pain with suspected cauda equina syndrome, based on BASS/SBNS guidance (senior ED discussion, anal tone and perianal sensation documented, MRI within 24 hours, spinal centre plan documented); no target stated
audits.f: ED assessment and senior discussion 24 (96%); discussion with spinal centre by senior ED doctor 13 (61.9%); anal tone documented 23 (92%); perianal sensation documented 18 (72%); spinal centre plan documented per SOP 5 (20%); MRI within 24 hours 25 (100%).
audits.c: Teaching on CES and neurological examination for T&O and ED juniors, posters of the pathway in ED, discussion between T&O and ED on GP referrals, and emails to staff; an electronic SBAR documentation template was also created.
audits.r2: ED assessment and senior discussion 26 (90%, p=0.727); discussion by senior ED doctor 2 (9%, p=0.000); anal tone documented 28 (97%, p=0.887); perianal sensation documented 28 (97%, p=0.028); spinal centre plan documented 0 (0%, p=0.033); MRI within 24 hours 29 (100%).

audits.t: Preventing pressure ulcers from paediatric femoral traction: use of an audit cycle to assess a new concise manual and a daily care chart.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Three patients (23%) developed grade 2 pressure sores; mean traction 8.5 days; pressure site check documented in only 7.7%.
audits.c: New single-page traction manual and daily care chart introduced into patient care notes.
audits.r2: One patient (12.5%) developed a grade 1 sore; mean traction 8.4 days; pressure site monitoring documented in 75%.

audits.t: Can introducing a direct endocrine pathway reduce hyponatraemia in elective knee and hip replacements? A closed-loop audit and service evaluation study.
audits.st: Hyponatraemia protocol based on NICE guidance (sodium cut-off 133 mmol/l per local guidance); no numeric target stated
audits.f: Hyponatraemia in 36 (12%); only 38% of hyponatraemic patients investigated, 33% had endocrine input; mean 3.6 days to endocrine referral; length of stay 7.7 vs 4.6 days; 4 of 11 profound cases admitted to critical care (8 days in total).
audits.c: Direct endocrine pathway developed with endocrinology based on NICE guidance: protocol poster displayed in clinical areas and agreement for same-day endocrine review of arthroplasty patients referred via ICE.
audits.r2: Hyponatraemia in 31 (11.7%); all 3 profound cases investigated and referred to endocrinology; mean 2.3 days to endocrine referral; length of stay reduced by 0.7 days (p = 0.008144); no critical care admissions (p = 0.031622).

audits.t: An audit of computed tomography request practices for suspected cervical spine injury post-guideline change in a tertiary referral paediatric hospital.
audits.tp: Cervical spine CT imaging in children
audits.st: Hospital Clinical Procedure: cervical spine CT only at request of the orthopaedic service
audits.c: Hospital guideline modified so CT only at request of the orthopaedic service.

audits.t: Perioperative administration of tranexamic acid in hip fracture surgery (The PATHS study): national audit of current practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 48.0% of eligible patients received TXA; rates varied from 0 to 100%; arthroplasty 57.6% vs internal fixation 38.4%.

audits.t: A retrospective audit of the timescales involved in the diagnosis and management of suspected Achilles tendon ruptures at a single National Health Service trust: A quality service improvement and redesign project.
audits.st: Local departmental standards (ultrasound within one week of request; treatment decision within two weeks) and SMART protocol timeframes (scan within 48 hours)
audits.f: 78% (n = 88) diagnosed by ultrasound within one week of request; 83% (n = 91) treatment decision within two weeks; 7% (n = 8) scanned within 48 hours.
audits.c: Revised patient pathway developed after multidisciplinary discussion (not re-audited in this paper).

audits.t: Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip: An Audit of the Ultrasound Screening Programme.
audits.st: Recommended scan within 6 weeks (stated in results)
audits.f: 255 (26%) referred to orthopaedic clinic; only two infants referred on for persistent DDH; no baby scanned within the recommended 6 weeks later presented with dislocation or needed tertiary referral.

audits.t: Documentation of neurovascular assessment in fracture patients in a tertiary care hospital: A retrospective review.
audits.tp: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
audits.st: British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) on documentation of neurovascular assessment; no target stated
audits.f: ED notes: no neurovascular documentation 17 (22.1%), 'NVI' only 30 (38.9%), specific documentation 30 (38.9%). Orthopaedic notes: no documentation 3 (3.8%), NVI only 16 (20.7%), specific documentation 58 (75.3%). Post-manipulation in ED (n=19): no documentation 12 (63.2%), specific 6 (31.6%).
audits.c: Posters in trauma units, generic educational emails to all ED and orthopaedic doctors, and consultant-led joint ED and orthopaedic teaching sessions.
audits.r2: ED notes: no documentation 6 (7.3%), NVI only 8 (9.7%), specific documentation 68 (82.9%). Orthopaedic notes: no documentation 0 (0%), NVI only 4 (3.6%), specific documentation 74 (90.2%). Post-manipulation in ED (n=22): no documentation 7 (31.8%), NVI only 4 (18.1%), specific 11 (50%).

audits.t: The effectiveness of a multifaceted, group-facilitated audit and feedback intervention to increase tranexamic acid use during total joint arthroplasty.
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines and local practice protocols supporting tranexamic acid as standard of care in THA and TKA
audits.f: TXA use 66.6% for THA and 62.4% for TKA.
audits.c: Two individual data reports on TXA use and transfusion compared with peers, plus a group-facilitated feedback session
audits.r2: TXA use 74.4% for THA (absolute change 7.9%, 95% CI 2.4 to 13.3) and 82.3% for TKA (absolute change 19.9%, 95% CI 15.0 to 25.0).

audits.t: The Fragility Fracture Postoperative Mobilisation multicentre audit : the reality of weightbearing practices following operations for lower limb fragility fractures.
audits.st: British Orthopaedic Association Standard: all surgery in the frail patient should allow full weightbearing for activities required for daily living
audits.f: 16,614 (85.0%) instructed to weightbear for daily living immediately postoperatively: 15,543 (95.7%) hip fracture and 1,071 (32.3%) non-hip fracture patients.

audits.t: Evaluating the measures in patient-reported outcomes, values and experiences (EMPROVE study): a collaborative audit of PROMs practice in orthopaedic care in the United Kingdom.
audits.st: National orthopaedic society recommendations on PROMs collection
audits.f: PROMs collected for 83.3% of hip and 80.6% of knee replacements; 69% (221/318) used paper as primary collection method; variation outside incentivised programmes failed to meet the audit standard.

audits.t: Quality improvement initiative: how the setting up of an anaesthesia consultant-led perioperative outreach service addressed anaesthesia-specific issues to improve anaesthesia consult and surgery timings for hip fracture patients.
audits.st: Surgery within 48 hours of hip fracture; aims of a 10% increase in patients seen by anaesthesia within 24 hours and a 10% increase in surgery within 48 hours
audits.f: Median time to first anaesthesia consult 35.3 hours; consults <24 hours 39%; median time to surgery 61.5 hours; surgery within 48 hours 38%.
audits.c: Consultant-led anaesthesia perioperative outreach service seeing patients within 24 hours of admission, with case manager notification, REDCap follow-up database, standardised workflow and guidelines, and 6-monthly PDSA audits.
audits.r2: Median time to anaesthesia consult 21.5 hours (p = 0.029); consults <24 hours 67% (p < 0.003); median time to surgery 46 hours in results (50 hours in abstract) (p = 0.897); surgery within 48 hours 51.6% (p = 0.904).

audits.t: Retrospective Review of Arthroplasty Radiographs: How to Define an Adequate Radiograph.
audits.st: Local consensus criteria (seven arthroplasty and three radiology consultants): nine criteria for adequate post-operative hip and knee arthroplasty radiographs, four essential
audits.f: 69/100 radiographs adequate overall; whole prosthesis and cement visible 86%, relevant anatomy visible 83%, pubic symphysis centred 31%, GT/LT level 32%.
audits.c: Local guidelines published with radiology, educational and feedback meetings with radiographers, poster in radiography rooms and a quality improvement proforma.
audits.r2: 84/100 adequate overall; prosthesis and cement visible 93%, relevant anatomy 95%, pubic symphysis centred 47%, GT/LT level 43%; 11/56 (19.6%) hip and 5/44 (11.4%) knee radiographs inadequate.

audits.t: Comparison of Digital Versus Conventional Documentation of Ward Round in Terms of Staff Satisfaction, Effect on Education, and Adherence to British Orthopaedic Association Guidelines.
audits.st: BOA guidance on ward round documentation (patient ID and name, ward round clinician, documenting clinician, grade, date, time, whom to contact)
audits.f: Paper notes: patient ID and name 29 (65.91%); documenting clinician 17 (38.64%); time of ward round 26 (59.09%); grade of ward round clinician 18 (40.91%); whom to contact 0 (0%) (percentages as stated).
audits.c: Introduction of electronic ward round record keeping.
audits.r2: Electronic records: patient ID and name, ward round clinician, documenting clinician, date, time and grade all 34 (100%); whom to contact 5 (14.70%).

audits.t: Implementing large-scale data quality validation in a national arthroplasty registry to improve compliance : the National Joint Registry data quality audit programme.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Compliance of NJR entries validated against each unit's Patient Administration System; target 95% or higher compliance
audits.f: Baseline average organisation-level compliance 92.64% (92.6%), with over 7,000 cases in provider data but missing from the NJR; 9.7% of revision hips missing vs 5.6% of primaries, and 9.8% of revision knees vs 5.1% of primaries.
audits.c: Annual bidirectional data quality audit cycle: statements of missing cases sent to units for retrospective entry, named data quality lead per unit, data completeness awards and tariff top-up targets, audit reports with action plans to CEOs and clinical leads, unit visits, communications and user guides, and a semi-automated upload platform from 2018.
audits.r2: Baseline compliance rose year-on-year to 96.0% in 2018/19, reaching 97.9% overall after closure of the audit cycle; 76.4% of units achieved >95% compliance (61.5% of units achieved ≥95% on first run of the 2018/19 audit). 314 units completed the 2018/19 audit.

audits.t: Improving Hourly Rounding on an Orthopaedic/Trauma Unit.
audits.st: Hourly rounding
audits.f: Hourly rounding compliance 77.3%.
audits.c: Several PDSA cycles: educational material, repeated interventions and a 'redline' unit policy for isolation precautions communicated at huddles.

audits.t: Improving referrals to a fracture liaison service: Screening for osteoporosis.
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: Recommended FLS guidelines: referral of patients meeting age criteria with first fragility fracture
audits.f: 5% FLS referrals.
audits.c: Alert button in the electronic health record prompting surgeons to refer eligible patients to FLS.

audits.t: Timing and safety of hip fracture surgery in patients on direct-acting oral anticoagulants.
audits.st: Hospital protocol: surgery within 24 h of last DOAC dose (if creatinine clearance >50 ml/min) with 1 g tranexamic acid at induction
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: After the second cycle: compliance with surgical timing 55% and tranexamic acid 81%; mean blood loss 500 ml vs 330 ml in non-anticoagulated controls (P = 0.0115).

audits.t: Improving Acute Orthopaedic Admission Note Documentation Standards at a Tertiary Centre Through Proforma Introduction: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Irish HSE Standards and Recommended Practices for Healthcare Records Management and HSE National Model of Care for Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery documentation standards (checklist)
audits.f: Unscripted notes: consultant on call 78% (39/50); time of injury 72% (36/50); associated injury 48% (24/50); smoking status 86% (43/50); alcohol 42% (21/50); vital signs 28% (14/50); other systems 14% (7/50).
audits.c: Standardised admission proforma developed with multidisciplinary stakeholders after results were presented at departmental teaching, with an accompanying education session; one-month introduction period.
audits.r2: Proforma notes: consultant on call 100% (p=0.0005); time of injury 100% (p=0.0001); associated injury 100% (p=0.0001); smoking 100% (p=0.0001); alcohol 94% (p=0.0001); vital signs 70% (p=0.0001); other systems 74% (p=0.0001).

audits.t: Results of an Audit of Orthopaedic Operation Notes from a Tertiary Care Centre: Are We Doing It Right and Can We Do More?
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice guidelines (2014)
audits.f: 100% for date/time, surgeon, procedure, extra procedure; operative diagnosis 99.35%; antibiotic prophylaxis 99.35; incision 94.77%; findings 92.16%; prosthesis 97.37%; DVT prophylaxis 96.08%; post-op instructions 93.46%; tourniquet time 41.83%; blood loss 59.48%; closure 16.99%; complications 51.63%; elective/emergency setting 0%.

audits.t: Improved Outcomes Following a Care Guideline Implementation: Part 1 of an Analysis of 12 355 Patients After Total Knee Arthroplasty.
audits.st: Achievement of minimal clinically important difference on KOS-ADL following TKA
audits.f: 25.8% of patients did not progress on the KOS-ADL.
audits.c: Physical therapy care guideline introduced in 2013, with outcome data access, audit feedback, performance goals and financial incentives
audits.r2: 14.3% of patients did not progress on the KOS-ADL.

audits.t: Intervention to Improve Compliance With National Guidelines on Venous Thromboembolism Chemoprophylaxis for Patients With Operatively Managed Ankle Fractures.
audits.st: NICE guidance on pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for ankle surgery with immobilisation, and BOAST requirement that VTE prophylaxis follows agreed local protocols; no target stated
audits.f: Operation note documentation of VTE chemoprophylaxis: agent and duration specified 40 (29%), nonspecific 40 (29%), none 57 (42%). Discharged with VTE chemoprophylaxis 78 (57%).
audits.c: Quality Improvement Half-Day educating surgeons and ward junior doctors; new written local policy of enoxaparin 40 mg once daily for 6 weeks for all operatively managed ankle fractures unless contraindicated; posters for 3 weeks in theatre and ward areas; review of prophylaxis at 2- and 6-week clinics.
audits.r2: Operation note agent and duration specified 44 (90%), nonspecific 3 (6%), none 2 (4%) (all P<0.001). Discharged with VTE chemoprophylaxis 48 (98%) (P<0.001).

audits.t: Expediting the Management of Suspected Cauda Equina Syndrome (CES) in the Emergency Department Through Clinical Pathway Design at a District General Hospital: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean MRI completion from arrival 13:54:49; mean MRI request from arrival 14:12:03; arrival to action plan 27:29:00; 28% stayed less than 24 hours.
audits.c: Findings shared with ED and radiology; reserved MRI slots for suspected CES booked directly by ED with prioritised vetting; red-flag checklist and bladder scan protocol; proposed CES pathway; posters and pathway distributed to ED and orthopaedic staff.
audits.r2: Mean MRI completion from arrival 10:39:00; mean MRI request from arrival 06:10:00; arrival to action plan 15:38 (43.1% reduction vs cycle 1); 54.4% stayed less than 24 hours.

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Project to Assess if Preoperative Trauma Patients Are Receiving Their Prescribed Medications Preoperatively.
audits.st: Local and national (Royal College of Anaesthetists) guidance that preoperative trauma patients receive prescribed medications while nil by mouth, except anticoagulants, ACE inhibitors and ARBs
audits.f: 16/41 (39%) received their medications correctly; 22 critical drug class omissions; 19 omitted because nil by mouth.
audits.c: Poster on drug trolleys listing which medications to give or withhold, meetings with ward managers and nursing staff, and presentation at orthopaedic and anaesthetic audit meetings.
audits.r2: 25/41 (61%) received their medications correctly; 10 critical drug class omissions; 12 omitted because nil by mouth.

audits.t: Provision of revision knee arthroplasty services across Scotland: A national audit.
audits.st: Current national guidelines for unit case volume per year and recommended individual surgeon case volumes
audits.f: 5/17 (29%) units met national case volume guidelines; 11/77 (14%) surgeons met recommended individual volumes; 37/77 (48%) surgeons did 2 or fewer cases per year.

audits.t: Postoperative Mobilization Protocol in Lumbar Laminectomy Patients.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Retrospective chart audit showed documentation of mobility at 24 and 48 hours was lacking (no figures given).
audits.c: Staff education with a self-paced module on benefits of mobility and EMR documentation, including the Johns Hopkins Highest Level of Mobility scale and 6-clicks scale.
audits.r2: Improved documentation of early mobilised patients (no figures given).

audits.t: An Audit of Orthopaedic Discharge Summaries Comparing Electronic With Handwritten Summaries: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Standard discharge summary checklist from a systematic review (predetermined set of criteria)
audits.f: Handwritten summaries: complications in hospital 50%, contact information 34%, condition at discharge 66%, understandability 58%, allergies 66%, problem list/issues pending 35%, discharge medications 88%, follow-up plan 80%; patient signature 0%
audits.c: Introduction of electronic discharge summaries using a standardised form completed by orthopaedic residents (from 8 January 2022)
audits.r2: Electronic summaries: complications in hospital 100%, contact information 95%, condition at discharge 96%, understandability 100%, allergies 100%, problem list/issues pending 92%, discharge medications 100%, follow-up plan 100%; patient signature 100%

audits.t: Early Management of Paediatric Wrist and Forearm Fractures in a Busy District General Hospital Emergency Department: A Retrospective Cohort Comparison Study and Audit of BOAST Guidelines.
audits.tp: Paediatric buckle and forearm fracture management
audits.st: BOAST early management of distal forearm fractures in children (May 2021): early ED manipulation, neurovascular and consent documentation, orthogonal X-rays, fracture clinic within 7 days
audits.f: 23/72 (31.94%) manipulated in ED; 11 of 23 ED manipulations failed.
audits.c: Local trust pathway in line with BOAST introduced from July 2021 (analgesia/sedation, location, manipulation and referral guidance) with staff education.
audits.r2: 73/87 manipulated in ED (p<0.00001); 63 (86.31%) acceptable reduction, 10 (13.69%) failed. BOAST compliance: neurovascular documentation pre-manipulation 93.10% (81/87), before discharge 64.36% (56/87); consent documentation 73.56% (64/87); orthogonal X-rays 100% (87/87); fracture clinic within 7 days 49.42% (43/87), mean 8.25 days.

audits.t: Standardization of global hip fracture audit could facilitate learning, improve quality, and guide evidence-based practice.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Fragility Fracture Network minimum common dataset (2022): 20 core and 12 optional fields
audits.f: First-generation registries collect 60% of fields, second-generation 75%, third-generation 85%; 5/20 core fields collected by all; prefracture mobility, cognition and bone protection collected by 11/17 (65%)

audits.t: A Five-Year Retrospective Audit on Bone Protection Prescribing in Patients With Fragility Fractures in Primary Care.
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: NICE guidance on bone protection (bisphosphonates first line) after fragility fracture
audits.f: 33/47 on bone protection agents (26 bisphosphonate plus calcium/vitamin D, 7 bisphosphonate alone); 2 on calcium/vitamin D alone; 12/47 on neither therapy.
audits.c: Educational poster on recognition and coding of fragility fractures; untreated patients reviewed individually and started on treatment, referred for DEXA or specialist advice.

audits.t: Enhancing Patient Management and Financial Efficiency: Adherence to National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Pediatric Distal Radius Buckle Fractures.
audits.tp: Paediatric buckle and forearm fracture management
audits.st: NICE guideline: manage paediatric distal radius buckle fractures with a soft cast and discharge directly from the ED
audits.f: 33/84 discharged at first visit; 69 had a single X-ray, 12 had two and 4 had three X-rays
audits.c: Results presented to the department and ED; parents educated on fracture type and cast removal with option to forgo clinic visits; safety brochures; email reminders to fracture clinic staff about NICE guidance
audits.r2: 62/64 discharged directly from the ED (42 focal rigidity cast removed at home, 10 backslab, 10 crepe bandage); 2 returned to plaster room and 1 to fracture clinic

audits.t: The British Orthopaedic Oncology Management (BOOM) audit.
audits.st: BOOS/BOA guidelines for metastatic bone disease
audits.f: No designated MBD lead in 39% of centres (33/84); inadequate radiographs in 19% (160/846); no up-to-date staging CT in 29% (247/846); oncology opinion 69% (584/846); prognosis estimation 38% (223/846).

audits.t: Orthopaedic Out of Bed Project (OOBP): improving early mobilisation following femoral fracture using a therapy-led education programme.
audits.st: NHFD metric: patient mobilised (standing or hoisted) out of bed by the day after surgery; target at least the UK national average of 81%
audits.f: Mean 60% of patients mobilised by the day after surgery. Hip Sprint cohort (n=60): 1.7% mobilised by healthcare assistants before physiotherapy assessment.
audits.c: Therapy-led ward education programme for trauma healthcare assistants (1-hour 2:1 face-to-face session plus observed sign-off), ward posters and Trust media campaign, delivered over two PDSA cycles (June-July 2020 and June-August 2022)
audits.r2: Mean 79.2% mobilised by the day after surgery after PDSA cycle 2 (from 60% in 2019). Healthcare assistant mobilisation before physiotherapy assessment 30% (n=51 cohort).

audits.t: Management of displaced supracondylar fractures in children and adherence to the BOAST guideline- experience in a District General Hospital, UK.
audits.tp: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
audits.st: BOAST guideline for supracondylar fractures
audits.f: ED: capillary refill 65%, radial pulse 59.2%, individual nerve function 37.9%; pre-op nerve function 42.7%; 2 mm K-wires 53.3%; post-op pulse/CRT 27.2%, nerve function 9.7%
audits.c: Supracondylar fracture assessment proforma and focused educational sessions
audits.r2: ED: capillary refill 95.5% (p=0.0038), radial pulse 95.5% (p=0.0009), nerve function 72.7% (p=0.0040); pre-op nerve function 50%; 2 mm K-wires 89.5%; post-op pulse/CRT 54.2%, nerve function 50%

audits.t: An Audit on the Pre-operative Fasting Time of Trauma-List Orthopaedic Patients at a District General Hospital in Chichester, United Kingdom.
audits.st: RCN, AAGBI, European Society of Anaesthesiology and ASA guidelines: fasting of two hours for clear fluids and six hours for solids
audits.f: All 50 patients (100%) fasted beyond six hours for solids (mean 15.8 hours, range 9–24) and 49 (98%) beyond two hours for clear fluids (mean 10.5 hours, range 2–20); only 5 (10%) had correct documented fasting instructions; 31 (62%) were 'nil by mouth from midnight'.

audits.t: Audit on the Adequacy of Consenting Practices for Neck of Femur Fracture Surgeries.
audits.st: GMC Decision Making and Consent (2020), RCS England Consent: Supported Decision-Making (2016) and the BOA-endorsed orthoconsent.com model hip fracture consent form
audits.f: Infection documented in 98.4%, blood clots 95.2%, bleeding 92.1%, neurovascular injury 79.4%, dislocation 77.8%, pain 74.6%, anaesthetic complications 73%, failure 68.3%, leg length discrepancy 60.3%, bone damage/fracture 50.8%, death 49.2%, wound complications 42.9%, hip stiffness 14.3%, catheterisation 0%. Diagnosis missing in 22.2% (n=14), benefits in 12.7% (n=8), responsible consultant in 28.6% (n=18), blood transfusion in 25.4% (n=16).

audits.t: Development of a New Knee Arthroscopy Operative Proforma Saving Thousands of British Pounds.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Correct ICD-10 and OPCS-4 coding of arthroscopic knee procedures from the operation note; proforma based on Royal College guidance for operation notes
audits.f: 17/34 (50%) cases coded incorrectly; tariff value £85,026 as coded versus £114,351 after correction, a loss of £29,325.
audits.c: New coding-friendly knee arthroscopy operation note proforma with tick boxes, developed with coding staff and agreed at a consensus meeting, disseminated by email, notice boards and governance meetings.
audits.r2: 2/37 (5%) cases coded incorrectly; £86,886 as coded versus £89,540 after correction, a loss of £2654.

audits.t: Examining the Effectiveness of Telephone Clinics: A Review of a Telephone Foot and Ankle Orthopaedic Clinic in a District General Hospital in the United Kingdom.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Discharged 20 (19%); further face-to-face follow-up 52 (50%); further phone consult 12 (12%); did not attend 17 (17%); scans requested 5 (5%); listed for operation 2 (2%).
audits.c: Orthopaedic clinician-led triage to select patients for telephone clinic.
audits.r2: Discharged 44 (30%, p=0.030); further face-to-face follow-up 59 (40%, p=0.053); further phone consult 31 (21%, p=0.026); did not attend 13 (9%, p=0.033); scans requested 18 (12%, p=0.023); listed for operation 6 (4%, p=0.172).

audits.t: A Clinical Audit of Orthopaedic Clinical Documentation of Acute Ankle Fractures: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: BOAST ankle fracture standards and NICE NG37: documentation of mechanism, skin integrity, circulation, neurological examination and repeat neurovascular examination after reduction; target 100%
audits.f: Mechanism of injury 86%; skin integrity 54%; circulation status 54%; detailed vascular examination 17%; neurological examination 54%; sensory detail 48%; MRC motor scale 48%; repeat neurovascular examination after reduction 56%; overall precise documentation of clinical findings 17%.
audits.c: Targeted education on documentation standards at induction and trauma meetings, with case-based discussion reports; made a permanent part of departmental teaching.
audits.r2: Mechanism of injury 100%; skin integrity 100%; circulation status 88%; detailed vascular examination 88%; neurological examination 88%; sensory detail 88%; MRC motor scale 88%; repeat neurovascular examination after reduction 88%; overall precise documentation 88%.

audits.t: Suspected Cauda Equina Syndrome: Can the Presence of an Orthopaedic Doctor in the Emergency Department Reduce Waiting Times for MRI Scans and Inpatient Stays?
audits.tp: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
audits.st: NICE, BASS and SBNS guidelines and local trust protocol; National Suspected CES Pathway recommends MRI within four hours of request
audits.f: Mean MRI waiting time 12.5 hours (8am-4pm 9.5 h; 4pm-12am 18 h; 12am-8am 8.5 h); same-day discharge 27 (29%); inpatient stay 66 (71%)
audits.c: Introduction of a middle-grade trauma and orthopaedic doctor in the emergency department (urgent treatment centre) to assess suspected CES patients
audits.r2: Mean MRI waiting time 8 hours (8am-4pm 5.5 h; 4pm-12am 13 h; 12am-8am 6.5 h); all MRI scans and reports within 24 hours; same-day discharge 21 (58%); inpatient stay 15 (42%)

audits.t: Improving Completion Rates of Treatment Escalation Plan (TEP) in a London Teaching Hospital: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: Trust treatment escalation plan (TEP) policy: TEP completed for emergency adult admissions, within 48 hours
audits.f: Overall TEP completion 69.5%; completed within 48 hours 47.82%; mean time to complete 4.4 days; mean overrides 3.2; longest 35 days; 24 instances of skipping. Incomplete TEPs 30.4% (n=7).
audits.c: Revised local TEP pathway/algorithm allowing F1+ doctors to complete TEPs for young patients with simple fractures, algorithm displayed in trauma room, emails, individual teaching, and reminders to discuss TEP status on the post-take ward round.
audits.r2: Overall completion 88.2%; completed within 48 hours 35.29%; mean time 3.7 days; mean overrides 1.3; longest 13 days; 5 instances of skipping. Incomplete TEPs 11.76% (n=2).

audits.t: Introduction of a New Protocol to Limit the Number of Cancelled Elective Orthopaedic Operations Due to Asymptomatic Bacteriuria.
audits.tp: Elective cancellations due to asymptomatic bacteriuria
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 33 all-cause cancellations, 7 (21.2%) were cancelled for UTI risk on positive urinalysis; only 1 (14.3%) of these was symptomatic, so 6 (85.7%) were cancelled for asymptomatic bacteriuria.
audits.c: New symptom-based protocol from 1 May 2019: all patients complete a 7-item UTI symptom questionnaire and surgery is cancelled only if two or more symptoms are reported, regardless of urinalysis.
audits.r2: Of 45 all-cause cancellations, 2 (4.4%) were cancelled for UTI risk, both symptomatic; 4 (8.8%) had positive urinalysis, the 2 asymptomatic ones cancelled for unrelated reasons. No cancellations for asymptomatic bacteriuria; estimated 71.4% reduction in cancellations for UTI risk.

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Manipulation of Paediatric Forearm Fractures in the Emergency Department at a District General Hospital: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Paediatric buckle and forearm fracture management
audits.st: BOAST and GIRFT recommendations that units have protocols for manipulation of paediatric forearm fractures under procedural analgesia in the ED, avoiding admission and general anaesthesia; local standard operating procedure
audits.f: Pre-implementation (n=11 suitable fractures): manipulation in ED 1 (9.1%); theatre required 4 (36.4%).
audits.c: New standard operating procedure and paediatric fracture manipulation pathway in the ED using intranasal fentanyl and Entonox, agreed with ED, orthopaedics, radiology and theatre managers; information leaflets planned after cycle 2.
audits.r2: Third cycle (n=52): manipulation in ED 9 (17.3%); theatre required 1 (1.9%). All nine manipulable fractures were manipulated in the ED.

audits.t: Improving the Safety of Tourniquet Use in a Trauma Theatre According to the British Orthopaedic Association Guidelines: A Closed Loop Audit.
audits.st: BOAST guidance on the safe use of intraoperative tourniquets (2021): document skin condition and isolation method, pressure SBP + 50-100 mmHg upper limb and + 70-130 mmHg lower limb in adults, ischaemic time under 120 minutes
audits.f: Skin status documented 37%; isolation method documented 43%; tourniquet pressure documented 71%; pressure within BOAST safe limit 25%; tourniquet time under 120 minutes in 97%.
audits.c: Results presented at departmental audit meeting; tourniquet details made a mandatory part of the electronic operation note template; labels on tourniquet machines to calculate pressure; BOAST guidance posted in the theatre doctors' office.
audits.r2: Skin status documented 69% (p = 0.004); isolation method 74% (p = 0.003); pressure documented 94% (p = 0.003); pressure within BOAST safe limit 75%; tourniquet time under 120 minutes in 97%.

audits.t: Introducing a new proforma for the safe use of intraoperative tourniquets in orthopaedic surgery.
audits.st: BOAST 'The Safe Use of Intraoperative Tourniquets': document exsanguination method, isolation method, skin condition, pressure and duration; pressure lower limb SBP + 70–130 mmHg, upper limb SBP + 50–100 mmHg; duration ideally < 120 min
audits.f: Exsanguination method documented 5.6%, isolation (shut-off drape) 2.4%, skin condition 0%; duration not in operative note 23.0%, not recorded at all 1.6%; > 120 min in 1.6%; pressure within standard in 24.3% lower limb, 34.8% upper limb and 66.7% paediatric cases.
audits.c: Local presentation at trust Quality & Safety Half Day and 'PRESSURE' mnemonic posters in theatres and offices, followed by a new electronic patient record with a tourniquet section and BOAST-based auto-text proforma in the operation note.
audits.r2: Exsanguination method documented 42.9% (p = 0.001), isolation 42.9% (p = 0.0001), skin condition 64.3% (p = 0.0001); duration not in operative note 10.2% (p = 0.0269), not recorded 0%; none > 120 min; pressure within standard 13.0% lower limb, 35.7% upper limb, 14.2% paediatric (no significant change).

audits.t: Hand and Wrist Trauma: Antimicrobials and Infection-Audit of Clinical Practice (HAWAII-ACP).
audits.st: WHO global guidelines for the prevention of surgical site infection
audits.f: Surgical hand preparation 91%, drapes and gowns 92%, standard postoperative dressings 98%; adherence low for other antimicrobial practices

audits.t: The current standard of the shoulder trauma series in Ireland - A national audit.
audits.st: Pre-defined audit criteria for AP and axillary/Velpeau views
audits.f: Two views in 75.92% (n = 599); axillary or Velpeau view in 21.17% (n = 167); AP view met audit criteria in 23.09% (n = 181).

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Project to Measure and Improve the Quality of Below-Knee Ankle Cast Application in Emergency Departments.
audits.st: AO Foundation guidance: ankle immobilised in neutral plantigrade position; acceptable tibia-to-sole angle 80-100 degrees on lateral radiograph
audits.f: Mean angle 108.5 degrees (SD 11.7); 18/65 (27.7%) within 80-100 degrees (DGH 1 n=32, DGH 2 n=33).
audits.c: Single interactive session led by plaster technicians (for UTC nurses at DGH 1 and for ED junior doctors at DGH 2) plus educational posters where plastering occurred.
audits.r2: Mean angle 106.2 degrees (SD 11.9) (p=0.285); 23/61 (37.7%) within 80-100 degrees (p=0.231) (DGH 1 n=28, DGH 2 n=33).

audits.t: Audit of a Revised Pathway Aimed at Expediting Diagnosis and Treatment for Suspected Achilles Tendon Rupture.
audits.st: Timescales compared with 2018 local study (scan within 48 hours and one week; treatment decision within one week)
audits.f: Presentation to USS request 2.9 days; request to scan 6.8 days; 81% scanned within one week and 18% within 48 hours; presentation to treatment decision 10.9 days; 34.5% with plan within one week.
audits.c: Revised pathway allowing investigation and referral to be initiated by other healthcare professionals.
audits.r2: USS request 1.1 days; request to scan 3.2 days; 95% scanned within one week and 31.3% within 48 hours; treatment decision 6.2 days; 74.2% with plan within one week (p < .01).

audits.t: Current practice of pre-operative assessment at a public sector hospital in Pakistan - a clinical audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 249 responding surgeons: 98% ordered full blood count, 69.5% urea and creatinine, 92% viral markers, 78.7% blood glucose, 71.5% cardiac fitness tests.

audits.t: Traumatic Native Hip Dislocations: An Audit at a Major Trauma Centre and Assessment of Clinical Practice at Centres Across the United Kingdom.
audits.tp: Native hip dislocation time to reduction
audits.st: No formal standard; practice measured against reduction within 6 hours and 12 hours of injury, based on published research
audits.f: Mean time to reduction 532 minutes (240–804); 4 (29%) reduced within 6 hours and 11 (79%) within 12 hours (abstract gives 28.6% and 71.4%). ED reductions (n=2) mean 275 minutes vs theatre (n=13) 576 minutes.

audits.t: Preoperative investigation practices for elective surgical patients: clinical audit.
audits.st: NICE guideline on routine preoperative tests for elective surgery
audits.f: 350 investigations requested; 71 (20.28%) ordered without justification or against NICE recommendations (about 79.71% in line). FBC requested in 240 (97.16%); inappropriate FBC in 45 patients, ECG in 5, urinalysis in 4, hemostasis in 1, CXR in 1. Indicated PT/PTT not done in 4 and HbA1c not done in 4.

audits.t: Enhancing Clarity and Patient Safety: Evaluating the Inclusion of Laterality in Orthopaedic Outpatient Correspondence in Galway, Ireland.
audits.st: Laterality (left or right) stated in the diagnosis in outpatient clinic letters; no named guideline or target stated
audits.f: Laterality mentioned in 65.1% of letters. By grade: SHO 78.8%, registrar 62.7%, consultant 54.3% (P<0.05).
audits.c: Educational sessions on specifying laterality, reminder stickers placed in the clinic as visual prompts, and liaison with secretarial staff who transcribe dictated letters.

audits.t: International Lower Limb Collaborative Paediatric subpopulation analysis (INTELLECT-P) study: multicentre, international, retrospective audit of paediatric open fractures.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median time to antibiotics 2 h; median time to primary wound excision 11 h; combined orthopaedic and plastic surgery care from debridement in 14%; consultant-led excision 71%. Wound infection 20 (12%), deep infection 8 (5%), non-union 9 (6%).
audits.co: International (13 countries, 66 patients from the UK)

audits.t: Creating Novel Standards for Datapoints on an Elective Orthopaedic Theatre List Document.
audits.st: No existing standard; locally defined datapoints (surgical team, anaesthesia type, side, prosthesis/equipment, fluoroscopy, acronyms, extra patient information), later adopted as the 'William Harvey theatre list standard'
audits.f: 115 lists, 326 cases. Consultant in charge recorded in 85%; lead anaesthetist missing in 4.3%; 98% listed as GA (spinal 0.3%); 76.8% had no prosthesis/equipment detail; fluoroscopy requirement stated in 11% of cases needing it; acronyms used in 28%; extra patient information in 6%.
audits.c: Proforma of essential information for waiting list coordinators, minor IT changes to the theatre list input form, and education of waiting list coordinators and trainees.
audits.r2: 100 lists, 255 cases. Consultant in charge recorded in 100%; 80% listed as GA (14.5% spinal per abstract; 37 regional); no prosthesis/equipment detail fell to 43% (abstract: prosthesis/equipment mentioned 34% vs 23%); fluoroscopy stated in 25% of cases needing it; acronyms 6%; extra patient information 49.8%.

audits.t: Evaluating Compliance With the Ottawa Rules: A Retrospective Clinical Audit at a District General Hospital in the UK.
audits.tp: Ottawa rules and radiograph request appropriateness
audits.st: Ottawa Ankle and Knee Rules (incorporated in NICE guidance) for requesting X-rays
audits.f: Overall compliance 59.5%; knee X-rays 74.6% (n=182); ankle X-rays 33.1% (n=46). Positivity 18.0% knee and 32.0% ankle.
audits.c: Educational session, leaflets, posters in ED and UTC and emails to clinicians (August 2023).
audits.r2: Overall compliance 85% (221/260); knee X-rays 89.9% (152); ankle X-rays 75.8% (69). Positivity 18.9% knee and 44.0% ankle.

audits.t: Embracing Digital Transformation: A Three-Cycle Audit on Improving Intraoperative Tourniquet Documentation Following BOAST (British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma) Guidelines.
audits.st: BOAST safe use of intraoperative tourniquets: documented skin checks, isolation, exsanguination, pressure (SBP-based) and time; ischaemic time under 120 minutes
audits.f: Full adherence 3 (6.0%), partial 16 (32.0%), overall compliance 38.0%; not adhered 31 (62.0%).
audits.c: After EPR introduction: survey, department emails and theatre posters; then findings presented at audit meeting and an EPR smart phrase template with drop-downs and automatic SBP calculation introduced.
audits.r2: Full adherence 9 (18.0%), partial 22 (44.0%), overall compliance 62.0% (p=0.0005 vs 17.0% in cycle 2). Pressure documented 76%, time 94%, skin pre 56%, post 60%, isolation 60%, exsanguination 24%; pressure within standard 24 (63.1%).

audits.t: Treatment Outcomes of Dynamic Hip Screws Versus Short Intramedullary Nails for Extra-capsular Fragility Hip Fractures and Their Coding Audit.
audits.tp: Total hip replacement for intracapsular hip fracture
audits.st: NICE hip fracture guidance: sliding hip screw for 31A1/A2 fractures, intramedullary nail for 31A3 and reverse oblique fractures
audits.f: Compliance with national guidance on appropriate operation 63% (n=33/52) initially, 73% (n=38/52) after senior review of coding and classification; days to discharge from therapies 8.4 (short nail) vs 11 (DHS), P=0.03.

audits.t: Perioperative pain management intervention in older patients with hip fracture in an orthogeriatric unit. A controlled before/after study assessing an audit and feedback intervention (PAIN-AGE).
audits.tp: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block
audits.st: Unit pain protocol: routine acetaminophen 1 g three times a day (3 g/day) during the three postoperative days
audits.f: Postoperative 3 g/day acetaminophen 16% (16/99); preoperative 9%; nurse adherence to acetaminophen prescriptions 13% preoperatively and 13% postoperatively.
audits.c: Audit and feedback with nurses: two 1-hour pain teaching sessions, distribution of a pain assessment scale, protocol updated to 'give acetaminophen regardless of pain assessment', medicine staffing reviewed with clinical pharmacy, and night/weekend standby with a Saturday ward round.
audits.r2: Postoperative 3 g/day acetaminophen 60% (60/100) (OR 8.55, p < 0.001; versus control OR 6.76, p < 0.001); preoperative 16% (p = 0.13); nurse adherence 32% preoperatively and 52% postoperatively.

audits.t: Value of an orthopaedic admission proforma.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England record-keeping standards (GSP 2014); target 80% or more for all aspects
audits.f: Poor documentation of 50% of aspects: author name 50%, date 70%, medications 20%, functional status 30%, investigation results 30%, social history 40%, systemic review 75%
audits.c: Orthopaedic admission proforma introduced and discussed at morbidity and mortality meeting; then dedicated slots in departments and printable from any hospital computer
audits.r2: Author name 100%, date 100%, medications 95%, social history 70%, functional status 65%, systemic review 90%, investigation results 35%

audits.t: Orthoplastics Management of Open Lower Limb Fractures at a Major Trauma Centre: Audit of Adherence to BOAST4 Guidelines.
audits.st: BOAST 4 open lower limb fracture standards, e.g. IV antibiotics within 1 h of injury; debridement within 12 h for high-energy and 24 h for other fractures; definitive soft tissue cover within 72 h; gentamicin on induction; photographs; saline lavage
audits.f: Debridement within 24 h 81% (108/133); high-energy within 12 h 25% (15/60); mean time to first debridement 18.77 h. Definitive fixation/closure within 72 h 75% (95). Prehospital antibiotics within 1 h 76% (87/115); neurovascular documentation 94% (120/128); realignment and splinting 51% (45/89); photographs 86% (115); gentamicin on induction 65% (87); saline wash documented 78% (104).

audits.t: Orthopaedic audit--review of inpatient waiting lists.
audits.st: not reported
