audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Understanding Barriers to Early Rehabilitation Following the Surgery for Fragility Hip Fractures: A Single-Centre Audit.
audits.st: National guidelines (NICE): mobilisation on the day of or the day after hip fracture surgery; two hours of physiotherapy in the first week after surgery; no target stated
audits.f: 93% (106/113) seen by a physiotherapist on the day of or day after surgery (main orthopaedic ward 94%, 80/85; outliers 93%, 21/28; P=0.3). 40% (46/113) had delayed mobilisation. 83% (94/113) had two hours of physiotherapy in the first week. Clear documentation of mobilisation in 85% (97/113).

audits.t: Intra-articular knee injections in patients with primary osteoarthritis in a tertiary clinical setting: a best practice implementation project.
audits.st: JBI evidence-based audit criteria for selection and administration of intra-articular knee injections
audits.f: Low adherence with all audit criteria, including informed patient decision-making and recommending alternative treatments
audits.c: Educational briefings for physicians and informative flyers for patients
audits.r2: Substantial improvements in several criteria, including stepwise referral to conservative therapy and injection content

audits.t: Hip Fracture Management in a Major Trauma Centre: The Impact of 'Smart Phrase' Integration Into Electronic Clerking on Culture and Adherence to Guidelines.
audits.tp: Total hip replacement for intracapsular hip fracture
audits.st: NICE CG124 Section 1.6 (choice of arthroplasty, THR for eligible displaced intracapsular fractures, extramedullary implants for A1/A2 trochanteric fractures, intramedullary nail for subtrochanteric fractures)
audits.f: Overall compliance 76.04% (1244/1636). THR documented as considered in 43.6% (193/443) of eligible patients; 56.43% of THR-indicated patients had no documented consideration (65.41% in 2020).
audits.c: A 'smart phrase' NICE THR-eligibility checklist added to the electronic (Epic) neck of femur clerking proforma in June 2021.
audits.r2: Overall compliance 87.43% (459/525) (z = 5.556, p < 0.01). THR considered in 57.89% (77/133); 42.11% of THR-indicated patients lacked documented consideration (z = 2.904, p < 0.01).

audits.t: Oral Nutritional Supplementation in Older Adults with a Hip Fracture-Findings from a Bi-National Clinical Audit.
audits.st: ESPEN guideline and ANZ Hip Fracture Clinical Care Standard: all older adults with hip fracture should be offered oral nutritional supplements regardless of nutritional status
audits.f: ONS provided or prescribed for 182/385 (47.3%) of older adults having hip fracture surgery. ONS was more likely if malnourished on formal testing (OR 11.92; 95% CI 6.57, 21.69).

audits.t: Labelling of Fluids in the Sterile Field During Orthopaedic Surgery: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Labelling of fluids in the sterile field
audits.st: Royal Pharmaceutical Society and Royal College of Anaesthetists guidelines: all syringes/containers of fluid in the sterile field labelled with fluid name and concentration
audits.f: 3/30 procedures (10%) compliant with labelling guidelines; labelling information adequate in only 1 of these 3
audits.c: Sterile stickers with surgical marker pens for labelling by the scrub nurse, a mandatory 'tactical pause and check' after opening sets, and an awareness campaign (posters, emails, educational sessions)
audits.r2: 32/34 procedures (94%) compliant (p<0.00001, Fisher's exact test); labelling adequate in 28 of labelled cases

audits.t: The National Joint Registry Data Quality Audit of elbow arthroplasty.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Completeness of NJR elbow dataset against Hospital Episode Statistics, and accuracy of recorded components
audits.f: Completeness 63%; radial head arthroplasty completeness 35%; accuracy 94%; 5539 unmatched and 448 inaccurate arthroplasties from 254 hospitals
audits.c: National collaborative audit through trainees: hospitals checked records, added missing arthroplasties and corrected inaccurate ones
audits.r2: Completeness 83% (total elbow arthroplasty 93%); radial head arthroplasty completeness 70%; accuracy 98% after correcting 212 of 448

audits.t: Evaluating the Compliance to 24-Hour Venous Thromboembolism Risk Re-assessment Following Orthopaedic Surgery at a Tertiary Center: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit.
audits.st: NICE VTE guideline (over 16s): VTE risk reassessment within 24 hours after surgery; target 100%
audits.f: 6/4780 (0.13%) had VTE reassessment completed within 24 hours of surgery.
audits.c: Automated system prompt on EPMA reminding staff to complete VTE reassessment 24 hours after surgery.
audits.r2: 112/156 (74%) completed within 24 hours (p<0.0001); 131/156 (83%) completed at any time.

audits.t: Evaluation of Patient-Initiated Follow-Up (PIFU) Service in a Fracture Clinic: A Comprehensive Service Evaluation and Patient Satisfaction Audit.
audits.tp: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
audits.st: Local SMART objective: satisfaction rate of at least 80% among patients assigned to PIFU
audits.f: 203 of 3828 fracture clinic patients (5.3%) assigned to PIFU; 183 (90.15%) received the leaflet; 41 (20.2%) used PIFU; 163 (80.3%) rated the service 5/5 and all 203 reported satisfaction, so the 80% target was met.

audits.t: Improving Patient Care and Streamlining Follow-Up: Compliance With National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Pediatric Distal Radius Buckle Fractures.
audits.tp: Paediatric buckle and forearm fracture management
audits.st: NICE guidance for children's distal radius buckle fractures: removable splint instead of full cast and no routine follow-up; no target stated
audits.f: ED: 0% splint (all back slab). Fracture clinic: 62 (95.4%) full cast, 3 (4.6%) splint. Discharged at first visit 5 (7.7%); second visit 56 (86.2%); third visit 4 (6.2%).
audits.c: New ED and fracture clinic pathway (splint or soft cast with information leaflet and no follow-up), posters in ED and fracture clinic, and email reminders to staff.
audits.r2: ED: 17 (19.5%) splint, 70 (80.4%) back slab. Fracture clinic: 44 (50.6%) converted to splint and 2 remained in splint (53%), 41 (47.1%) cast. Discharged at first visit 39 (44.8%); second visit 48 (55.2%).

audits.t: A Retrospective Audit of Osteoporosis Management Following Fragility Fractures in a Hospital Setting.
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: Six Standards of Hip Care (assessment for antiresorptive medication after fragility fracture) and NOGG UK 2021 guidance; NICE recommendations on vitamin D and bone protection
audits.f: Inpatient bisphosphonates started in 23/144 (16%); 105/121 (87%) not started by GP after discharge; FRAX recorded in 78/144 (54%); vitamin D assessed in 89/144 (62%) and replaced in 78/144 (54%); 110/144 no DEXA scan; 34/144 (25%) referred to metabolic bone clinic
audits.c: Teaching sessions, MDT meetings and bedside teaching; local protocol flowcharts; push to start antiresorptives before discharge; new orthogeriatrics SHO role; new older people osteoporosis clinic
audits.r2: 105/165 (64%) did not receive appropriate bisphosphonates (34 started as inpatients); 104/131 (around 80%) not started by GP after discharge; FRAX recorded in 30/165 (18%); vitamin D checked in 57/165 (35%) and 99/165 (60%) received no replacement; DEXA and bone clinic referrals remained low

audits.t: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on the Implementation and Adoption of a Virtual Fracture Clinic Pathway: A Closed Loop Audit.
audits.tp: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
audits.st: Three modified BOASTs: early senior review (BOAST: new fracture clinic within 72 hours; measured as VFC review within 24 hours), minimising outpatient visits, and patient-initiated follow-up as the default; no target stated
audits.f: 39% of non-operative patients triaged to the VFC within 24 hours; 61% sent directly to face-to-face clinic. 35,399 face-to-face fracture clinic appointments (also given as 35,339 in the results).
audits.c: COVID-19-era policy changes: mandatory VFC triage of all non-operative injuries via a smartphone referral app with daily consultant-led multidisciplinary review, and an early appropriate discharge / patient-initiated follow-up policy; national lockdowns also occurred.
audits.r2: 100% of non-operative patients assessed in the VFC within 24 hours. Face-to-face appointments fell to 17,639, a 50.2% reduction: 3.7% attributed to national lockdowns, 14.7% to VFC triage and 35.5% to early appropriate discharge.

audits.t: Looped quality improvement project of consent forms in patients admitted with hip fracture.
audits.st: BOA standardised list of risks for NOF fracture procedures
audits.f: Average of only 56.6% of risks included on each consent form; significant risks such as mortality frequently missed.
audits.c: Stickers for consent forms and team education sessions.

audits.t: Early Screening for Confusion and Vitamin D Deficiency in Elderly Hip Fracture Patients: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Mitigate the Risk of Postoperative Delirium.
audits.tp: Hip fracture delirium and cognitive assessment
audits.st: Confusion screening (AMTS) and vitamin D testing within 24 hours of admission in hip fracture patients aged 60 and over (no target stated)
audits.f: 27/100 (27%) screened; 14/27 (51.85%) of screens done within 24 hours.
audits.c: Educational sessions for clinicians, nurses and ancillary staff, posters, email reminders and screening prompts added to the admission checklist (July 2023).

audits.t: Improving Adherence to National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for the Use of Tranexamic Acid in Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: NICE: combined topical and intravenous tranexamic acid in knee arthroplasty for patients without renal impairment (1 g IV only with significant renal impairment)
audits.f: TXA used in 20 (48.8%), not used in 21 (51.2%); combined IV and topical 3 (7.3%); IV only 14 (34.1%); topical only 3 (7.3%).
audits.c: Targeted emails to consultants and registrars, presentation at a specialty meeting, and posters on TXA and NICE guidance on computers across the elective surgical suite.
audits.r2: TXA used in 38 (73.1%) (p=0.016), not used in 14 (26.9%); combined IV and topical 16 (30.8%) (p=0.005); IV only 22 (42.3%).

audits.t: Preoperative Templating Prior to Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Closed-Loop Audit.
audits.st: Templating radiographs 7–180 days before THA (New Zealand Orthopaedic Association, South African Arthroplasty Society and GIRFT guidance); goal 100%
audits.f: 10/50 (20%) had templating radiographs within 7–180 days; mean 140 days (range 0–788) from latest radiograph to surgery.
audits.c: Departmental protocol requiring preoperative assessment with templating radiographs, education of NCHDs on radiographs to order, and a departmental rota assigning NCHDs to order them.

audits.t: The positive impact of a quality improvement collaborative on process indicators for geriatric hip fracture care.
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: Adherence to 23 quality indicators for geriatric hip fracture care
audits.f: Lowest adherence: nerve blocks 8.0%, steroids 9.7%, tranexamic acid 22.2%.
audits.c: Anonymous benchmarking fed back to centres and three educative sessions on specific topics.
audits.r2: Nerve blocks 25.4%, steroids 26.4%, tranexamic acid 30.7% (significant improvement).

audits.t: Adding value in radiology-improved radiological diagnosis of osteoporotic vertebral fragility fractures following National UK Audit and Interventions.
audits.tp: Vertebral fragility fracture reporting on CT
audits.st: RCR audit standards for reporting incidental vertebral fragility fractures on CT
audits.f: Audit standards not achieved.
audits.c: A series of interventions (not detailed in abstract).
audits.r2: Generalised improvement in compliance, including a 6-percentage point increase in moderate/severe VFFs reported.

audits.t: Improved radiological diagnosis of osteoporotic vertebral fragility fractures following UK-wide interventions and re-audit-can this be maintained and translated into clinical practice?
audits.tp: Vertebral fragility fracture reporting on CT
audits.st: RCR national audit of reporting vertebral fragility fractures (Genant grading) on non-trauma CT including the thoracolumbar spine in patients over 70
audits.f: Moderate/severe vertebral fragility fractures reported in 26%.
audits.c: A series of UK-wide interventions between audits (details not given in the abstract).
audits.r2: Moderate/severe vertebral fragility fractures reported in 32%; VFF incidence 21.7%; improvements across all patient-related and organisational parameters.

audits.t: Improving Orthostatic Hypotension Screening in Fall Prevention: A Two-Cycle Audit on Falls Assessment and Lying and Standing Blood Pressure Measurement.
audits.st: NICE falls guidance: completion of falls assessment and lying and standing blood pressure measurement; target 100%
audits.f: Falls assessment completed 38/41 (93%); lying and standing BP recorded 14/41 (34%).
audits.c: Cycle 1 results presented at departmental teaching, daily reminders at the morning huddle, educational flyers and targeted education for doctors, nurses and healthcare staff.
audits.r2: Falls assessment completed 40/41 (98%) (p = 0.61); lying and standing BP recorded 28/41 (68%) (p = 0.004).

audits.t: Assessment of urgent investigative images transfer effectiveness from trauma and orthopaedic to neurosurgery department: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Image transfer time for neurosurgical referrals
audits.st: 100% of NORSe referrals should have images sent to neurosurgery within 1 hour; neurosurgery should review imaging and respond within 6 hours at least 90% of the time
audits.f: Mean time from referral to image transfer 18 hours; 36% (n=14) transferred within 1 hour; neurosurgery response averaged 18 hours with 38% (n=14) reviewed within 6 hours.
audits.c: Image exchange portal software introduced so T&O registrars, then junior doctors, could send images directly without the PACS team; supported by departmental presentation, video demonstration, emailed instructions, QR-code posters and induction teaching.
audits.r2: Mean time to image transfer 3.6 hours; 61% (n=96) transferred within 1 hour; neurosurgery response averaged 7 hours with 87% (n=138) reviewed within 6 hours; 45% (71) of images sent by the T&O team.

audits.t: Improving the suspected cauda equina syndrome pathway at a district general hospital: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
audits.st: GIRFT National Suspected CES Pathway 2023: emergency MRI within 4 hours of request; local SMART aim of median under 4 hours from ED attendance to MRI within 1 year
audits.f: Median time from ED presentation to MRI 5.9 hours (IQR 4.9–14.7) although median MRI request to scan was 1.7 hours (IQR 1.1–3.7), meeting the GIRFT target; 8% of patients incorrectly sent to the GP-led MEDOCC service. At PDSA 1: 38% of MRIs unnecessary, 0.5 CES MRIs/day, time to analgesia 5.3 hours (IQR 3.8–7.0), 9% inappropriately triaged to MEDOCC.
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles (July 2023 to January 2024): CES working group and trust-level awareness; new locally adapted SOP based on the GIRFT pathway with CES-specific shorter MRI sequences; ED triage and assessment posters, board round, grand round and senior-led teaching. Planned extension of MRI hours was not achieved.
audits.r2: Approximately 27 patients per cycle. Median ED presentation to MRI 5.7 hours (IQR 4.1–14.3), primary aim not met; GIRFT 4-hour request-to-scan target met in all cycles. Unnecessary MRIs fell from 38% to 18%, CES MRIs 0.5/day to 0.4/day, time to analgesia 5.3 to 4.2 hours (IQR 2.7–7.0), and inappropriate MEDOCC referrals 9% to 0%.

audits.t: Clinical audit of Ankylos implant abutment fractures for a ten-year period in practice.
audits.st: Published abutment fracture rate from literature review: median 2.2% (all studies) and 1.8% (Ankylos-specific studies)
audits.f: Overall abutment fracture rate 0.6% (105/17,207), 1.6% below the 2.2% literature rate and 1.2% below the 1.8% Ankylos rate; first molar fracture rate 1.9% (87/4,709)

audits.t: A multicenter audit of 1295 daptomycin prescriptions in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region.
audits.st: Guidelines on daptomycin prescribing (appropriateness assessed by local referent)
audits.f: 87.1% (1128) appropriate; of 132 inappropriate prescriptions, 33.3% wrong indication, 25% no de-escalation, 16.7% wrong dose, 15.9% wrong duration

audits.t: Assessing Compliance With Ottawa Foot and Ankle Rules in the Emergency Department: A Closed-Loop Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Ottawa rules and radiograph request appropriateness
audits.st: ED clerking documentation and X-ray request clinical details should contain the relevant Ottawa Ankle or Foot Rule criteria in all cases (NICE; RCR/IR(ME)R 2017)
audits.f: 100 ankle and 100 foot X-ray requests. Ankle: documentation compliance 74%, X-ray request compliance 43%. Foot: documentation compliance 48%, X-ray request compliance 32%.
audits.c: First-cycle results distributed and an Ottawa rules handout given to ED staff, plus a small-group teaching session for ED junior doctors on assessing, documenting and requesting foot and ankle X-rays (mid-April 2024)
audits.r2: Ankle: documentation 87% (p<.05), X-ray request 57% (p<.05). Foot: documentation 78% (p<.001 in abstract; p<.0001 in results), X-ray request 54% (p<.01).

audits.t: Improving Patient Care and Clinical Services: Compliance With the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis After Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
audits.st: NICE VTE guidance: THR 28 days LMWH plus anti-embolism stockings until discharge; TKR 14 days LMWH plus stockings
audits.f: THR 23/25 (92%) and TKR 20/23 (87%) received enoxaparin plus stockings; overall compliance 90%.
audits.c: Arthroplasty discharge pack displayed as posters and handouts at the arthroplasty station, regular teaching sessions on NICE discharge guidance, and final check of discharge letters by the nurse in charge.
audits.r2: THR 24/24 (100%) and TKR 22/23 (96%) correct; overall compliance 98%.

audits.t: Designing a new orthopaedic trauma meeting proforma to improve documentation in a large UK teaching hospital.
audits.st: Locally designed trauma meeting documentation standards (no UK guideline exists); record keeping guidance from GMC, RCS England and BMA
audits.f: 58/90 (64%) had some documentation. Consultant on call 43%, other consultants 29%, imaging 20%, MDT concerns 7%, diagnosis 29%, laterality 22%, clear plan 63%, weight-bearing 1%.
audits.c: Electronic trauma meeting proforma (EPR shortcut) introduced, then revised after MDT feedback (theatre checklist added); teaching video and poster for new doctors before the one-year re-audit.
audits.r2: 71/85 (84%) had some documentation. Consultant on call, other consultants and imaging 100%, diagnosis 97%, laterality 75%, clear plan 98%.

audits.t: Joint resolution. Rationale for criteria for a medical audit of total knee replacement.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: A Clinical Audit of Perioperative Antibiotic Prophylaxis and Intraoperative Monitoring in Orthopaedic Trauma Surgery: An Audit Cycle.
audits.st: Northern Care Alliance 2023 orthopaedic antibiotic prophylaxis guideline (choice, timing within 60 minutes, duration) and NICE NG180 (blood pressure within 20% of baseline, core temperature 36.5-37.5°C); 100% target for timing and blood pressure
audits.f: Correct intraoperative antibiotic 68/104 (65.4%); given within 60 minutes 104/104 (100%); postoperative duration compliant 67/104 (64.4%); overuse 25/104 (24%); blood pressure within target 104/104 (100%); temperature documented 36/104 (35%).
audits.c: Planned: EPR alerts for antibiotic choice and duration, mandatory temperature documentation fields, staff education and a compliance dashboard; re-audit planned in six months.

audits.t: A Retrospective Audit of the Management of Shoulder Dislocations at a Trauma Unit.
audits.st: Health board clinical pathway for traumatic anterior shoulder instability, aligned with BOA and BESS guidance (pre- and post-reduction radiographs, neurovascular assessment, specialist follow-up)
audits.f: Pre- and post-reduction radiographs in 97/100 (97%), post-reduction only in 3 (3%); MUA successful in 98 (98%); mean time to reduction 152 minutes; nerve injury in 28 (28%)

audits.t: Evaluating the Impact of Audits and Re-audits on Adherence to the Ottawa Knee Rules in a High-Volume UK Trauma Centre.
audits.tp: Ottawa rules and radiograph request appropriateness
audits.st: Ottawa Knee Rules (endorsed by NICE and RCR iRefer) documented in knee radiograph requests; target 100%
audits.f: At least one OKR criterion documented 41%; age >=55 52%; fibular head tenderness 3%; isolated patellar tenderness 13%; inability to flex to 90 degrees 3%; inability to bear weight 14%. Adequate documentation: orthopaedic SHOs/registrars 35.7%, ENPs/ANPs/triage 52.4%.
audits.c: Posters and leaflets in clinical areas, presentations at departmental meetings, formal and informal teaching, and emails summarising the rules.
audits.r2: At least one OKR criterion 91% (p<0.01); age 62%; fibular head tenderness 68%; patellar tenderness 72%; inability to flex 65%; inability to bear weight 57%. Adequate documentation: orthopaedic SHOs/registrars 92.9%, ENPs/ANPs/triage 88.2%.

audits.t: Improving the rate of use of fascia iliaca compartment blocks in patients presenting with hip fractures.
audits.tp: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block
audits.st: Target fascia iliaca block in 50% of hip fracture patients within 18 months
audits.f: Baseline fascia iliaca block rate 2.0%; 6 physicians performing it.
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: educational materials and standardised equipment carts; staff and trainee education sessions; further education, audit and feedback, and incentives.
audits.r2: Fascia iliaca block rate 22.6%; 35 physicians performing it; special cause variation (shift) on SPC chart.

audits.t: The impact of direct oral anticoagulants on hip fracture care in Australia and New Zealand: a prospective patient sprint audit.
audits.st: ANZ hip fracture clinical care standard and international consensus: surgery within 36 hours (including for patients on DOACs)
audits.f: Median time to surgery 39 h (IQR 24–48) on DOACs, 25 h (IQR 20–39) on no antithrombotic and 27 h (IQR 20–44) on other antithrombotics; DOAC patients had higher odds of surgery >36 h (aOR 3.65, 95% CI 2.40–5.55); 43% of DOAC patients had surgery within 36 h versus 61% on other antithrombotics.

audits.t: Improving Adherence to Perioperative Cognitive Assessment Documentation in Hip Fracture Patients: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Hip fracture delirium and cognitive assessment
audits.st: NICE: cognitive assessment (AMTS or 4AT) within 24 hours of admission for hip fracture patients aged 65 and over, with regular postoperative assessment
audits.f: Admission AMTS within 24 hours 15 (78.9%); postoperative AMTS 18 (94.7%); postoperative 4AT 9 (47.4%); no postoperative delirium.
audits.c: Educational posters with QR codes for AMTS and 4AT calculators on wards and doctors' office, and a staff training session for doctors.
audits.r2: Admission AMTS 29 (96.7%); postoperative AMTS 26 (86.7%); postoperative 4AT 18 (60.0%); postoperative delirium 6 (20.0%).

audits.t: Post-operative Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis for Non-arthroplasty Knee Surgery: A Closed Loop Clinical Audit.
audits.st: NICE VTE guidance: prophylaxis after arthroscopy if anaesthetic time 90 minutes or more (or VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk), and after all other non-arthroplasty knee surgery; target 100%
audits.f: Arthroscopy with anaesthetic time >90 minutes 2/4 (50%) received prophylaxis; other non-arthroplasty surgery 9/25 (36%).
audits.c: Formal teaching session for the joint replacement unit team by a senior consultant on recording anaesthetic time, weight-bearing status and VTE prescription on operation notes and postoperative instructions.

audits.t: Assessing the Quality of Operative Notes in the Orthopedic Surgery Department at Gezira Traumatology Center, Sudan, in Accordance With the Royal College of Surgeons Guidelines.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice operative note guidance (14 parameters)
audits.f: Mean compliance 82.0%; theatre anaesthetist name 1 (4.3%), anticipated blood loss 3 (13%), antibiotic prophylaxis 2 (8.7%), complications 12 (52.2%); procedure 22 (95.7%) and signature 23 (100%)
audits.c: Staff education, a standardised RCS-aligned operative note template, posters in theatres and staff areas, and a senior feedback mechanism
audits.r2: Mean compliance 83.4%; anaesthetist name 19 (82.6%), anticipated blood loss 19 (82.6%), antibiotic prophylaxis 16 (69.6%), complications 21 (91.3%)

audits.t: Evaluating Compliance to Intra-operative Syndesmosis Stress Testing During Ankle Fracture Fixation: Are We Stressing It?
audits.st: BOAST ankle fracture guidance; radiological evidence of intra-operative syndesmosis stress testing saved and documented on operation notes, target 80% each
audits.f: Radiological evidence saved 55% (n=49); documentation on operation notes 71% (n=63); neither in 25% (n=22).
audits.c: Findings presented at clinical governance; poster in on-call room and theatre areas and a teaching presentation by an associate specialist foot and ankle surgeon.
audits.r2: Radiological evidence saved 82% (n=41), p=0.001; documentation 82% (n=41), p=0.14; neither in 6% (n=3). Both targets met.

audits.t: Weight-Bearing Status After Peri-Prosthetic Proximal Femur Fracture Open Reduction and Internal Fixation (ORIF) or Revision Arthroplasty: A Clinical Audit.
audits.st: British Hip Society guidance: aim for full weight-bearing in the immediate postoperative period; no target stated
audits.f: 28 (73.7%) had surgery (19 ORIF, 9 revision). Of these, 22 (78.6%) were full weight-bearing, 4 (14.3%) limited weight-bearing and 2 (7.2%) non-weight-bearing. One fixation failure (3.5%).
audits.c: Results presented at a local orthopaedic educational meeting on aiming for immediate full weight-bearing; no re-audit reported.

audits.t: Improving the compliance of orthopaedic wrist and hand referrals against the musculoskeletal recommendations from the 2018 Evidence-based Interventions programme, along with local guidance in Greater Manchester: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Hand and wrist surgical referral compliance with Evidence-based Interventions guidance
audits.st: 2018 Evidence-based Interventions programme and Greater Manchester local guidance for carpal tunnel release, Dupuytren's release, ganglion excision and trigger finger release; project target ≥85% (provider internal national target 95%)
audits.f: Referral compliance 70%, 15% below the provider's internal national average and 25% below its 95% internal target.
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles over 14 weeks: education session and case discussions, digital folder with clinical referral flowchart, knowledge quiz with case discussions, repeat quiz and Q&A.
audits.r2: Compliance 71% after PDSA 1, 85% after PDSA 2, 99% after PDSA 3 and 100% in PDSA 4; average compliance improved 16% against the audit, 1% above the 85% target.

audits.t: Variation in post-operative weight-bearing practice following hip fracture surgery: A national hip fracture audit review.
audits.st: NICE hip fracture guideline (2011): early unrestricted weight-bearing after surgery; no target stated
audits.f: 93.2% full weight-bearing, 3.1% (2310) non-weight-bearing and 3.6% not recorded. Nine hospitals made 10% or more of cases non-weight-bearing; one site recorded 100% non-weight-bearing.

audits.t: Adequacy of Lateral Ankle Radiograph Views in Acute Trauma Setting: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: BOAST and radiographic positioning criteria for a true lateral ankle view (four criteria); target 100% for each
audits.f: Criterion 1 (fibula superimposed by posterior tibia) 83%; criterion 2 (talar domes superimposed) 61%; criterion 3 (open uniform tibiotalar joint) 69%; criterion 4 (landmarks included) 99%.
audits.c: Posters in the emergency department and orthopaedic on-call room/radiography suites, and a teaching session by a foot and ankle associate specialist for orthopaedic staff and radiographers.

audits.t: A Retrospective Audit of the Timescales Involved in the Diagnosis and Management of Soft Tissue Knee Injuries at a Single National Health Service Trust: A Quality Service Improvement and Redesign Project.
audits.tp: Soft tissue knee injury pathway timescales and MRI use
audits.st: NHS Constitution RTT standard (92% of consultant-led pathways completed within 18 weeks); Diagnostics DM01 standard (<1% waiting over six weeks for MRI); BOA/BOAST and regional MSK guidance of MRI within two weeks where diagnosis uncertain, with review within 7-14 days; NICE CKS and EBI guidance on selective MRI
audits.f: MRI utilisation 77.7% (269/346). Median waits: presentation to knee clinic 7 days, MRI referral to scan 33 days, scan to review 22 days; median presentation to diagnosis 60 days and to definitive management 97 days. 58.0% waited over four weeks for MRI; only 11.9% scanned within one week; 10.3% reviewed within seven days and 26.2% within 14 days. 42.8% of MRIs normal/degenerative.

audits.t: Optimising Hand Trauma Management in a Tertiary National Health Service (NHS) Plastic Surgery Department: A Quality Improvement Initiative Aligned With the United Kingdom's Prevalence Data and British Society for Surgery of the Hand (BSSH) Guidelines.
audits.tp: Distal radius fracture time to surgery
audits.st: BSSH hand trauma standards: open fractures/joints and bites within 24 hours, other open injuries within four days, closed fractures within seven days; project target 80% compliance
audits.f: Overall compliance 73% (part of national BSSH-RSTN collaborative audit).
audits.r2: Overall compliance 83% (82/99); open soft tissue 97% (32/33); bites 100% (10/10); open fractures/joints 64% (9/14); tendon injuries 76.5% (13/17); closed fractures 67% (16/24), surgical fixation 50% (7/14); median decision-to-surgery time 42.7 hours.

audits.t: Assessing Adequacy of Marker Ball Placement in Preoperative Pelvic X-rays: Are We Missing the Mark?
audits.st: Local trauma unit guideline: marker ball entirely visible and placed between the femurs inferior to the symphysis pubis; agreed target 80% for each
audits.f: Marker ball present in 27 (45%). Of these, entirely visible 16 (59%) and correctly positioned 11 (41%); overall compliance 59% (n=16).
audits.c: Poster reminders in radiography areas, a presentation to the radiography team by a T&O registrar, and a mandatory checklist for all such X-rays.
audits.r2: Marker ball present in 39 (78%). Entirely visible 33 (84%, p=0.042) and correctly positioned 32 (82%, p=0.0014); overall compliance 80% (n=31, p=0.132), meeting the target.

audits.t: Improving Clinical Management in ENT Casualty: A Multi-domain Quality Improvement Project Using a Digital Toolkit.
audits.tp: ENT casualty management of common acute presentations
audits.st: NICE Clinical Knowledge Summaries (otitis externa), ENT UK nasal trauma guidance, ENT UK position statement and AAO-HNS guideline (SSNHL), British Rhinological Society epistaxis guideline; e.g. audiogram within 24 hours for SSNHL, nasal fracture review within 7 days
audits.f: Tympanic membrane integrity documented in otitis externa 34.3%; nasal fracture reviewed within 7 days 58.3%, MUA within 14 days 92.9%; SSNHL audiogram within 24 hours 33.3%; epistaxis cautery for visible vessel 87.2%, documentation of counselling 28.0%.
audits.c: Web-based ENT toolkit with QR-code access in casualty, condition-specific pathways, structured documentation templates, procedure checklists and diagrams, introduced to FY doctors at induction with a short training session.
audits.r2: Tympanic membrane documentation 67.7% (p = 0.002); nasal fracture review within 7 days 94.7% (p = 0.006), MUA within 14 days 100% (p = 0.31); SSNHL audiogram within 24 hours 80.0% (p = 0.09); epistaxis cautery 98.1% (p = 0.03), counselling documented 46.0%.

audits.t: Orthogonal Radiographs After Shoulder Reduction: Are We Meeting the Standard?
audits.st: BESS guideline and local hospital policy: orthogonal post-reduction views (AP plus axillary or scapular Y view)
audits.f: Adequate orthogonal post-reduction radiographs in 5/22 (22.7%, 95% CI 10.1-43.4); 17/22 (77.3%) inadequate, with inadequacy recognised by resident doctors in 2/17 (11.8%).

audits.t: Suspected Achilles Tendon Ruptures and the Course of Action: Assessing Compliance With Local Protocols.
audits.st: Local UHD Achilles tendon rupture pathway: VTE prophylaxis, boot with wedges, non-weight-bearing advice, ultrasound within 14 days and virtual fracture clinic referral; target 100%
audits.f: VTE prophylaxis 110/138 (80%); boot immobilisation 110/138 (80%); ultrasound within 14 days 59/138 (43%); non-weight-bearing advice 91/138 (66%); VFC referral 132/138 (96%).
audits.c: Results emailed with recommendations, pathway posters displayed in ED, orthopaedic team room and fracture clinic, and a new 'Ultrasound Achilles' imaging request form.
audits.r2: VTE prophylaxis 35/44 (80.5%, p=0.91); boot immobilisation 38/44 (86%, p=0.04); ultrasound within 14 days 26/44 (59%, p=0.03); non-weight-bearing advice 29/44 (66%, p=0.99); VFC referral 44/44 (100%, p=0.01).

audits.t: Enhancing Cognitive Impairment Assessment and Management in Hip Fracture Patients: A Two-Cycle Clinical Audit.
audits.tp: Hip fracture delirium and cognitive assessment
audits.st: BOAST hip fracture standards and NICE guidance on cognitive assessment; AMTS documented at admission, postoperative days 1 and 2, and day 4; target 80% compliance
audits.f: Initial AMTS 14/30 (46.7%); postoperative day 1 0/30 (0%); postoperative day 2 0/30 (0%); day 4 19/30 (63.3%); overall 33/120 assessments (27.5%).
audits.c: Automated Cerner EPR alerts prompting AMTS at set timepoints, mandatory 90-minute staff training, AMTS built into handover and ward round templates, visual reminders, and monthly audit feedback.

audits.t: Analgesia and Fascia Iliaca Compartment Block Utilisation for Neck-of-Femur Fracture Patients: A Closed-Loop Audit.
audits.tp: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block
audits.st: NICE CG124 and RCEM guidance: FICB performed where applicable (100%); contraindications documented if FICB not performed (100%); pain re-evaluation within 30 minutes of analgesia (100%)
audits.f: FICB performed 26/40 (65%); contraindications documented in 0/14 (0%) without FICB; pain re-evaluation within 30 min 21 (52.5%); mean time to first analgesia 130 ± 28.8 min; mean time to FICB 228 ± 36.2 min.
audits.c: Practical sessions to familiarise ED clinicians with FICB, and a mandatory analgesia checklist for all suspected neck of femur fractures (pain scores, analgesia times, FICB details and reason if not given).
audits.r2: FICB performed 26/40 (65%, p=0.74); contraindications documented in 9/14 (64.3%); pain re-evaluation within 30 min 20 (50%, p=0.99); mean time to first analgesia 38.8 ± 13.2 min (p<0.001); mean time to FICB 63.4 ± 19.1 min (p=0.002).

audits.t: Audit of Ottawa Knee Rules Compliance in the Emergency Department: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Study at a General Hospital.
audits.tp: Ottawa rules and radiograph request appropriateness
audits.st: RCR iRefer guidelines: ≥95% of knee radiographs requested in accordance with Ottawa Knee Rules; ≥95% of requests documenting an OKR indication; unnecessary imaging ≤10%
audits.f: OKR compliance 50 (72.5%); non-compliant requests 19 (27.5%); documentation of suspected fracture/bone injury 23 (32.9%); negative X-rays 37 (52.9%)
audits.c: Interactive teaching session for ED clinicians, OKR leaflets distributed and emailed, and posters in ED clinical areas and beside imaging request stations
audits.r2: OKR compliance 66 (83.5%) (χ²=2.05, p=0.15); non-compliant requests 13 (16.5%); documentation of suspected fracture/bone injury 44 (55.7%) (p=0.01); negative X-rays 30 (38.0%) (p=0.08)

audits.t: Traumatic Ankle Injuries in the Emergency Department: Evaluating the Adequacy of Clinical Documentation With Reference to the Ottawa Ankle Rules.
audits.tp: Ottawa rules and radiograph request appropriateness
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists: 100% of ankle plain-film requests for trauma should reference the Ottawa Ankle Rules
audits.f: 37/100 (37%) requests referenced the OAR. 21 (21%) fractures; 13 (61.9%) of these requests documented the OAR and 8 (38.1%) did not (P = 0.011).
audits.c: Findings presented at clinical governance meetings; focused education sessions for front-line clinicians and targeted briefings for radiographers who vet X-ray requests.
audits.r2: 51/100 (51%) requests referenced the OAR (P = 0.046). 31 (31%) fractures; 26 (83.9%) had OAR documented and 5 (16.1%) did not (P < 0.001).

audits.t: Time to Surgery for Distal Radius Fractures: A Quality Improvement Audit.
audits.tp: Distal radius fracture time to surgery
audits.st: BOAST distal radius fracture guidance: intra-articular fractures operated within 72 hours and extra-articular within seven days; local target ≥80%
audits.f: Intra-articular within 3 days of injury 16/27 (59%); extra-articular within 7 days of injury 24/26 (92%); intra-articular within 3 days of referral 20/27 (74%)
audits.c: Staff education on BOAST guidance for doctors and trauma coordinators at the morbidity and mortality meeting (PDSA 1), then repeat education and changing the trauma list spreadsheet dropdown to separate intra-articular and extra-articular distal radius fractures (PDSA 2)
audits.r2: Intra-articular within 3 days of injury 24/32 (75%) (p=0.2665; p trend=0.1924); extra-articular within 7 days of injury 13/19 (68%) (p=0.0119; p trend=0.0243); intra-articular within 3 days of referral 28/32 (88%)

audits.t: Early Weight-Bearing Following Ankle Fixation in a United Kingdom Major Trauma Centre: Real-World Adoption Versus a Contemporary Randomised Trial and British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma.
audits.st: BOAST ankle fracture guidance (weight-bearing as tolerated after stable fixation) and WAX trial (weight-bearing from two weeks)
audits.f: First weight-bearing at 2 weeks 2/42 (4.8%), 2–6 weeks 9/42 (21.4%), over 6 weeks 31/42 (73.8%) (6–8 weeks 21/42, 50.0%; over 8 weeks 10/42, 23.8%). Median 48 days (IQR 42–56); none discharged weight-bearing as tolerated.

audits.t: International Normalized Ratio (INR) Sample Rejection in Neck of Femur Fracture Patients: A Retrospective Closed-Loop Study From a Major UK Trauma Centre.
audits.st: Correct filling of 3.2% sodium citrate tubes to maintain 9:1 blood-to-anticoagulant ratio, with discard tube first when using butterfly sets; no numerical target stated
audits.f: 66/399 INR samples rejected (16.5%, 95% CI 13.2-20.5%); 62 (94%) for underfilling and 4 (6%) for haemolysis.
audits.c: Education sessions for junior doctors, phlebotomists and nurses on discard-tube use with butterfly sets, routine stocking of short-tubing collection devices, and visual reminder prompts at sampling points.
audits.r2: 29/261 rejected (11.1%, 95% CI 7.8-15.5%); absolute reduction 5.4 percentage points, relative ~33%, not significant (p ≈ 0.11); 27 (93%) underfilling, 2 (7%) haemolysis.

audits.t: Assessing the quality of orthopaedic operation notes: an audit cycle.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England operation note guidelines (19 parameters)
audits.f: 64 notes (45 (70%) typewritten); 64 (100%) compliant for surgeon name, operative procedure, diagnosis and post-op instructions.
audits.c: Findings presented in ward meetings with surgeons and educational workshops arranged.
audits.r2: Average improvement of 40 (31.1%), with 17 of 19 categories improving.

audits.t: Audit of Shoulder Dystocia Management and Outcomes at a Busy Hospital in the United Kingdom: A Comprehensive Analysis of Contemporary Practice.
audits.st: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 42 (shoulder dystocia)
audits.f: Incidence 1.32% (56/4,247 vaginal deliveries). Emergency response activated in 98.2% (mean response 2.3 minutes); McRoberts plus suprapubic pressure first line in 80.4%; internal manoeuvres in 37.5%; mean head-to-body delivery after recognition 4.7 minutes. Maternal complications 53.6%, PPH 7.1%; neonatal complications 83.9%, resuscitation 26.8%, NICU 3.6%, no permanent brachial plexus injury.

audits.t: System-Level Barriers to National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guideline Compliance in Distal Radius Fracture Management: A Retrospective Audit Study.
audits.tp: Distal radius fracture time to surgery
audits.st: NICE fractures guidance: manipulation for dorsally displaced distal radius fractures (1.4.5); surgery within 72 hours for intra-articular and within 7 days for extra-articular fractures (1.4.3)
audits.f: 90% (27/30) underwent manipulation and plaster in the ED; 3 (10%) went straight to surgery, 2 (6.7%) without a documented reason.
audits.c: Email to all T&O registrars about NICE guidance, dedicated teaching sessions, and an internal management pathway for distal radius fractures.
audits.r2: Overall surgical timing compliance 11.6% (5/43): 10% (4/40) of intra-articular fractures within 72 hours (mean 8.6 days) and 33.3% (1/3) of extra-articular fractures within 7 days (mean 6.3 days).

audits.t: Compliance With Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Hip Arthroplasty Following Neck of Femur Fractures: A Retrospective Clinical Audit Study.
audits.st: Trust guideline: three postoperative IV doses of flucloxacillin (teicoplanin if penicillin allergic) after hip arthroplasty for NOF fracture; target 100%
audits.f: Postoperative antibiotics given to 150/179 (83.8%), none to 29 (16.2%); 84/121 (69.4%) flucloxacillin recipients completed all three doses; 97/179 (54.2%) fully compliant overall.

audits.t: Improving adherence to appropriate use criteria for paediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: a three-cycle quality improvement project.
audits.st: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS) appropriate use criteria (AUC) for paediatric supracondylar humerus fractures; primary outcome proportion of cases managed 'appropriately'
audits.f: 62.1% (36/58) managed 'appropriately'; 19.0% (11/58) 'rarely appropriate'; 19.0% (11/58) 'may be appropriate'. 65% of type IIa fractures were managed with casting alone ('rarely appropriate').
audits.c: Cycle 2: mandatory 2-hour AUC workshop, pocket reference cards and a departmental protocol with a type II fracture flowchart. Cycle 3: three refresher workshops, AUC training in resident orientation, laminated AUC flowcharts in ED, theatre and ward, departmental grand round presentations, weekly case discussions and individualised audit feedback.
audits.r2: 87.9% (51/58) managed 'appropriately' (25.8% absolute improvement from baseline); 'rarely appropriate' 3.4% (2/58); 'may be appropriate' 8.6% (5/58). AUC tool use documented in over 95% of cases.

audits.t: Auditing the Early Management of Suspected Scaphoid Fractures in Comparison With the National Agreed Standard: A Retrospective Study.
audits.st: BSSH Scaphoid Standards: review in a specialist fracture clinic within 7 days of presentation, and a dedicated four-view scaphoid radiograph series at initial assessment (target 100% for both)
audits.f: Fracture clinic review within 7 days in 68.5% (170/248); four-view scaphoid series in 95.2% (236/248). Scaphoid fracture confirmed in 44 (17.7%); false-negative rate of initial radiographs 22.7% (10/44), false-positive rate 5.2% (13/248).

audits.t: Improving Perioperative Tranexamic Acid Administration in Hip Fracture Surgery: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project at Dorset County Hospital.
audits.st: NICE guideline: offer TXA to adults having surgery expected to cause moderate blood loss (>500 ml)
audits.f: 26/37 (70.0%) eligible patients received intraoperative TXA; contraindication documented in 0%
audits.c: Local hip fracture protocol updated to include TXA, targeted teaching for anaesthetic and theatre staff, and encouragement to record contraindications
audits.r2: 23/27 (85.2%) received TXA; contraindication documented in 7.4%; difference not significant (Fisher's exact p = 0.23, OR 0.41)

audits.t: Improving the Quality of Lateral Wrist Radiographs: A Closed-Loop Audit of Radiographic Compliance With Standard Positioning Criteria.
audits.st: Clark's Positioning in Radiography criteria for lateral wrist radiographs (styloid superimposition, anatomical inclusion, piso-scapho-capitate relationship); target 80% for each
audits.f: Styloid superimposition 72% (36/50); anatomical inclusion 98% (49/50); piso-scapho-capitate relationship 50% (25/50).
audits.c: Poster on positioning technique in the radiology department and trauma meeting rooms, and a formal teaching session by an associate specialist hand surgeon for radiographers and orthopaedic doctors.
audits.r2: Styloid superimposition 92% (46/50) (p = 0.047); anatomical inclusion 100% (50/50) (p = 0.992); piso-scapho-capitate relationship 82% (41/50) (p = 0.014).

audits.t: Enhancing Perioperative Oral Nutritional Supplements in Elderly Hip Fracture Patients: A Pilot Project on Evidence-Based Practice.
audits.st: 10 JBI-style review indicators derived from best evidence on perioperative oral nutritional supplements (ONS) in elderly hip fracture, e.g. staff ONS training (pass ≥80 points), NRS2002 screening within 24 h of admission, 24 h after surgery and before discharge, energy 25–30 kcal/(kg·d) and protein 1.0–1.5 g/kg, ONS 400–600 mL/d after surgery, post-discharge ONS 400 kcal and 30 g protein daily
audits.f: Compliance 0–10.7% across the 10 review indicators: staff training 10.7% (3/28); patient/caregiver education, screening, energy/protein targets, ONS use, disease-specific ONS, stopping rule, GI monitoring and discharge follow-up all 0%. Staff knowledge score 61.07±12.36.
audits.c: Nurse-led multidisciplinary team with nutrition support nurses; daily 20-minute staff training over five days; updated NRS2002 form in the nursing IT system with fixed screening time points and automated reminders; 24-hour dietary energy and protein record sheet; dietary lists, leaflets, education manuals, QR codes, videos and teach-back; ward ONS supply protocol; discharge follow-up manual and smart cloud follow-up platform.
audits.r2: Compliance 25–100% (all P < 0.05): 100% for indicators 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9; staff training 82.1% (23/28); ONS twice daily after surgery 56.8% (25/44); post-discharge ONS 25.0% (11/44). Staff knowledge score 85.57±16.89 (t = 6.195, P < 0.001).

audits.t: Improving Patient Care and Clinical Services: Compliance With the British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) Guidelines for Neurological and Vascular Assessment of Acute Fractures.
audits.tp: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
audits.st: BOAST Peripheral Nerve Injury guideline (December 2021): documentation of specific nerve and arterial status; target 100%
audits.f: Any NV documentation 43/49 (87.8%); detailed neurological findings 19/49 (38.8%); detailed vascular findings 13/49 (26.5%).
audits.c: Single educational awareness presentation on the consequences of poor NV assessment (May 2024).
audits.r2: Any NV documentation 47/48 (97.9%) (p = 0.053); detailed neurological findings 26/48 (54.2%) (p = 0.129); detailed vascular findings 22/48 (45.8%) (p = 0.048).

audits.t: Improving Discharge Summary Follow-Up Documentation in a Major Trauma Center: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians Health Informatics Unit 2019 discharge summary content standards
audits.f: Follow-up plan fully detailed 15.6% (5/32); new medication indication documented 9.4% (3/32); patient advice fully detailed 21.2% (7/33); inpatient management fully detailed 30.3% (10/33).
audits.c: Educational poster with a checklist of RCP components, interactive teaching sessions, a discharge summary self-assessment checklist, reminders with one-to-one feedback for junior doctors and a team campaign (August to September 2025).
audits.r2: Follow-up plan fully detailed 90.0% (18/20) (p < 0.0001); new medication indication 50.0% (9/18) (p = 0.004); patient advice fully detailed 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.0002); inpatient management fully detailed 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.001).

audits.t: Mobilisation After Total Knee Replacement Within an Enhanced Recovery Pathway: A Two-Cycle Clinical Audit.
audits.st: Mobilisation within 24 hours after surgery, in keeping with ERAS principles and local pathway expectations
audits.f: 35/53 (66.0%) mobilised within 24 hours; median length of stay 2 days.
audits.c: MAKE1 findings presented to the multidisciplinary team; reinforcement of enhanced recovery practices, better documentation of reasons for delayed mobilisation and prompt management/escalation of pain, nausea and hypotension.
audits.r2: 57/63 (90.5%) mobilised within 24 hours; median length of stay 2 days.

audits.t: Use of Pre-operative Echocardiograms in Traumatic Neck of Femur Fracture Patients: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Local trust guideline: no surgical delay awaiting echo; TTE only for listed indications; all TTE reports acknowledged by the anaesthetist; target 100%
audits.f: No surgical delay 12/12 (100%); appropriate requests 4/12 (33.3%); reports acknowledged by anaesthetist 10/12 (83.3%).
audits.c: Teaching sessions, posters of request criteria, dissemination of audit findings, reminders at safety meetings and printed prompt cards.
audits.r2: No surgical delay 17/17 (100%); appropriate requests 16/17 (94.1%); reports acknowledged 12/17 (70.6%).

audits.t: The Paediatric ACL National Audit (PANA) study: a multicentre review of UK practice and adherence to BOAST guidelines.
audits.st: BOAST guideline for paediatric ACL injuries (2022)
audits.f: 65% of centres use acute knee pathways; 68% collaborative imaging pathways; 59% radiological growth monitoring; 30% report functional outcomes; <50% report re-rupture rates; 74% adhere to rehabilitation protocols

audits.t: Improving the Completeness of Orthopaedic Operation Notes Through a Two-Cycle Clinical Audit at Prince Osman Digna Referral Hospital.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice: 18 core operation note criteria
audits.f: Anticipated blood loss, antibiotic prophylaxis and DVT prophylaxis each 0/50 (0%); operative findings 17/50 (34%); tissue removed/altered 16/50 (32%); surgical approach 20/50 (40%); surgeon name 49/50 (98%).
audits.c: Presentation of findings at a governance meeting, distribution and discussion of RCS operation note standards, and senior-led feedback and reinforcement in theatre.
audits.r2: Anticipated blood loss 10/35 (28.6%); antibiotic prophylaxis 7/35 (20%); DVT prophylaxis 5/35 (14.3%); operative findings 26/35 (74.3%); tissue altered 25/35 (71.4%); surgical approach 28/35 (80%); surgeon name 35/35 (100%).

audits.t: Achieving effective and timely quality of care in same-day discharge total hip arthroplasty without compromising patient safety.
audits.st: Aim of >80% successful same-day discharge among eligible primary THA patients without compromising safety (unscheduled 30-day hospital encounters)
audits.f: Standard cohort: 57/105 (54.3%) discharged same day; complications preventing same-day discharge 48 (45.7%); unscheduled 30-day hospital encounters 11 (10.5%).
audits.c: Enhanced Recovery Canada recommendations: pre-emptive nausea prophylaxis (aprepitant, scopolamine patch), pre-emptive multimodal oral analgesia, and lidocaine epidural anaesthesia via a 'STAR Module' in the electronic order set, supported by STAR rounds, website posts and a video; then a switch to spinal lidocaine.
audits.r2: Spinal lidocaine cohort: 80.6% discharged same day vs 54.3% (OR 3.4, 95% CI 1.34 to 8.66, p=0.0102).

audits.t: Improving GIRFT compliance and patient experience of accessibility and shared decision making for elective hip and knee replacement: incorporation of a digital patient information leaflet.
audits.tp: Shared decision making and patient information documentation for joint replacement
audits.st: NICE NG157 and GIRFT Elective Hip and Knee Pathway: documentation of patient information leaflet provision and shared decision making domains (no numerical target stated)
audits.f: PIL offered documented in 7% (hip) and 9% (knee); consent form copy given 30% (hip) and 50% (knee); understanding and willingness to proceed 79% (hip) and 73% (knee); recovery expectations, spinal anaesthetic and wound care ≤9%.
audits.c: QR code-linked digital patient information leaflet (procedure, recovery, anaesthetic options, wound care, translation links) given at the end of clinic; staff encouraged to offer it and document its provision.
audits.r2: PIL offered documented in 24% (hip) and 36% (knee); understanding and willingness to proceed 90% (hip) and 100% (knee); recovery expectations, spinal anaesthetic and wound care up to 36%; consent form copy 28% (hip) and 50% (knee).

audits.t: Fracture risk assessment in patients prescribed pre-exposure prophylaxis for HIV: An audit and comparative evaluation of screening tools.
audits.tp: Fracture risk assessment in PrEP users
audits.st: UK guidelines: fracture risk assessment for PrEP users aged over 50 (FRAX or QFracture)
audits.f: Fracture risk assessment completed for 156/220 (71%); DEXA requested where indicated in 6/15 (40%).

audits.t: De-implementation of movement precautions after total hip replacement in a German university hospital: a best practice implementation project.
audits.tp: Hip precautions after total hip replacement
audits.st: JBI best practice recommendation: no routine hip movement precautions after THR
audits.f: Compliance 16.67%.
audits.c: Two implementation workshops with evidence-based presentations and group discussions.

audits.t: WaSTE: a multicentre audit of waste segregation practices in elective knee and hip arthroplasty.
audits.st: National waste management guidance: infectious (orange) stream only for suspected infectious agents, otherwise offensive (tiger-stripe) and general streams; no numerical target stated
audits.f: 92 THAs and 130 TKAs; mean total waste 14.79 kg per THA and 13.61 kg per TKA; infectious waste the largest category (9.88 kg THA, 8.68 kg TKA). Only 5/10 trusts used an offensive waste stream and 8/10 used recycling; significant inter-hospital variation in all waste categories (p < 0.001).

audits.t: The Children's Urgent Reduction of Forearm Fractures in the Emergency Department (CURFFED) project : a national prospective trainee-led collaborative audit of practice.
audits.tp: Paediatric buckle and forearm fracture management
audits.st: BOAST Early Management of the Paediatric Forearm Fracture (2021)
audits.f: Mean overall BOAST compliance 63% (42.5% to 86.9%). Pain scores 83 (20%); regular analgesia 372 (87%); complete pre-manipulation NV assessment 214 (50%), post-manipulation 147 (35%); consent 163 (38%); analgesia and advice on discharge complete 95 (23%); consultant review within 48 h 328 (78%); clinic within 7 days 238 (59%). 423/577 (73%) manipulated first in ED.

audits.t: Closing the loop on tourniquet safety in distal radius fracture fixation surgery: a two-cycle quality improvement project.
audits.st: BOAST 'The Safe Use of Intraoperative Tourniquets' (2021): documentation of seven parameters (time, skin condition, padding, site, compressive exsanguination, pressure, size)
audits.f: Tourniquet pressure 20.5% (7/34), time 55.9% (19/34); site, padding, exsanguination, skin condition and size all 0%.
audits.c: Teaching session for junior doctors and theatre staff, a three-part tourniquet safety checklist in theatres, and BOAST posters in theatre preparation areas.
audits.r2: Pressure 59.0% (37/63), site 32.0% (20), padding 14.0% (9), exsanguination 13.0% (8), skin condition 11.0% (7), size 10.0% (6), time 56.0% (35).

audits.t: Overuse of knee ultrasound in acute knee injury pathways in primary care: a quality improvement report.
audits.tp: Ottawa rules and radiograph request appropriateness
audits.st: ACC imaging guidelines for knee ultrasound
audits.f: 9.8% had knee ultrasound before specialist review; only one scan met ACC criteria; 80% requested by physiotherapists (P = 0.015).

audits.t: Reducing unwarranted variation in medication reviews following a fall: a closed-loop audit in primary care.
audits.st: NICE CG161/NG5 and NHS England guidance: documented medication review within 4 weeks after a fall; target 100%
audits.f: 22% (14/63) documented review within 4 weeks.
audits.c: Clinician education on NICE guidance, SystmOne prompts and weekly MDT fall reviews.

audits.t: Electronic patient blood management monitoring using routine health record data: A proof-of-principle study monitoring perioperative tranexamic acid use.
audits.st: NICE Quality Standard QS138 statement 2 (pre-2026 definition): adults having surgery with expected blood loss >500 mL should receive perioperative tranexamic acid
audits.f: Overall automated TXA compliance 78.7%.
audits.r2: Overall automated TXA compliance 86.3% (manual QI audit same period 90%, 10 cases); trauma and orthopaedics 98.2% (n = 393), cardiac surgery 83.7%, gynaecology 83.2%, urology 94.2%, colorectal 43.5%, vascular 0%. Improvement from 2024 included gynaecology +26.8% and cardiac surgery +15.6%.

audits.t: Cross-Matching in Spinal Surgery - An Audit of Compliance at the National Spinal Injuries Unit (NSIU).
audits.tp: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
audits.st: Maximum Surgical Blood Order Schedule (MSBOS)
audits.f: MSBOS compliance 33/63 (52%); over-crossmatching 27/63 (43%).
audits.c: Revised spine-specific departmental transfusion guideline aligned with MSBOS.

audits.t: International benchmarking of secondary fracture prevention in older adults with hip fracture: a Chinese hospital-based KPI audit.

audits.t: 158 AN AUDIT ON DISCHARGE SUMMARIES IN A MEDICAL GERONTOLOGICAL WARD

audits.st: Secondary care letters state indication and duration of DAPT; stop date on prescription; DAPT for correct duration

audits.t: 259 AN AUDIT OF DNACPR FORM USAGE IN A LEVEL 4 HOSPITAL FOLLOWING RE-DESIGN AND IMPLICATIONS FOR ITS FUTURE USE

audits.t: 1255 IMPROVING COMMUNICATION BETWEEN NEXT OF KIN AND MEDICAL STAFF FOR OUR MOST VULNERABLE PATIENTS: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

audits.t: 1581 POSTURAL HYPOTENSION – A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
