audits.t: 81 Audit of Use of Oakland Score on Patients Presenting with PR Bleeding and Effect on Admissions with Retrospective Application
audits.tp: Lower GI bleeding risk stratification (Oakland score)
audits.st: Validated Oakland Score for safe discharge of patients presenting with PR bleeding (discharge thresholds of 8 and 10 tested)
audits.f: 0/72 patients had an Oakland Score on initial clerking. On retrospective application, 41/75 (55%) (threshold 8) and 42/75 (56%) (threshold 10) were admitted or discharged correctly.

audits.t: 139 “Never Event, Never Again” - a Closed Loop Audit on the Documentation of Nasogastric Tube Position Following X-Ray Confirmation
audits.st: Documentation of nasogastric tube position after X-ray confirmation using the NGT documentation sticker (Never Event prevention)
audits.f: Sticker used 42.1%; patient identity verified 39.5%; most recent X-ray confirmed 44.7%; time and date verified 34.2%; NGT position documented 63.1%; feeding instructions 65.8%; confirming staff recorded 60.5%.
audits.c: Teaching doctors to use the sticker supplied with each NGT pack, ward posters, and reminding nurses to check documentation before feeding.
audits.r2: Sticker used 85%; identity verified 100%; most recent X-ray 100%; time and date 85%; position documented 75%; feeding instructions 75%; confirming staff 75%.

audits.t: 216 Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsies for Malignant Melanoma – a Single Centre, Closed-Loop Audit
audits.tp: Sentinel lymph node biopsy in melanoma
audits.st: UK consensus statement: SLNB for primary cutaneous melanoma ≥pT2a, or pT1b with lymphovascular invasion or mitotic rate ≥2/mm2
audits.f: 6.5% (n = 9) did not meet criteria; a further 4.3% (n = 6) lacked documented lymphovascular invasion or mitotic index.
audits.c: Standard referral letters disseminated to referring sites, with instruction to include full histology reports.
audits.r2: 3% (n = 3) did not meet criteria; a further 11% (n = 11) lacked documented lymphovascular invasion or mitotic index in the referral.

audits.t: 286 Two-Cycle Audit on Post-Tonsillectomy Analgesia
audits.st: National standards; new ibuprofen guidance 7.5mg/kg QDS
audits.f: 95% prescribed inadequate ibuprofen (mean 5.5mg/kg); 6% presented with bleeding, none returned to theatre.
audits.c: New ibuprofen prescribing guideline (7.5mg/kg QDS instead of 5mg/kg TDS) with reduced opioid prescribing.
audits.r2: 55% prescribed correct 7.5mg/kg QDS; no readmissions for pain; low number of bleeds.

audits.t: 331 Improving Equity of Access in a Post-Covid World: A Closed Loop Audit of the Varicose Vein (VV) Referral to Treatment (RTT) Pathway
audits.st: Local CCG varicose vein referral criteria (April 2021)
audits.f: 158 (63.2%) failed criteria but actual rejection rate was 44.9%, with significant variation between consultants (P<0.001); 62.9% of ineligible patients seen had investigations.
audits.c: Results presented at clinical governance on 09/03/22 and change implemented.
audits.r2: 96 (63.7%) failed criteria; 15.5% improvement in appropriate outright rejection (p = 0.02); no significant difference between consultants (P = 0.46).

audits.t: 369 Should We Be Group and Save Testing for Laparoscopic General Surgical Procedures? a Retrospective Audit of Transfusion Rates at a District General Hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 2 patients (0.11%) received transfusion within 72 hours of laparoscopic procedures.
audits.c: Local trust policy changed to reduce or eliminate group and save for most elective and emergency laparoscopic procedures.

audits.t: 397 The Effects of a Virtual Specialist Nurse-Led Clinic on Plastics Outpatient Services at a Major Trauma Centre: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 95% of consultant clinics over capacity; 54 forced bookings.
audits.c: Virtual specialist nurse-led clinic replacing suitable face-to-face follow-ups
audits.r2: 71.8% of consultant clinics over capacity (p=0.002); 10 forced bookings (p=0.006); new patients seen per month up 15.3% (p=0.019).

audits.t: 459 Standardised Surgical Admission Proformas: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons (England) documentation guidelines
audits.f: Vital signs documented in less than 46%, medications 43%, allergies 72%; smoking and alcohol under 40%.
audits.c: Standardised structured surgical admission proforma replacing freehand notes.
audits.r2: 100% proforma uptake; vital signs documentation improved by a mean 60.0%; medications +46.9%, alcohol +43.1%, smoking +40.6%, laboratory results +17.5%; 96.1% had identifiable registration numbers.

audits.t: 472 An Audit on the Optimal Timing of Imaging in Acute Pancreatitis
audits.st: IAP/APA and BSG guidance: diagnosis within 48 hours, ultrasound within 24 hours of diagnosis, CT at 72-96 hours after onset or after 48 hours of admission
audits.f: Correct diagnosis within 48 hours 90%; CT after 48 hours of admission 6.15%; CT within 72-96 hours of onset 29.23%; ultrasound within 24 hours 17%; CT initial imaging in 75%.

audits.t: 474 Audit of ENT Department Handover Practice: An Improved Patient Safety Outcome
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England Guidance on Safe Handover (2007)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: RCS England guidance distributed, regular feedback to junior doctors and emphasis on handover at clinical governance and induction sessions.
audits.r2: Morning handover complete on 70% of days, incomplete 30%, absent 0%; evening handover complete 75%, incomplete 25%, absent 0%.

audits.t: 481 An Audit on the Completion of Hand Trauma Proformas – a Tertiary Centre Experience
audits.st: BSSH guidelines; RCS England Safe Handover minimum data
audits.f: X-ray obtained in 80%; hospital of X-ray documented in 40%; X-ray findings documented in 60%.
audits.c: Access to a generic doctors' account for external PACS as a temporary measure; re-audit planned in 6 months

audits.t: 493 Audit of Antibiotic Prescriptions in Appendicectomies and Adherence of Surgeons to National and Local Trust Guidelines: Preoperative and Postoperative
audits.st: BMJ Best Practice (preoperative prophylaxis for all; postoperative antibiotics only for complicated cases) and local trust MicroGuide guidelines
audits.f: 100% received prophylaxis but only 25% of penicillin-allergic and 2.2% of non-allergic patients received trust-adherent agents; 100% of complicated cases had postoperative antibiotics while 80% of uncomplicated cases had them unnecessarily.

audits.t: 568 Audit of Laceration Management and Documentation
audits.st: NICE guidelines on laceration management
audits.f: Laceration size documented 49%; infection risk 9%; wound cleaning 72%; appropriate closure 77%; dressing type 19%; tetanus appropriately managed 59%; detailed wound care instructions 36%; 6% given antibiotics despite closed wound.
audits.c: Planned: laceration clerking template with compulsory elements, with re-audit in February.

audits.t: 596 A Local Audit Assessing Completeness of Morbidity and Mortality Records in Vascular Surgery in a Tertiary Centre in the UK
audits.st: Good Surgical Practice and Royal College of Surgeons advice that formal records of M&M discussions are kept
audits.f: No record included the hospital number; 20.6% had all five sections complete; 'when' completed in 29.4% and 'attending consultants' in 41.2%; 29.4% had no record of discussion; 35.2% no action plan; 47.0% no responsible person.

audits.t: 612 Consultant Review in the Emergency General Surgical Take: A Single-Centre Audit for Compliance to Royal College of Surgeon’s Guidelines
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England timeframes for consultant review
audits.f: 70% reviewed within recommended time; 10% missing documentation; 20% seen 1 to 2 hours outside the window.
audits.c: Educational sessions and email reminders on documentation
audits.r2: 80% reviewed within recommended time; 5% missing documentation.

audits.t: 634 Analgesia Use in Acute Renal Colic Patients- Complete Audit Cycle
audits.st: NICE NG118: NSAIDs first-line analgesia for renal colic, then IV paracetamol and opiates
audits.f: 60% compliance.
audits.c: Findings presented at departmental meetings and posters of the analgesic pathway in clinical areas.

audits.t: 639 An Audit to Evaluate the Prevalence and Efficiency of the ‘Acute Abdomen Pathway’ Proforma Used in a Large District General Hospital
audits.st: Use of the acute abdomen pathway proforma for patients meeting its criteria
audits.f: Only 4 of 112 eligible patients were started on the pathway; with the proforma, CT request to report 5 hours (from 14), triage to diagnosis 5 hours (from 12), triage to management 5 hours (from 13).
audits.c: Planned: raise awareness of the pathway and re-audit.

audits.t: 640 Ambulatory Ultrasound - Could We Be More Efficient? Re-Audit -a District General Hospital Experience
audits.st: National guidelines on ultrasound in selected patients with RIF pain
audits.f: 41% had working diagnosis matching USS request; 13% had working diagnosis matched with USS results.
audits.r2: 94 (86%) had working diagnosis matching USS request; 22 (20%) had working diagnosis matched with USS results.

audits.t: 683 Closed Loop Regional Audits on Quality Predictive Indicators for Renal Cell Carcinoma Management in Northern Ireland
audits.st: Ten NHS Scotland National Cancer Quality Steering Group QPIs for renal cell carcinoma
audits.f: Targets met in 3 of 10 QPIs (nephron sparing surgery, trifecta rate, 30/90-day mortality).
audits.r2: Targets met in 7 of 10 QPIs (additionally pre-treatment CT/MRI, histodiagnosis in cryotherapy and chemotherapy, MDT discussion).

audits.t: 690 Quality Improvement Project: Improving Engagement with Smoking Cessation Services Among Emergency Surgical Admissions
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Smoking status documented 83% (n=166); proforma completed 55% (n=112); among 49 smokers NRT prescribed 29%, CURE involvement 31%; 10% accepted ongoing support.
audits.c: Structured teaching session on smoking cessation for incoming doctors (August 2022)
audits.r2: Smoking status documented 96% (n=157); proforma completed 91% (n=148); among 47 smokers NRT 40%, CURE involvement 64%; 21% accepted ongoing support.

audits.t: 691 Gallbladder Polyp Surveillance Audit
audits.st: ESGAR/EASES/EFISDS/ESGE joint guidelines (6, 12 and 24 monthly scans for 6-9mm polyps; cholecystectomy >10mm); local trust guideline of 12 and 24 monthly scans
audits.f: Of 82 (36.6%) 6-9mm polyps, 62 (75%) followed up; mean time to second scan 472 days, median 556 days; timing not within recommended guidelines.

audits.t: 699 Audit of Post-Splenectomy Patients in Primary Care
audits.st: National immunisation and antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines for post-splenectomy patients
audits.f: Three patients had outstanding pneumococcal vaccine in the past five years; 100% compliance with annual influenza vaccine; two patients on incorrect antibiotic prophylaxis and four without antibiotic prophylaxis.

audits.t: 722 Audit on Improving the Management of Pre-Operative Medication Prior to Elective Surgery
audits.st: Correct prescribing and management of regular medications before elective surgery
audits.f: 19/50 (38%) received medications correctly.
audits.c: Posters in elective surgical wards (first cycle) and local departmental teaching (second cycle).

audits.t: 730 An Audit of Antibiotic Prescription in Acute Pancreatitis
audits.st: NICE NG104 on acute pancreatitis
audits.f: 65.5% prescribed antibiotics on admission; 12.1% for necrosis, 12.14% for concurrent cholecystitis, 33.4% without indication.
audits.c: Results and NICE guidance disseminated to general surgery team and at governance meeting.

audits.t: 733 ERAS Audit: Junior Doctor Compliance with the Elective Colorectal Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) Pathway at Bristol Royal Infirmary
audits.st: Elective colorectal ERAS pathway: early postoperative nutritional drinks and avoidance of postoperative opioids
audits.f: Early postoperative nutrition and/or solid food in 60 (68.2%); nutritional drinks prescribed for 39 (44.3%), average 3 days to prescribe; systemic opioids avoided in 7 (7.9%).
audits.c: Face-to-face education for new colorectal junior doctors and posters in the doctors' office.

audits.t: 804 Audit of Hand-Written Consent Form Documentation for Skin Lesion Excisions in the Plastic Surgery Procedure Room
audits.st: Local consensus of the consultant body on consenter details, form completion and documented risks (no standard guidelines)
audits.f: All consenters documented job title, signed and dated; 100% used correct form, documented procedure, site and risks and labelled every page; intended benefits 83%; procedure name in full 58%; risks documented: bleeding and infection 100%, pain 54%, re-excision 75%, recurrence and wound breakdown 71%, scarring 96%, injury to surrounding structures 46%, anaesthetic risk 0%.

audits.t: 861 Getting the Surgical Handover Right: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons twelve-point handover guideline
audits.f: Highlighting need for additional review 33.3%; handover of outstanding tasks 31.5%; resuscitation status 7.0%.
audits.r2: Highlighting need for additional review 91.0%; outstanding tasks 84.3%; resuscitation status 9.2%.

audits.t: 900 Assessing the Use of GIRFT Guidelines and the Role of a Natural Language Processing Artificial Intelligence System for Operation Note Documentation in Emergency General Surgery – a Closed Loop Prospective Audit & Comparative Study
audits.st: GIRFT procedure-specific operation note guidelines
audits.f: Five consecutive operation notes each for laparoscopic appendicectomy, laparoscopic cholecystectomy, open inguinal hernia and emergency laparotomy/small bowel resection scored against GIRFT.
audits.c: All surgeons educated on the four GIRFT guidelines.
audits.r2: Median scores improved by +12.3% (p = 0.033) LA, +0.6% (p = 0.500) LC, +25.5% (p = 0.006) IH, +9.5% (p = 0.030) ELS; best was LA in cycle 2, median 72.7% (IQR 8.5).

audits.t: 906 A Prospective Clinical Audit of Pre-Operative Fasting Practices at a Tertiary Care Hospital in India
audits.st: Indian Society of Anaesthesiologists national preoperative fasting guidelines
audits.f: Median fasting 10 hours from clear fluids and 12.5 hours from solids; 99% gave an incorrect reason or did not know the reason for fasting.
audits.c: Patient information leaflets in English and the local language distributed to every ward for patients the day before surgery; surgical and anaesthetic trainees and nurses made aware of the findings.
audits.r2: Median fasting 3 hours from clear fluids and 11 hours from solids; 35% knew the correct reason, 50% gave an incorrect reason, 15% did not know.

audits.t: 946 A Complete Cycle Audit of the Appropriate Management of Stable Patients Presenting Acutely with a Lower GI Bleed Using the Oakland Score Risk Stratification Tool in Order to Avoid Unnecessary Admissions
audits.tp: Lower GI bleeding risk stratification (Oakland score)
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology guidance on Oakland score risk stratification (safe discharge threshold ≤8)
audits.f: 6/63 (10%) had a documented Oakland score; three patients with OS <8 were inappropriately admitted.
audits.c: Tailored teaching with a summary sheet and link to an e-calculator, after a departmental survey.
audits.r2: 16/38 (42%) had a documented Oakland score; all 8/8 with OS ≤8 appropriately discharged.

audits.t: 987 Audit of Prophylactic Antibiotic Prescriptions in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery and Adherence of Surgeons to Local Trust Guidelines
audits.st: Local trust prophylactic antibiotic guidelines (MicroGuide)
audits.f: 100% given prophylactic antibiotics; compliance 100% for uncomplex dentoalveolar/salivary surgery, 20% for fractured mandible and 0% for all other categories.

audits.t: 1033 Renal Colic Emergency Management - an Audit Cycle
audits.st: BAUS and NICE renal colic recommendations: CT within 14 hours, NSAIDs, referral criteria
audits.f: NSAIDs prescribed 87%; CT within 14 hours 93%; 100% meeting referral criteria referred; 67% not meeting referral criteria referred.
audits.c: Updated NSAID dosing and updated health board renal colic pathway.
audits.r2: NSAIDs prescribed 50%; CT within 14 hours 100%; 50% not meeting referral criteria referred.

audits.t: 1039 Preventing Avoidable Harm with Safe IV Fluid Therapy – a Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: NICE CG174 intravenous fluid therapy
audits.f: Regular hydration assessment 10%; appropriate resuscitation fluid 32%; maintenance fluid when indicated 52%; correct maintenance composition 0%.
audits.c: Findings presented at a local meeting, posters and regular teaching on safe IV fluid prescribing.
audits.r2: Regular hydration assessment 28%; appropriate resuscitation 66%; maintenance fluid when indicated 84%; correct composition 15%.

audits.t: 1041 Audit of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) Protocol in Elective Colorectal Surgery (A Loop Audit)
audits.st: ERAS guidelines for elective colorectal surgery
audits.f: Overall adherence 63.9% (pre-admission 59.2%, pre-operative 73.9%, intra-operative 70.1%, post-operative 52.7%); no ERAS anaesthetic component; mean LOS 9.8 days.
audits.r2: Overall adherence 81.1% (pre-admission 88%, pre-operative 80.25%, intra-operative 76.8%, post-operative 79.6%); all anaesthetic components included; mean LOS 7.1 days.

audits.t: 1083 Evaluating Adherence to Best Practice for Tissue Sampling in Diabetic Foot Surgery: A Quality-Improvement Study
audits.tp: Microbiology sampling in diabetic foot infection
audits.st: NICE guidelines on tissue sampling in diabetic foot surgery
audits.f: Clinically clean bone samples 68% (n=40); microbiology changed targeted antibiotics in 58% (n=33).
audits.c: Departmental teaching programme, then an online operation note proforma
audits.r2: Clinically clean bone samples 89% (n=24) (p=0.140); antibiotics changed in 95% (n=19).

audits.t: 1120 Time to Revascularisation for Chronic Limb Threatening Ischaemia – Audit of a Major UK Vascular Service
audits.tp: Time to revascularisation for chronic limb-threatening ischaemia
audits.st: VSGBI PAD-QIF 2019 and CQUIN 2022/23: revascularisation within 5 days of referral for inpatients and 14 days for outpatients
audits.f: 59 inpatients and 33 outpatients; 54% of inpatient and 83% of outpatient revascularisation candidates breached targets. Most inpatient breaches revascularised within 6-10 days; most outpatient breaches within 46-75 days.

audits.t: 1144 Audit of Microbiological Sampling in Patients with Diabetic Foot Infections Presenting to a Tertiary Vascular Centre in the North-East of England
audits.tp: Microbiology sampling in diabetic foot infection
audits.st: NICE NG19 and International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot guidance on microbiological sampling
audits.f: 56.8% (21/37) had microbiology sent; 47.6% (10/21) before antibiotics; tissue samples 35.1% (13/37).
audits.c: Introduction of a podiatrist-led 'Hot Foot Clinic'.
audits.r2: 74.2% (23/31) had microbiology sent; 23.5% (4/17) of tissue samples taken before antibiotics.

audits.t: 1162 Management of Acute Gallstone Disease at an Urban Acute Trust During the Pandemic – Closed-Loop Audit
audits.tp: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.st: National guidelines on early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.f: 49 patients had LC, only 20% performed acutely; 70% of acute operations were during re-admissions.
audits.c: Hot cholecystectomy list opened to other surgeons and acute LC encouraged on the emergency theatre list.
audits.r2: 21% underwent LC, of which 52% were acute operations; 50% of emergency operations were in re-admissions.

audits.t: 1237 Audit Project on Golden Patient Policy Adherence and Its Improvement to Theatre Efficiency
audits.st: Local trust Golden Patient criteria (ASA grade/anaesthetic type, case duration, team availability, sent for before 08:30)
audits.f: Baseline operation start times of first patients on list (figures not reported).
audits.c: Golden Patient policy: first patient on next day's list identified and reviewed the day before.
audits.r2: Start times improved by 30 minutes on average; 62.9% of Golden Patients met all criteria; 68.6% sent for before 08:30; 97.1% met ASA/anaesthetic and 94.3% case duration criteria.

audits.t: 1268 An Audit of the Time to Surgery Following Diagnosis of Gallstone Pancreatitis
audits.st: BSG guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy during index admission or within 2 weeks of discharge
audits.f: 14 (67%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy, 9 (64%) of these within 2 weeks; 7 (33%) had no surgery; median wait 3 days, average 64 days; 6 readmissions while waiting.
audits.c: Weekly semi-emergency theatre list introduced; re-audit planned.

audits.t: 1326 Temporal Artery Biopsy for Giant Cell Arteritis (GCA): A Ten-Year Retrospective Audit in an Irish Hospital
audits.tp: Temporal artery biopsy for giant cell arteritis
audits.st: American College of Rheumatology criteria for giant cell arteritis
audits.f: 107 (69%) met the guidelines; 27 (17.4%) biopsies positive for GCA.

audits.t: 620 Re-Operation Following Initial Breast Conservation Surgery for DCIS and Invasive Breast Cancer at ELHT Breast Unit, in 2021
audits.st: Association of Breast Surgery margin guidance; national re-excision rates of 13% (invasive) and 22% (DCIS)
audits.f: Re-excision rate 15.1% (31/205) for invasive disease and 33.3% (9/27) for DCIS.

audits.t: 589 Medication Prescribing for Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery with Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) and Review of Left Ventricular (LV) Function Documentation - A Departmental Audit
audits.st: 2016 ESC guidelines: ACEi/ARNI, beta-blocker and MRA prescribed, titrated or contraindication documented in HFrEF (LVEF 40% or less)
audits.f: Compliance ACEi/ARNI 67% (10/15), beta-blocker 80% (12/15), MRA 67% (10/15).

audits.t: 712 Improving Post-Op Length of Stay (PLOS) in First-Time Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG)- a Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: National average post-operative length of stay 7.9 days after first-time CABG
audits.f: Average post-operative length of stay 9.4 days.
audits.c: Encouraging early nurse-led mobilisation of post-operative patients.
audits.r2: Average post-operative length of stay 8.5 days.

audits.t: 1016 A Quality Improvement Project Addressing the Healthcare Dimension of Effectiveness in a Large Cardiothoracic Surgery Department by Ensuring the Contents of the Current Emergency Surgical Chest Drain Boxes Are Correctly Stocked Through Additional Rigorous Checks by June 2022, by Using the Model for Improvement Approach
audits.st: Complete stocking of emergency chest drain boxes (target date June 2022)
audits.f: Missing equipment prevalent in emergency chest drain boxes (baseline number of missing items not stated).
audits.c: Revised stock checklist produced with the project champion, thoracic audit lead and procedural document team, introduced over two PDSA cycles
audits.r2: 81% reduction in the 3-month average number of reported missing items; 92% increase in perceived confidence that the box will be correctly stocked.

audits.t: 455 Fine-Needle Aspiration, Ultrasound and Thyroidectomies in Patients with Thyroid Nodules Presenting to a District General Hospital – a Retrospective Audit
audits.st: RCPath Thy category malignancy risks and BAETS guideline for investigation of thyroid nodules
audits.f: 21% malignant; Thy1a/c malignancy 5% vs 4% nationally; 100% of Thy3–5 had diagnostic hemithyroidectomy; 84% compliance with repeat FNAC and 97% with MDT discussion; 15 lacked U classification.

audits.t: 943 An Audit of the Management of Necrotizing Otitis Externa Within Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital
audits.st: ENT UK advice (swabs and imaging in outpatient recognition)
audits.f: At admission 66% had a swab and 7% had imaging; IV antibiotics started within 24 hours in all; microbiology consulted within 6 days in 93%.

audits.t: 1208 Post-Tonsillectomy Re-Admissions – a Real Pain in the Mouth for Our Patients
audits.st: National Prospective Tonsillectomy Audit and ENT UK Tonsillectomy Commissioning standards: overall readmission <15%, pain readmission <1%, return to theatre <1%
audits.f: Overall readmissions 15.5%, pain readmissions 1.4% (n=1), return to theatre 2.8%; documentation of analgesia instruction and discharge medication 83%.
audits.c: Departmental education and dissemination of post-operative verbal/written patient education.
audits.r2: Overall readmissions 9.3%, pain readmissions 2.3% (n=1), return to theatre 0%; documentation of analgesia instruction and discharge medication 98%.

audits.t: 706 An Audit of Antibiotic Prescribing in Acute Pancreatitis and Introduction of a Patient Safety and Cost Saving Diagnostic Tool
audits.st: Antibiotics only for infected pancreatitis
audits.f: 19/52 (36.5%) with uncomplicated pancreatitis given antibiotics; 22/36 (61.1%) with infection received antibiotics; 36/41 (87.8%) given broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.

audits.t: 895 A Retrospective Analysis of National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) Data at a Tertiary Hospital
audits.st: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) national figures used as comparison
audits.f: Mean length of stay 33.59 vs 15.1 days nationally (median 15 days); geriatrician review 87% vs 24% nationally; 30-day mortality 5.5% vs 9.7% nationally
audits.c: Proposed only: special discussion of long-staying patients in weekly ward round meetings

audits.t: 905 To Operate or Not to Operate? a Clinical Audit in the Management of Adhesional Small Bowel Obstruction
audits.st: National audit of small bowel obstruction 2017 and Bologna guidelines
audits.f: IV fluids 100%; analgesia 38 (88.4%); anti-emetics 36 (83.7%); NG tube 21 (72.1%); 37% of conservatively managed patients received water-soluble contrast; average time to theatre 4 days (96 hours).

audits.t: 1068 Are There Delays to Emergency CEPOD Theatre Times? a Closed-Loop Audit Before and After Having a Dedicated CEPOD Registrar
audits.st: Hospital policy: first patient sent for by 08:40 AM and arrival by 09:00 AM
audits.f: Single on-call registrar: mean time sent for 09:33, arrival 10:00, turnover 00:39.
audits.c: Dedicated CEPOD registrar separate from the on-call registrar.
audits.r2: Dedicated CEPOD registrar: mean time sent for 09:08 (p=0.015), arrival 09:32 (p=0.010), turnover 00:11 (p=0.018).

audits.t: 1193 Review of Pre-Operative Antibiotic Prophylaxis (POAP) in National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) Patients in a Regional Acute Tertiary Hospital
audits.tp: Antibiotic prophylaxis timing in emergency laparotomy
audits.st: WHO: pre-operative antibiotic prophylaxis within 120 minutes before incision; SIGN: 30-60 minutes
audits.f: 83% had documented POAP; 68% of these had a recorded time before incision (mean 99 minutes, range 19 to 386); 77% of those received POAP within 120 minutes.

audits.t: 1202 National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA): Difficulties Achieving the Best Practice Tariff (BPT) Criteria
audits.st: NELA Best Practice Tariff: 80% of NELA high-risk patients have consultant surgeon and consultant anaesthetist present during surgery and are admitted directly to critical care
audits.f: 57% of high-risk cases met BPT criteria; consultant surgeon present 100%; consultant anaesthetist 63% (37% SAS-grade anaesthetist); 87% admitted to critical care.

audits.t: 871 Audit on Compliance and Documentation of GMC Guidelines Regarding the Use of Chaperone During the Intimate Examination
audits.st: GMC guidance on chaperones during intimate examination
audits.f: 9/168 (5.3%) had chaperone documentation, of which 1/9 (11%) complete; perianal examination 1/23 (4.3%); abdominal examination 8/141 (5.6%).
audits.c: Results shared with the department with education; chaperone stickers (name, position, gender) to be attached to notes.

audits.t: 102 An Audit of Phimosis Management at Primary Care Level
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons recommendations for phimosis management and paediatric surgical referral
audits.f: 25 (71.4%) referred; 32% of referrals (n = 8) without a topical steroid trial; 53.5% of steroids (n = 15) weaker than RCS recommends; 14 (73.7%) reviewed had physiological phimosis.

audits.t: 333 Inequity of Access to Investigations and Treatment of Varicose Veins by Clinician Grade: A Single Centre Retrospective Audit
audits.st: Norfolk and Waveney CCG referral to treatment criteria: only disease above C4 treated
audits.f: 71 referrals rejected and 158 should have been; of 70 seen in clinic 35 did not meet criteria; 62.9% (22) of ineligible attenders had investigations; discharge rate SpRs 13.3% vs consultants 45% (p=0.046).
audits.c: Education of SpRs on referral criteria recommended

audits.t: 347 General Surgery Ward Round Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Locally created 15-point ward round checklist
audits.f: Documented management plan 100% (other baseline figures not reported)
audits.r2: Improvement in 11 of 15 items: 3-point patient ID 100% (+43.7%), NEWS/observations +22.5%, medication review +26.7%, thromboprophylaxis +53.4%, examination +45.3%, escalation/DNACPR +37.7%; management plan remained 100%

audits.t: 649 Closed Loop Audit: Improving Surgical Handover in a Major Trauma Centre (RSCH)
audits.st: RCS handover guidelines
audits.f: Age documented 73%, responsible consultant 92%, significant investigations 60%, management plan 64%.
audits.c: Teaching session and RCS guidelines given to all surgical doctors.
audits.r2: Age 97%, responsible consultant 98%, significant investigations 93%, management plan 96%.

audits.t: 732 Who’s Your Consultant Surgeon? - a Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Francis Inquiry Report (2013) Recommendation 236: all inpatients should have a nominated responsible clinician
audits.f: 71% did not know their surgeon's name and 62% did not know their nurse's name; 76% of ward whiteboards had correct nominated staff information; 2% of bed-headboards had the surgeon's details.
audits.c: Junior doctor education to encourage communication with patients about their responsible care team
audits.r2: 14% improvement in awareness of surgeon's name; whiteboards correct 95%; bed-headboards with surgeon's details 24%.

audits.t: 759 Electronic Discharge Summary Audit
audits.st: PRSB electronic discharge summary guidance (endorsed by NICE), 13 categories
audits.f: 8% overall compliance.

audits.t: WP1.8 - No, we can’t repair your hernia: An audit to assess pre-operative optimisation for umbilical hernia repair
audits.tp: Preoperative risk optimisation in hernia repair
audits.st: European Hernia guidelines: smoking cessation and BMI <35 before elective umbilical/epigastric repair
audits.f: 12% (N=7) known smokers; 13% (N=8) BMI over 35; smoking status clearly documented in only 15 cases; 10% (N=6) poor diabetic control (HbA1c > 48) not addressed.

audits.t: WP1.9 - An audit of prophylactic antibiotic use in elective inguinal hernia repair
audits.st: National guidance: no antibiotic prophylaxis for low-risk patients; single dose for high-risk patients
audits.f: 53.33% of patients received antibiotics in line with national guidelines; 50.00% had prophylactic antibiotics overall

audits.t: WP2.11 - Improving prescription of discharge medications for day case surgery patients using electronic patient records system (EPIC); a closed loop audit
audits.st: GIRFT guidelines for day case discharge prescribing (analgesia, antiemetics, laxatives)
audits.f: 25% of patients received the correct discharge medications.
audits.c: Pre-populated discharge medication order set created in the EPIC electronic record.
audits.r2: 83% of patients received the correct discharge medications.

audits.t: WP4.6 - Reducing Unnecessary Transfusion of Blood Products – A Quality Improvement Project in a General Surgical Department in a District General Hospital
audits.st: NICE blood transfusion guideline thresholds
audits.f: 112 units in 42 patients; 45 units (40.2%) prescribed per NICE guidelines; 23 units (20.5%) transfused back-to-back inappropriately.
audits.c: Departmental teaching sessions and posters of NICE transfusion thresholds on surgical wards.
audits.r2: 133 units in 43 patients; 67 units (50.4%) prescribed per NICE guidelines; 6 units (4.51%) back-to-back inappropriately.

audits.t: WP4.9 - Audit on writing outpatient clinic letters in the general surgery department at a tertiary care hospital
audits.st: Academy of Medical Royal Colleges guidance on writing clinic letters
audits.f: Missing data by parameter: plan for patient/carer 37.5%, care planning arrangements 44.6%, complications 67.5%, anaesthesia issues 89.4%, allergies 94%, diagnosis 94%, time 99.4%, preferred name 100%, personal identifiers 100%.
audits.c: Findings presented at clinical governance meeting and a generic clinic letter template with mandatory parameters introduced; induction teaching planned.

audits.t: WP7.4 - A closed loop audit assessing adherence to NELA frailty guidelines in over 75’s undergoing Emergency Laparotomy
audits.tp: Frailty and geriatric review in emergency laparotomy
audits.st: NELA 2023: clinical frailty score recorded in over-65s and Care of the Elderly input if frail or aged 80+
audits.f: 0 patients had CFS recorded; 16% had COE review.
audits.c: Presentation at clinical governance, discussion with the COE consultant, and a poster for the surgical assessment unit.
audits.r2: 92% had CFS recorded; 46% had COE review.

audits.t: WP7.11 - An Audit of Geriatric Input and Analysis of The Barriers For Elderly Patients Undergoing Emergency Laparotomy
audits.tp: Frailty and geriatric review in emergency laparotomy
audits.st: NELA recommendations for geriatrician input in patients over 65
audits.f: Only around 10% received medical or geriatric input after emergency laparotomy.

audits.t: WP8.3 - "Effectiveness of Malnutrition Screen and Interventions for Surgical Inpatients - A MUST Score Based Audit"
audits.st: Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) completion, accuracy and updating
audits.f: MUST scores completed in 83.3% but with significant inaccuracies (BMI, weight loss, acute disease effect); only 15.6% updated.
audits.c: Malnutrition awareness week with dietitians and teaching sessions for healthcare staff on the MUST tool.

audits.t: WP8.4 - A closed-loop audit on the use of abbreviations in consent forms in the digestive disease department at a tertiary care centre
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Abbreviations in 99% of surgical and 76% of endoscopy consent forms.
audits.c: Posters, teaching sessions and clinical governance discussion.
audits.r2: Abbreviations in 56% of surgical and 4% of endoscopy consent forms.

audits.t: WP8.5 - Operative Documentation of Laparoscopic Appendicectomies at FVRH based on GIRFT - An Audit
audits.st: GIRFT guidance for laparoscopic appendicectomy operative documentation (27 data points)
audits.f: Best documented: findings 168 (98%), closure 168 (98%), stump securing 161 (94%). Worst: drain 7 (4%), blood loss 5 (3%), suture removal 6 (3%). Only 6 (37%) with a normal appendix confirmed whether it was removed.

audits.t: ThP1.2 - Management of breast cancer sentinel lymph node macrometastasis in the axilla; audit of current unit practice and evaluation of factors that influence patient management
audits.tp: Axillary management of sentinel node macrometastasis
audits.st: Association of Breast Surgery guideline on management of sentinel lymph node macrometastasis
audits.f: Completion ANC 56 (44.1%), axillary radiotherapy 37 (29.1%), no further treatment 34 (26.8%); all with >3 macrometastases (n=10) had cANC; 58% of post-menopausal BCS patients with ER+HER2- T1 tumours (n=12) had further axillary treatment contrary to guideline.

audits.t: ThP1.4 - Evidence-Based Perioperative Improvements in Microvascular Breast Free Flap Reconstruction: An Audit-Centric Evaluation & Retrospective Cohort Study
audits.tp: Perioperative care in breast free flap reconstruction
audits.st: ABS and BAPRAS guidelines; length of stay target under 3 days
audits.f: 22 flaps; average LOS 5.47 days (target <3d); no unplanned readmissions; 18% return to theatre; 18% total complication rate.
audits.c: Planned: evidence-based modified ERAS protocol via MDT collaboration.

audits.t: ThP5.3 - A Clinical Audit on Assessing Severe Acute Pancreatitis: Improving the use of the Glasgow-Imrie Criteria and outcomes
audits.st: Glasgow-Imrie Criteria scoring on admission for acute pancreatitis; scores ≥3 reviewed by senior and/or HDU/ITU
audits.f: 44% (22/50) of patients were scored using the Glasgow-Imrie Criteria.
audits.c: Presentation, posters and email, then a scoring tick box in the electronic clerking notes
audits.r2: 84% (49/58) scored; escalation of scores ≥3 rose from 17% to 100%.

audits.t: ThP6.13 - A closed loop clinical audit on adherence of weight-based and renal function-adjusted venous thromboprophylaxis prescribing to local guidelines in emergency general surgical patients
audits.st: Local trust guideline on weight- and renal function-adjusted VTE prophylaxis
audits.f: 49 (86.0%) prescribed per guideline; of 8 non-adherent, 5 (62.5%) had no prophylaxis and 3 (37.5%) incorrect doses.
audits.r2: 39 (90.7%) adhered; no dosing errors, but 4 (9.3%) had no prophylaxis prescribed.

audits.t: ThP6.17 - ‘If it’s not documented, it didn’t happen’: an audit into surgical ward documentation and clinicians expectations in a district general hospital
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons guidelines on adult surgical ward round documentation
audits.f: 21 daily and 21 post-take ward round entries: date 90%, consultant name 95%, time documented 29% and 35%, examination findings 33% (DWR) and 40% (PTWR), presenting complaint 45% of PTWR.

audits.t: ThP7.15 - An audit to assess the usefulness of investigations for patients with acute appendicitis
audits.st: NICE: acute appendicitis should be diagnosed clinically
audits.f: Imaging in 50.9%; CT 91.5% accurate, bloods 65.5%; ultrasound detected 57.1% of histologically proven appendicitis and reported 52% as normal.

audits.t: ThP7.16 - Multidisciplinary management of elderly patients undergoing emergency laparotomy: an audit at a small district general hospital
audits.st: NELA: early geriatrician involvement for patients aged over 80, or 65 and frail
audits.f: 17 patients met criteria for early geriatrician involvement; frailty score recorded in 22 of 34 aged 65+ (64%); less than 10% had early geriatrician input.

audits.t: ThP7.18 - Post-operative management and outcomes in emergency laparotomy - an audit of the updated 2023 NELA Standards in a busy district general hospital
audits.tp: Critical care admission after high-risk emergency laparotomy
audits.st: Updated 2023 NELA standards: high-risk patients (NELA risk 5% or more) admitted directly to critical care
audits.f: 38 of 43 high-risk patients directly admitted to critical care; median LOS 14 days, 7 died within 30 days (O/E mortality 1.12).

audits.t: FP1.11 - An audit of post colonoscopy Colorectal cancers within a Northern Ireland Health and Social Care Trust
audits.st: BSG key quality indicator of PCCRC rate (published rates 2-8%)
audits.f: 33 of 524 CRCs (6.3%) were PCCRCs; of these 21 (63.6%) had complete colonoscopy, 22 (66.6%) fair/satisfactory bowel preparation, 24 (72.7%) a lesion detected, 3 (9%) prior IBD.

audits.t: FP1.14 - A Re-audit of the prevalence of faecal incontinence in hospital inpatients
audits.tp: Identification of faecal incontinence in inpatients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Nursing bowel documentation 90%, medical 48%; 10.8% had FI; 31% would have been identified by medical documentation; all (100%) referred appropriately
audits.r2: Nursing bowel documentation 94%, medical 47%; 5.3% had FI; only 28% would have been identified by medical documentation; some action taken in 71.42% but no referral arranged in any

audits.t: FP3.5 - Colonoscopy post diverticulitis – Compliance with ACPGBI guidance in a single centre audit
audits.st: ACPGBI guidance on colonoscopy after diverticulitis
audits.f: 90 uncomplicated diverticulitis without surgery: 71 (59% of total) had colonoscopy, 19 (16%) did not; 78.9% of uncomplicated cases had colonoscopy, which may have been unnecessary. Complicated: 15 surgery, 15 no surgery, 11 (9.2%) colonoscopy, 4 (3.3%) no colonoscopy.

audits.t: FP4.6 - A Re-audit on the completion of pathology request forms following Colorectal Cancer Resection
audits.st: Royal College of Pathologists parameters for colorectal cancer resection request forms
audits.f: Approach mentioned 78%; diagrams 44%; preoperative therapy 4.5%.
audits.r2: Approach 30%; diagrams 36%; preoperative therapy 20%; no significant overall improvement.

audits.t: FP5.12 - Write what you know: A retrospective documentation audit
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians: every entry dated, timed and signed with name and designation, standardised structure and chronological order
audits.f: 89.8% dated; 42.0% timed; 93.2% standardised structure; 6.8% had author designation and 3.4% signature.

audits.t: FP5.14 - Enhancing Patient Communication in Surgical Care: an Audit of Practice at a DGH
audits.st: NICE guideline on patient experience in adult NHS services (clear information on diagnosis, oral and written communication, communication with family)
audits.f: Understanding of diagnosis varied before the intervention.
audits.c: Clear written information on imaging results and plans, and a patient information sheet to use throughout admission and share with family.
audits.r2: Majority (n=9) felt information was appropriately pitched; 13 received accessible information and found the sheet helpful.

audits.t: FP6.13 - A Quality improvement project to reduce the number of readmissions to surgical assessment unit (SAU) in East Sussex hospitals (ESHT) following laparoscopic cholecystectomy
audits.st: UK national average readmission rate of 5%
audits.f: Readmission rate 8.1%; about two-thirds on day one after discharge, half due to pain; almost 90% needed no intervention.
audits.c: Proposed: more clinic time for consent, junior doctor and nurse education, and patient leaflets and websites

audits.t: FP7.7 - Evaluation of small bowel obstruction management: A local audit in comparison to NASBO guidelines
audits.st: National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction (NASBO) recommendations
audits.f: CT on admission 98.3% (NASBO 80%), average time to CT 9 hours; surgery 27% with average time to surgery 2.4 days (NASBO 1 day); nutritional screening 100% (NASBO 90%).

audits.t: FP7.10 - An audit assessing the documentation of antibiotic indication and course length on an acute surgical unit
audits.tp: Antibiotic indication and review date documentation
audits.st: Documentation of antibiotic indication and course length on drug charts at prescription (recommended in numerous publications)
audits.f: Indication documented in 54.0% and course length in 42.0%.
audits.c: Results presented to junior doctors and reminder cards attached to drug charts
audits.r2: Indication documented in 74.0% and course length in 68.0%.

audits.t: EP51 - Uses of pharmaceutical and mechanical VTE prophylaxis - A clinical audit
audits.st: Local and NICE CG46 guidance on pharmacological and mechanical VTE prophylaxis
audits.f: Proforma completed in 87%; appropriate pharmacological prophylaxis 100%; appropriate mechanical prophylaxis under 40%.
audits.c: New proforma and teaching of junior doctors.
audits.r2: not reported (post-intervention data still being collected)

audits.t: EP127 - Audit on Acute PR Bleed Admissions to the Surgical Assessment Unit and the Use of the Shock Index and Oakland Score
audits.tp: Lower GI bleeding risk stratification (Oakland score)
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology: Shock Index (≤1) and Oakland Score (≤8) for safe discharge in acute PR bleeding
audits.f: SI documented in 0/37 and OS calculated in 1/37 at clerking; 12/34 (35%) managed appropriately; by OS, 20/34 (58.9%) incorrectly discharged.

audits.t: EP181 - The role of abdominal X-rays in the acute abdomen: a retrospective audit
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists guidelines on AXR in the acute setting
audits.f: 97% of AXR requests compliant with RCR guidelines; 30/62 also had CT after AXR.

audits.t: EP218 - A closed-loop audit on the assessment of the documentation of frailty at admission in emergency general surgery admission at a tertiary care hospital
audits.st: NHS frailty guidelines: frailty score documented at first contact for patients aged 65+
audits.f: 3/136 (2.2%) had frailty documented at first encounter.
audits.c: Discussion at clinical governance, teaching for junior doctors and a specific frailty section added to documentation.

audits.t: EP230 - A Closed Loop Audit for Peri-Operative Outcomes Comparing Laparoscopic and Robotic-Assisted Nephroureterectomy for Upper Tract Transitional Cell Carcinoma
audits.tp: Time to mitomycin C after nephroureterectomy
audits.st: EAU guidelines: MMC instillation 2–10 days after radical nephroureterectomy
audits.f: Laparoscopic RNU: average time to MMC 14 days (SD 6.7); average length of stay 5 days; bladder recurrence 41% (n = 14).
audits.c: Expansion of the robotic-assisted RNU service.
audits.r2: Robotic RNU: average time to MMC 2 days (SD 0.57); average length of stay 4 days; bladder recurrence 30% (n = 8).

audits.t: EP274 - A clinical audit on nasogastric tube placement documentation and adherence with NICE guidelines in general surgical patients across a district general hospital
audits.st: NICE guidance on confirming NG tube position by aspirate pH testing or X-ray if indeterminate
audits.f: Correctly documented NG tube position confirmation 60%; feeding tubes 4/4 correct; drainage tubes 45.5% correct; insertion length documented 33.3%; X-ray requested and documented in all inconclusive pH cases.

audits.t: EP335 - Audit of the Use of WHO Surgical Safety Checklist and its Awareness, Perception and Acceptability Amongst Theatre Personnel in a Tertiary Hospital in Sub-Saharan Africa
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist
audits.f: Checklist used in 52.1% of surgeries (80% major, 5.4% minor); activities stopped at Time Out in 23%; Sign Out least completed.

audits.t: EP359 - Introduction of a pathway to improve post operative nutrition for patients undergoing a Whipple procedure - a closed loop audit
audits.st: Local post-operative nutrition pathway
audits.f: Pathway adherence day 2 22%, day 3 11%; median 8 days to soft diet; median day 9 to stop parenteral nutrition; median length of stay 15 days.
audits.c: Pathway updated so all patients followed the same oral pathway (then second cycle); education session for surgical trainees by a dietitian (before third cycle).
audits.r2: Adherence day 2 57%, day 3 43%; median days to soft diet 5; median day stopping parenteral nutrition 6; median length of stay 10 days.

audits.t: EP403 - Departmental Engagement in NELA AUDIT and Royal College Standards of Risk Assessment
audits.st: NELA and Royal College standards: NELA score documented by ST3+, frailty assessment in patients 65+
audits.f: NELA score documented 39.6%; documented by ST3+ 24.8%; P-POSSUM documented 61.4%; both NELA and P-POSSUM 32.7%; frailty assessed in 38.6% of patients 65+.

audits.t: EP421 - The multidisciplinary management of acute pancreatitis at a district general hospital – an NCEPOD audit
audits.st: NCEPOD Acute Pancreatitis 2016 recommendations
audits.f: Cause identified in 70%; 100% of alcoholic pancreatitis referred to alcohol services; nutritional assessment in only 10%; uncontrolled comorbidities not referred onwards.
audits.c: MDT teaching sessions and an admission proforma (second loop planned).

audits.t: EP427 - Are we following the RCS England Guidelines for documentation of the operation note for a laparoscopic appendicectomy: A complete audit loop
audits.st: RCS England Good Surgical Practice 2014 (18 parameters)
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Compliance increased significantly in 9 of 18 parameters, 6 unchanged at almost 100%; post-op antibiotic instructions 83%, DVT prophylaxis 53%.

audits.t: EP442 - An Audit on the Application of Enhanced Recovery Post Emergency Laparotomy
audits.st: Enhanced recovery protocols (NG tube and catheter removal)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: EP465 - Transfusion Associated Circulatory Overload (TACO) Audit - A prospective analysis of adherence to standards ensuring safe transfusions
audits.st: SHOT recommendations (pre-transfusion TACO risk assessment with mitigation, reporting and incident review) and NICE NG24 weight-adjusted red cell dosing
audits.f: TACO checklist completed for 15% of transfusions (35% nationally); mitigation considered for 4%.
audits.c: Teaching sessions, information leaflets and posters, induction pack presentation, and liaison with transfusion practitioners to modify the transfusion pathway.

audits.t: EP474 - Recycling Theatre Waste: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 86.6 tons of waste; 18.4% recycled; monthly range 9.3% (January) to 35.0% (December).
audits.c: Quick guide for waste disposal and recycling made with the environmental department, disseminated electronically and physically.

audits.t: EP529 - The Impact of Royal College of Surgeon (RCS) Guidelines on the Quality of Operation Notes Documentation: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England (2014) operation note guidelines
audits.f: Documentation rate 37.5%; timing of surgery, findings, complications, additional procedures, blood loss, closure technique and DVT prophylaxis lacking.
audits.c: Improved version of the operation note introduced in line with RCS guidelines.
audits.r2: Documentation rate 83.3%, with all parameters exceeding 83% (overall improvement 45.8%).

audits.t: EP551 - Assessment of Surgical Management for Mild and Moderate Acute Gallstone Pancreatitis in Accordance with AUGIS Guidelines: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: AUGIS guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy during index admission or within two weeks for surgically fit patients with mild to moderate gallstone pancreatitis
audits.f: 19 (16.5%) had inpatient cholecystectomy, 42 (36.5%) outpatient cholecystectomy, 4 (3.5%) declined, 10 (8.7%) unfit; no documented reason in 40 (34.8%).

audits.t: MS O02 - OGC An audit of waiting times of the oesophagogastric cancer diagnostic pathway at a high-volume, tertiary centre
audits.st: NHS England target: 21 days from OGD to communication of treatment plan
audits.f: 13.8% met the 21-day target; only 13.3% had next-day CT after OGD (median 5.0 days); median pathway 49.0 days curative vs 35.0 palliative.

audits.t: EGS SO03 - Audit of wound complications after Emergency laparotomies in A University Teaching Hospital: 2-cycle Prospective Audit
audits.st: Established guidelines on complication rates after emergency midline closure
audits.f: Wound infection 123/621 (19.8%); acute fascial rupture 66/621 (10.6%); incisional hernia 87/621 (14%).
audits.r2: Wound infection 49/802 (6.2%); acute fascial rupture 34/802 (4.3%); incisional hernia 42/802 (5.2%).

audits.t: EGS SO05 - Improving the Flow of Patients Attending Surgical Assessment Unit: Introduction of Ambulatory USS Slots - Closed Loop Audit
audits.tp: Ultrasound waiting times in acute surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median wait from arrival to ultrasound 2 hours 15 minutes (range 59 minutes to 3 hours 39 minutes).
audits.c: Two daily ultrasound slots for SAU patients negotiated with radiology.
audits.r2: Median wait 1 hour 5 minutes (range 4 minutes to 2 hours 20 minutes); 48% reduction.

audits.t: EGS SO09 - Documentation Of Mortality While Consenting For Major Emergency Operation In General Surgery : Are We Informing Patients Or Just Impressing NELA? A Three-Cycle Clinical Audit
audits.st: NCEPOD 2011: risk of mortality explicitly discussed and documented on consent forms and in medical records
audits.f: Mortality documented in NELA 93%, consent forms 40%, medical notes discussion 35%
audits.c: Periodic reminders for surgeons during meetings and posters
audits.r2: Mortality documented in NELA 90%, consent forms 92%, medical notes 51% (consent improvement p < 0.0001)

audits.t: OGC SO12 - Extended Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Postoperative Oesophagogastric Cancer Patients: A Completed Audit
audits.tp: Extended VTE prophylaxis after abdominal cancer surgery
audits.st: NICE: extended pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for 28 days after major abdominal cancer surgery
audits.f: Pre-2014: 13/92 (14.1%) discharged with 28-day prophylaxis; post-2014: 423/490 (86.3%) (p<0.05); VTE 0.17%
audits.c: Trust-wide policy of 28-day extended VTE prophylaxis after discharge adopted in 2014
audits.r2: 63/68 (92.6%) received prophylaxis (86.3% to 92.6%, p=0.145); VTE 0%; no bleeding readmissions

audits.t: OGC SO20 - Audit of the guidelines for staging laparoscopy in gastro-oesophageal cancers
audits.tp: Staging laparoscopy and peritoneal cytology in gastric cancer
audits.st: Local staging laparoscopy and peritoneal washings guidelines
audits.f: 225 had washings; 2 appropriately not done due to extent of disease; 12 had washings not in line with policy, all with a clinical reason.

audits.t: OGC SO23 - Audit on Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) in Oesophago-gastric Resections for Cancers
audits.st: Trust ERAS protocol for oesophagectomy and gastrectomy (oral intake, drain, catheter and epidural removal, mobilisation, discharge medications)
audits.f: Oral diet started on time 85%; epidural removal 52.6% (95% within 24 h); catheter 55% (90%); apical drain 55.6% (100%); basal drain 53.8% (85.7%); abdominal drain 81.8% (90.9%); daily mobilisation 65%; VTE prophylaxis 100%; discharge medications 86.7% to 100%.

audits.t: OGC SO36 - Complications of palliative oesophageal cancer stent insertion: Audit for a five year period
audits.st: Published international standards (not specified)
audits.f: 45% had stent-related complications; 14% stent migration into the stomach; 25% tumour overgrowth. Median survival after stenting 94 days.

audits.t: BN SO02 - Cholecystectomy HRG Coding Audit
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Correct HRG coding based on comorbidity and complication index
audits.f: 69.23% of procedures coded incorrectly; £72,232 lost potential tariff (£372.33 per cholecystectomy); commonest correct code GA10J (CCI 3 in 29%), commonest wrong code GA10K (presumed CCI 0).
audits.c: Education and awareness under way before re-audit.

audits.t: BN SO11 - Optimising Day Case Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A GIRFT-Based Audit and Efficiency Analysis
audits.st: GIRFT national median day case rate of 60%
audits.f: Day case rate 64% (55/86), exceeding the national median of 60%.
audits.c: Business case to extend DSU recovery staffing and hours from 6pm to 9pm; coding team asked to separate elective from hot list cases.

audits.t: BN SO13 - Re-Audit of Biliary Pancreatitis Management: Enhancing Compliance with Timely Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
audits.st: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy within two weeks of admission for biliary acute pancreatitis
audits.f: 32.6% compliance.
audits.r2: 64.5% had laparoscopic cholecystectomy within two weeks of admission.

audits.t: BN SO29 - Overinvestigation and unnecessary surgery for Gallbladder Polyps: An audit of compliance with ESGAR guidelines
audits.st: 2021 ESGAR guidance on management of gallbladder polyps
audits.f: 35 (36%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy, including all with polyp >10mm; histology cholecystitis 69%, true gallbladder polyp 6%; 47% of symptomatic patients had two ultrasounds and two clinic appointments. Adherence to ESGAR was inconsistent.

audits.t: HPB SO25 - The impact of chest physiotherapy on post-operative recovery from open liver surgery: A quality improvement project
audits.tp: Chest physiotherapy after open liver surgery
audits.st: Early postoperative chest physiotherapy as part of the enhanced recovery protocol
audits.f: 18/50 (36%) received chest physiotherapy on POD1; 16 (32%) received none; PPCs 20%.
audits.c: Intensive preoperative patient education, poster campaign and increased engagement with physiotherapists about timely chest physiotherapy
audits.r2: 20/36 (57%) received chest physiotherapy on POD1 (p=0.07); 7 (19%) received none (p=0.19); PPCs 8% (p=0.13).

audits.t: HPB SO38 - Assessing current pancreatic cancer reporting practice against the PACT-UK Synoptic Reporting Template: An initial clinical audit
audits.st: PACT-UK synoptic reporting template for pancreatic cancer CT; compliance defined as more than 90% of information available
audits.f: Compliance 0% for initial presentation scans and 4.2% (n=1) of 24 staging scans; the only compliant scan used the PACT-UK template

audits.t: HPB SO60 - A Re-Audit: Radiological Investigations In Patients Diagnosed With Gallstone Disease
audits.st: NICE guidance: liver function tests and ultrasound first line for suspected gallstones, MRCP/EUS if not detected
audits.f: 44 CT scans; CTAP as first scan in 38 patients.
audits.c: Findings presented at local general surgery clinical governance meeting and communicated to hospital doctors.
audits.r2: 31 CT scans (30% decrease); CTAP as first scan in 21 patients (45% drop).

audits.t: HPB SO63 - A Closed-Loop Audit on Surgical Ward Round Documentation in a Tertiary Hospital
audits.st: Key components of ward round documentation (date, time, diagnosis, procedure, consultant, author, information given, observations, investigations, plan)
audits.f: Time, history, NEWS and plan recorded in more than 50%; diagnosis, consultant, author, information to patient, wound and medication review, fluid balance, investigations and discharge plans in less than 50%.
audits.r2: Date and time 94%; consultant and author initials 84%; examination, information to patient, wound and medication review more than 80%.

audits.t: HPB SO65 - An audit of the day-case rate of laparoscopic cholecystectomies at a busy district general hospital and factors affecting this
audits.st: Model Hospital target day-case rate of 75% for laparoscopic cholecystectomy
audits.f: 34% (29/85) were not day cases; causes included post-operative nausea or pain (11), monitoring (9), MRCP (3), social issues (3), bleeding (2), IV antibiotics (1).

audits.t: HPB SO67 - An audit to improve the perioperative administration of tranexamic acid (TXA) to reduce the need for peri- and post-operative blood transfusion in major HPB resections
audits.st: RCS England recommendation (following NHSBT amber alert): tranexamic acid for all adult surgical patients where more than 500 ml blood loss is likely
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Prompt for TXA added to the WHO timeout pre-operative checklist.
audits.r2: The prompt did not increase the likelihood of a pre-operative TXA dose; change in haemoglobin and transfusion rates were similar between groups.

audits.t: O2 Are elderly patients undergoing emergency laparotomy receiving appropriate geriatrician input: a closed loop audit as looking at NELA standards
audits.st: NELA: CFS documented on admission for all aged 65+; geriatrician review for aged 80+ or 65+ with CFS 5 or more
audits.f: 70 laparotomies, 42 aged 65+; CFS documented in 40%; zero geriatric referrals.
audits.c: Email on how to refer, posters in offices and a talk by a senior geriatric medicine registrar at the governance meeting.
audits.r2: 59 laparotomies, 40 aged 65+; CFS documented in 58%; 15 had inpatient geriatrician review.

audits.t: eP12 Identifying and Managing Surgical Site Infections in Emergency and Elective General Surgery: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: GIRFT and PHE recommendations on SSI surveillance; CDC SSI definition
audits.f: 153/699 (21.8%) flagged as probable infection; 20/153 (13%) true infection; wound assessment clearly documented in 86/153 (56%).
audits.c: Electronic SSI bundle to standardise documentation.

audits.t: eP24 Streamlining Diverticulitis Care: An Audit of Hospital Admission Practices
audits.st: NICE guidelines on diverticulitis (admission, antibiotics, dietary advice, outpatient colonoscopy)
audits.f: Baseline figures not reported in abstract.
audits.c: Findings presented at M&M and teaching sessions, and posters across the department.
audits.r2: Dietary advice increased by 57.8%; outpatient colonoscopy requests rose by 30.7%; no reduction in IV antibiotic use for uncomplicated diverticulitis.

audits.t: eP27 Treatment Escalation Plan (TEP) Completion Rates in Emergency Surgical Admissions: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: Target of TEP completion on first consultant ward round
audits.f: 19 (15%) had TEP forms; 5 (26%) by parent surgical team; median time to completion 2 days; 39 of 47 operated patients (83%) had no TEP.
