audits.f: HbA1c and ketones checked in 53%; intra-operative CBG monitoring 59%, recovery 63%; appropriate long-acting insulin on VRI 45%; anaesthetic-to-ward handover 42%; hyperglycaemia 42%, hypoglycaemia 21%.
audits.c: Planned before cycle 2: targeted education for surgical and anaesthetic teams and clearer handover processes.

audits.t: 855 Management of Frail Patients in Acute Surgical Wards: A First-Cycle Audit of Compliance With National Standards
audits.st: National guidance on early frailty assessment, recognition of high-risk patients and specialist geriatric involvement
audits.f: 29 (34.9%) frail (CFS ≥5); frailty documented in all cases; none referred to or reviewed by the frailty team; DNACPR undocumented in 24.1% of frail patients.

audits.t: 887 Enhancing Frailty Assessment in Emergency Surgical Admissions: Two-Cycle Audit of Screening Practices
audits.st: GIRFT and BGS 'Six Steps to Better Care': frailty screening on admission for all patients aged 65 or over (CFS, baseline mobility, 4AT, MUST)
audits.f: CFS documented 8%; baseline mobility 44%; 4AT 100%; MUST 82%.
audits.c: Raising awareness, education of clerking teams and promotion of a frailty screening bundle (CFS, baseline mobility, 4AT, MUST).

audits.t: 895 Improving Ward Round Documentation Through Implementation of a Structured Template: An Audit Cycle
audits.st: 16-point ward round documentation checklist based on guidelines and standards
audits.f: Average completeness 71.38%; bleep number 37%; VTE prophylaxis 26.5%; antibiotics 30.1%; analgesia 19.28%.
audits.c: Structured ward round template in the electronic patient record.
audits.r2: Average completeness 82.1% (range 43.75% to 100%); bleep number 57%; VTE prophylaxis 69.5%; antibiotics 58.5%; analgesia 58.5%.

audits.t: 927 Cholecystostomy Audit of Practice in a District General Hospital: Time for a Standardised Pathway
audits.st: Best-practice standards: Tokyo Grade II/III indication >90%; decision within 48 hours >80%; tubogram completion >80%
audits.f: Tokyo Grade II/III indication 56%; decision within 48 hours 52%; antibiotics 100%; post-procedure documentation 96%; tubogram 40%; definitive plan within 8 weeks 80%.
audits.c: Planned: standardised cholecystostomy pathway to be introduced in early 2026, with re-audit one year later.

audits.t: 973 Assessing the Quality of TURBT: A Comprehensive 18-Month Audit from a UK District General Hospital
audits.st: BAUS and EAU guideline standards, including detrusor muscle present in 70% of specimens (BAUS) and EAU indications for re-resection
audits.f: Detrusor muscle present in 55.4% (below BAUS 70% standard); tumour number documented in 86%, size in 84%, completeness of resection in 78%; MMC given in 53.5% of all cases and 58.8% of eligible NMIBC; 39 of 43 re-TURBTs met EAU indications.
audits.c: Planned: standardised TURBT operative template and targeted education, with re-audit to follow.

audits.t: 1016 A 2 Cycle Audit Evaluating the Impact of an RCS-Aligned Proforma on Surgical Handover Compliance in a District General Hospital
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons core criteria for safe handover (13 criteria)
audits.f: Mean total compliance score 44.6%; shortcomings in operational issues and resuscitation status.
audits.c: Structured RCS-aligned handover proforma (later incorporated into the electronic system).
audits.r2: Mean total compliance score 70.2% (p<0.001), improved across all criteria.

audits.t: 1029 Time to Oesophagogastroduodenoscopy (OGD) in Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Two Cycle Audit at a Rural District General Hospital
audits.st: NICE: OGD within 24 hours of admission for acute upper GI bleeding
audits.f: 32% (n=19) received OGD within 24 hours.
audits.c: Formal inclusion of the AUGIB OGD caseload in the on-call handover.

audits.t: 1250 Improving Documentation of the Clinical Frailty Scale and Social History in ICU Admissions: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Clinical Frailty Scale and social history documentation
audits.st: Complete CFS and social history documentation in ICU clerking proformas; aim above 80% CFS completion
audits.f: CFS completion 52%; social history completion 54%.
audits.c: Educational posters, daily reminders at morning handover, and results shared at the monthly audit meeting.

audits.t: 1264 Audit: Compliance With ESTS and BTS Guidelines for Intraoperative Lymph Node Staging in NSCLC Surgery
audits.tp: Intraoperative lymph node staging in lung cancer surgery
audits.st: ESTS and BTS intraoperative lymph node staging guidelines for NSCLC resection
audits.f: Overall compliance 16.3% (thoracotomy 8.7%, VATS 6.5%); RATS highest-performing.
audits.c: Presentation of results and dissemination of guideline summaries.
audits.r2: Overall compliance 17.1% (thoracotomy 12.5%, VATS 8.0%); RATS remained highest.

audits.t: 1374 Theatre Turn-Around Times in Northern Ireland (NI) – a Baseline Audit
audits.st: National benchmarking target of 15 minutes theatre turnaround
audits.f: Mean overall turnaround 37.7 mins (SD 15.4), above the 15-minute target; cleaning 8.11 mins, extubation 5.11 mins, scrub 4.7 mins.

audits.t: 1378 Adherence to Guidelines on Smoking Cessation and Weight Optimisation in Elective Umbilical and Epigastric Hernia Repair: A Multi-Centre Audit
audits.tp: Preoperative risk optimisation in hernia repair
audits.st: European and American Hernia Society guidelines on preoperative smoking cessation and weight optimisation
audits.f: 19 (32.2%) BMI ≥35: 1 postponed and referred, 17 (89.5%) proceeded without documented intervention; 10 (16.9%) smokers: 2 received documented cessation advice, 8 none.

audits.t: 1386 Are We Recording What We Should? a Closed-Loop Audit of Surgical Operation Notes
audits.st: RCSEng Good Surgical Practice (2025) operation note documentation standards
audits.f: Surgeon details, procedure, date and findings >98%; time of operation 2%, elective/emergency status 10%, complications 22%, prosthesis 18%, EBL 2%, antibiotic prophylaxis 50%, DVT prophylaxis 48%.
audits.c: Findings presented at departmental audit meeting and posters displayed in the theatre office.
audits.r2: Time of operation 28%, elective/emergency status 28%, complications 40%, prosthesis 55%, EBL 20%, antibiotic prophylaxis 66%, DVT prophylaxis 56%.

audits.t: 1475 Advancing Rib Fracture Care: Two-Cycle Audit
audits.st: Local trust guidelines for multiple rib fractures (analgesia, imaging, chest injury scoring, pain team and regional anaesthesia referral, ABG, CCU referral)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Targeted interventions following first-cycle recommendations (not detailed).
audits.r2: Improvement in appropriate analgesia prescription and chest injury scoring documentation; over 75% of eligible patients not referred to Critical Care; ABG compliance in hypoxic patients deteriorated.

audits.t: 1108 Improving Patient Flow in a 2 Week Wait One-Stop Breast Clinic: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: RCS Outpatient Clinics: A Guide to Good Practice and GIRFT Clinically-Led Specialty Outpatient Guidance (2023)
audits.f: Mean 2 hours 20 minutes from imaging to results; only 20% required core biopsy, further imaging or assessment.
audits.c: New breast clinic proforma and pathway redesign allowing earlier discharge of patients with normal findings.
audits.r2: Total clinic duration reduced by 36 minutes.

audits.t: 333 Rates and Outcomes of Renal Replacement Therapy in Post-Cardiac Surgery Patients: A Single-Centre Audit Against National Recommendations
audits.tp: Renal replacement therapy after cardiac surgery
audits.st: GIRFT 2018 benchmark RRT rate (1.56%) and NICOR data (isolated CABG 0.98–1.45%)
audits.f: 90 of 3,261 patients required RRT (1.14%), below the GIRFT benchmark of 1.56%; isolated CABG RRT rate 2.76%, higher than NICOR reports (0.98–1.45%).

audits.t: EP 591 Follow-Up Colonoscopy in Acute Diverticulitis: A Retrospective Audit of Guideline Adherence
audits.st: WSES and ESCP guidelines: colonoscopy 6-8 weeks after complicated diverticulitis
audits.f: 1 of 21 colonoscopies within 6-8 weeks; timely colonoscopy in 5% of complicated cases; 1 malignancy.
audits.r2: 6 of 18 complicated cases had timely colonoscopy; overall 46% of complicated cases timely; no malignancies.

audits.t: 468 Post-Thyroidectomy Voice and Vocal Cord Function Outcomes and Management: A Two-Cycle Audit
audits.st: BAETS/ENT UK postoperative standards: voice documentation within 24 hours, FNE, SLT/laryngology referral, validated PROMs
audits.f: Voice documentation within 24 hours 89%; 35% of symptomatic patients had FNE within 24 hours; PROMs (VHI-10, EAT-10) not routinely used.
audits.c: Structured proforma, SLT referral pathway and PROM integration.
audits.r2: Early second-cycle data indicated improved documentation and referral rates; no figures given.

audits.t: 1195 Asymmetrical Tonsils - Audit of Clinical Practice
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 44 of 149 tonsillectomies were for histology, 29 for asymmetry; only 16 histology reports gave tonsil weight, 60% with weight difference of 0.5g or less; visual asymmetry did not predict weight difference (p=0.0561); no malignancy; postoperative bleeding 10.3%.

audits.t: 117 Initial Severity Assessment in Patients with Acute Pancreatitis in a UK District General Hospital: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.st: International Association of Pancreatology guidance on initial severity assessment (Modified Atlanta Classification)
audits.f: None had a formal severity assessment recorded.
audits.c: Pancreatitis Severity Scoring proforma with Modified Atlanta criteria in e-care, plus education at M&M meetings, junior doctor inductions and multidisciplinary awareness campaigns.
audits.r2: 66.6% (18/27) had a proforma completed, of which 38.8% (7/18) were fully completed.

audits.t: 1186 Outpatient Colonoscopy After Appendicectomy in Patients Over the Age of 40: Clinical Audit of Compliance in Practice
audits.tp: Colonic evaluation after appendicectomy in over-40s
audits.st: Local guideline: postoperative outpatient colonoscopy or CT colonography for patients aged ≥40 after appendicectomy
audits.f: 25 patients (37.3%) referred for postoperative colonic evaluation.
audits.c: Educational email with supporting evidence sent to surgical teams.
audits.r2: 28 patients (62.2%) received appropriate postoperative colonic evaluation.

audits.t: 473 Primary Care Perspectives on Bariatric Surgery: An Audit of Outcomes and Monitoring of Patients Discharged to Primary Care
audits.st: BOMSS annual nutritional monitoring (five blood tests), 80% standard; mean BMI reduction audit standard 20%
audits.f: Mean BMI reduction 23.07% (standard 20%); 14.29% had all five recommended annual blood tests; FBC 63.74% highest, 25-hydroxyvitamin D 25.27% lowest.

audits.t: 856 Gallbladder Polyp Surveillance at MFT Hospitals: Audit of Current Practice Against Latest Guidelines
audits.st: 2021 joint European guidelines on gallbladder polyp surveillance
audits.f: 17% of patient pathways adhered to the guidelines; 14% adherent for patients with risk factors; 58 unnecessary scans and 35 missed cholecystectomy referrals.
audits.c: Recommended: single guideline distribution, inclusion of unacknowledged size thresholds and a standardised radiology reporting template.

audits.t: 1088 Evaluating the Impact of an Advanced Nurse Practitioner on Surgical Referral-to-Review Times in General Surgery: A Closed-Loop Quality Improvement Cycle
audits.st: Trust standard: surgical referrals reviewed within 30 minutes (to support the four-hour ED standard)
audits.f: 33% of referrals reviewed within 30 minutes (27% in General Surgery); mean referral-to-review 1h 52m, median 1h 8m; administrative tasks 33.2% of time.
audits.c: Advanced Nurse Practitioner introduced to General Surgery.
audits.r2: 34% reviewed within 30 minutes; mean referral-to-review 1h 2m, median 40m; administrative tasks 24.4% of time (p = 0.045).

audits.t: 792 IR-Guided Cerebral Angiograms: A Local Audit of RCR Compliance
audits.st: RCR standards: written consent 100%, procedural documentation 100%, pseudoaneurysm/AV fistula ≤1%, access-site haematoma needing intervention ≤3%, dissection ≤1%, reversible neurological deficit ≤2%, permanent deficit ≤1%, major contrast reactions ≤5%
audits.f: Complications broadly within RCR thresholds but pseudoaneurysm frequency exceeded the ≤1% target (groin haematoma with pseudoaneurysm n=2, pseudoaneurysm with groin haematoma n=6); procedure-related bleeding n=4 and stroke n=4; consent and documentation consistent.

audits.t: 96 Enhancing Referrals to Our Surgical Ambulatory Unit: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: NICE QS174 and RCS England safe handover guidance: referral to include diagnosis, background and plan
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Team education and reminder prompts across the department
audits.r2: Improvement in all domains: diagnosis (p<0.0001), background (p<0.0001) and plan (p=0.0007); referrals with no information significantly reduced (p=0.0063)

audits.t: 347 Implementing SINBAD Classification for Improved Documentation of Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: NICE recommendation to document diabetic foot ulcers with a standardised system such as SINBAD
audits.f: Site 65%, ischaemia 41%, neuropathy 0%, bacterial infection 35%, area 58%, depth 35%; no notes used a standardised system.
audits.c: Staff training and a SINBAD-based documentation template.

audits.t: 430 A Two Cycle Closed-Loop Audit Evaluating MSU Compliance for New Urology Admissions at Royal Bolton Hospital
audits.tp: Urine culture before antibiotics in suspected UTI
audits.st: National and local guidance on MSU sampling for suspected UTI; SMART aim 100% adherence by July 2025
audits.f: MSU compliance 60%; 16.7% had MSU sent before antibiotics; median MSU-to-first-antibiotic time 22.25 hours.
audits.c: PDSA cycles raising awareness first among doctors, then nursing and HCA staff.
audits.r2: MSU sampling 67%; 50% received antibiotics after MSU collection; median MSU-to-antibiotic time 5 hours.

audits.t: 542 Assessment of Inflammatory Markers and Antibiotic Prescribing Practices in Acute Diverticulitis: Insights from a District General Hospital Audit
audits.st: National guidelines (NICE NG147, ACPGBI, GIRFT) recommending selective antibiotic use in uncomplicated diverticulitis
audits.f: Among immunocompetent patients with CT-confirmed uncomplicated diverticulitis (modified Hinchey ≤1A), 95.3% received antibiotics; 97% in the whole cohort.

audits.t: 550 A Closed Loop Audit of Ultrasound Use in Paediatric Patients Presenting with Abdominal Pain in a District General Hospital
audits.st: Ultrasound as the recommended first-line imaging for suspected appendicitis in children
audits.f: Ultrasound used in 30% of patients diagnosed with appendicitis; MRI was the index modality in 42%.
audits.c: More ultrasound slots, access to sonographer training and a standardised ultrasound reporting format
audits.r2: Ultrasound was the index imaging in 77%; specificity 93% (n=80), sensitivity 27% (n=11).

audits.t: 112 Empowering Surgical Trainees in ENT Emergencies: Lessons From a Dual-Cycle ED Audit
audits.tp: ENT casualty management of common acute presentations
audits.st: NICE and RCEM standards for epistaxis and vertigo management
audits.f: First-aid and procedural steps: epistaxis 33%, vertigo 69%; recognition of central-cause red flags (vertigo) 32%.
audits.c: Joint ED–EGS teaching with simulation and workshops, ENT management proformas and flowcharts on the intranet, and QR-linked video resources.
audits.r2: Epistaxis 84%; vertigo 80%; central-cause red flag recognition 85%.

audits.t: 676 So What Is NEWS? an Audit of Near to Peer Surgical Teaching With Qualitative and Quantitative Analyses
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Previous cycle: confidence responding to NEWS rose 62.2%, taking histories 7.09%, examining a patient 25.3%.
audits.c: Compound questionnaire added to assess confidence and formatively test knowledge before and after each session.
audits.r2: Confidence responding to NEWS rose 87%, using ABCDE 51%, escalating concerns 38%, emergency treatments 86%; formative scores rose from 61% to 72%.

audits.t: 828 Improving Access to Lymph Node FNA: An Audit of Diagnostic Timelines, Inconclusive Rates, and Outcomes in Cutaneous Malignancy
audits.tp: Lymph node FNA diagnostic timelines in skin cancer
audits.st: Faster Diagnosis Standard: diagnosis within 28 days; Cheshire and Merseyside guidelines and GIRFT standards
audits.f: 22 (38%) underwent FNA; median time from detection to FNA result exceeded the 28-day target by 8 days; inconclusive FNAs averaged 62.5 days to final diagnosis.

audits.t: 37 From Stones to Standards: A Two-Cycle Audit on Optimising Urolithiasis Management
audits.tp: Metabolic evaluation in urinary stone disease
audits.st: BAUS recommendation for urgent CT KUB; EAU guidelines on metabolic tests (calcium, uric acid) in confirmed urolithiasis
audits.f: CT KUB positive in 60/136 (44.1%); calcium checked in 38.3% (23/60); urate in 20.0% (12/60)
audits.c: Email reminder to urology middle grades and consultants

audits.t: 154 Recovering From Multiple Missed Torsions: A Service Improvement in a District General Hospital
audits.st: Timely surgery for suspected testicular torsion with TWIST score risk stratification
audits.f: Mean time to theatre 276 minutes from ED presentation and 200 minutes from decision-to-operate; TWIST score calculated in 3.6% of cases.
audits.c: New torsion pathway in 2023: expedited referral from triage, electronic TWIST-based risk stratification tool, and targeted ED and urology education.
audits.r2: Mean time to theatre 162 minutes from presentation and 100 minutes from decision-to-operate; TWIST documented in 75%.

audits.t: 327 Improving Compliance with a Ureteric Stent Database: A Two-Year Retrospective Audit
audits.st: Trust stent database documenting insertion and removal dates
audits.f: 173 (42.5%) had no documented stent outcome; 16 overdue stents, 12 already listed; two patients missed completely.

audits.t: 328 Is It Our Culture to Culture? a Second-Loop Audit of Preoperative MSU Screening Prior to Endourological Procedures
audits.st: EUA 2024 and GIRFT 2025 guidance on preoperative urine testing and treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria; 100% standard
audits.f: MSU uptake 3.8%; suboptimal management of positive cultures.
audits.c: New screening pathways in the pre-operative assessment clinic and microbiology team.
audits.r2: MSU uptake 47.9% (35/73); 13 (37.1%) culture-positive, of whom only 3 had documented antibiotic treatment.

audits.t: 730 Are We Over-Stenting? a Single-Centre Audit of Ureteric Stent Use After Uncomplicated Ureteroscopy
audits.st: Guidelines advise against routine ureteric stenting after uncomplicated ureteroscopy for stones
audits.f: 91/143 (63.6%) were stented and 52 (36.4%) were not stented.

audits.t: 1000 Improving Ureteric Stent Follow-Up: A Retrospective Audit of Delayed and Retained Stents in a District General Hospital
audits.st: Stent removal within 6 weeks or by target date
audits.f: Removal plan documented in 95.7% (93.5% of discharge summaries); timely removal 59.1%; delayed 35.5% (33/93), 4.3% in situ over six months; possible retained 3.2%; unknown 2.1%.

audits.t: 1068 Identifying gaps in the transition to benign LUTS Care Following Negative 2WW Prostate Cancer Referral: A NICE and EAU Guideline-Based Outpatient Audit
audits.tp: LUTS care after negative prostate cancer referral
audits.st: NICE CG97 and EAU 2024: LUTS assessment at 2WW appointment and lifestyle counselling, follow-up or LUTS pathway activation
audits.f: LUTS assessment documented in 203/268 (76%); of 143 with LUTS, 54 (38%) had LUTS pathway activated, 4 (3%) lifestyle advice; 84 (59% of those with LUTS) had no documented advice, pathway or follow-up.

audits.t: 1421 Epididymitis and Orchitis Management: An Audit of Compliance With GIRFT and Local Antimicrobial Guidelines
audits.st: GIRFT epididymo-orchitis pathway and local antimicrobial guidelines
audits.f: Antibiotic compliance 50%
audits.c: Posters with QR code links to GIRFT pathways and antimicrobial guidelines in SSDEC and SAU
audits.r2: Antibiotic compliance 70%; sexual health history and assessment uptake increased by 34%

audits.t: 742 Improving Cardiovascular Risk Optimisation in Vascular Surgery Patients: A Two-Cycle Audit of Adherence to VSGBI Standards
audits.tp: Best medical therapy in peripheral arterial disease
audits.st: VSGBI cardiovascular risk reduction framework: BMT, gastroprotection, HbA1c and lipid assessment
audits.f: Antiplatelet 124/153 (81.1%); anticoagulation 60/153 (39.2%); statin 122/153 (79.7%); gastroprotection 54/153 (35.3%); HbA1c 27/153 (17.7%); lipid profile 19/153 (12.4%).
audits.c: Surgical team teaching sessions and departmental posters.
audits.r2: Antiplatelet 50/60 (83.3%); anticoagulation 30/60 (50.0%); statin 48/60 (80.0%); gastroprotection 40/60 (66.7%); HbA1c 18/60 (30.0%); lipid profile 39/60 (65.0%).

audits.t: 780 Assessment of Alignment with National ReSPECT and Cardiac Arrest Decision-Making Standards: A Quality Improvement Audit of Escalation of Care Planning for Frail and Older Vascular Inpatients
audits.st: BMA, RCN and Resuscitation Council (UK) guidance: 100% ReSPECT form completion for eligible patients
audits.f: ReSPECT forms completed in 11 cases (23.4%).
audits.c: Recommended: ReSPECT initiation in admission workflows, escalation discussions on MDT rounds, electronic prompts and education for junior clinicians.

audits.t: 1414 Improving the Detection and Initial Management of Phantom Limb Pain Post-Amputation: A Close-Looped Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Phantom limb pain management after amputation
audits.st: NICE guidance on early neuropathic pain treatment
audits.f: PLP assessment within 48 hours 44%; pain team referral 52%; neuropathic medication within 48 hours 42%; discharge plan documented 21%.
audits.c: Education sessions and posters for junior ward doctors
audits.r2: PLP assessment 33%; pain team referral 67%; neuropathic medication 37%; discharge plan 22%.

audits.t: 12 Post-ERCP Pancreatitis in a District General Hospital: A Retrospective Audit of Incidence, Peri-Procedural Practice, and Clinical Outcomes in 157 Consecutive Procedures
audits.st: BSG standards (rectal diclofenac prophylaxis); published PEP incidence benchmark 3–8%
audits.f: PEP in 9/157 (5.7%); rectal diclofenac compliance ≈99%; pre-ERCP amylase documented in 6.3%; pre-operative IV fluids 29%; post-operative IV fluids 41.4%.

audits.t: 11 A Closed-Loop Audit of Operative Note Quality in HPB Surgery: Adherence to RCS Good Surgical Practice 2025 Standards
audits.st: RCS Good Surgical Practice 2025 operative note standards plus HPB-specific fields
audits.f: Overall compliance 67%; operative diagnosis 18.3%, estimated blood loss 23.9%, intraoperative complications 1.4%, IOUS 40.9%.
audits.c: EPIC SmartPhrase operation note template (hpbopnote), departmental presentations, theatre visual reminders and targeted education.
audits.r2: Overall compliance 94%; operative diagnosis 93.9%, blood loss 95.5%, complications 69.7%, IOUS 100%, Pringle's time 100%.

audits.t: 13 Routine Intraoperative Cholangiography (IOC) in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Single-Centre Audit of 279 Consecutive Cases
audits.st: SAGES 2025 guideline standards; 12-point checklist for IOC reading
audits.f: IOC successful in 93.2%; CBD filling defects in 6.2%; 4/279 (1.5%) needed further imaging; no post-cholangiography pancreatitis.

audits.t: Learning from Regional Excellence: Geographic Analysis of the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) Mortality Improvement
audits.st: NELA process standards (critical care admission, CT imaging, data completeness, elderly assessment)
audits.f: Mortality fell from 11.36% (2016) to 8.15% (2025); regional mortality ranged 5.4% (London South West) to 11.3% (Yorkshire & Humber).

audits.t: SP 2.07 A National Prospective Audit of Acute Pancreatitis in the era of GLP-1 agonists (PANDORA): Breaking Results
audits.tp: Acute pancreatitis with GLP-1 receptor agonist use
audits.st: Compliance with MHRA Yellow Card reporting
audits.f: 8% of patients with proven acute pancreatitis were taking a GLP-1RA; fewer than 5% of these cases were reported to the MHRA. Critical care admission 4.8% (GLP-1RA) vs 4.2% (non-GLP-1RA).

audits.t: SP 3.17 A Multicentre Audit Comparing Decision-Making Across Welsh Multidisciplinary Teams for Newly Diagnosed Rectal Cancer
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: TNT recommended in 21 cases; 11 managed with organ preservation intent; short-course radiotherapy use varied markedly between centres.

audits.t: SP 6.03 Improving Surgical Handover Report Documentation: A Three-Cycle Audit
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidance on safe handover
audits.f: Patient inclusion on handover list 42%; entries updated before handover 27%; documentation completeness 23%.
audits.c: Results disseminated departmentally, then a structured handover tutorial embedded in resident doctor induction.

audits.t: SP 9.13 Use of National and Local NELA Data for Quality Improvement of EGS Pathways Allows Calculation of Required Provision of CT Capacity for A “Straight to Test” (STT) CT Pathway for Potential Emergency Laparotomy (EL) Patients Presenting in The Emergency Department (ED)
audits.st: National guidelines: senior surgical assessment of emergency laparotomy patients; NELA data
audits.f: EGS audit: 23 CTs, 50% needed GS admission, 25% another specialty, 25% no admission. ED audit: 147 GI-coded patients, 34 potential EL, 20 had CT, only 15 referred to GS.
audits.c: Straight-to-test CT pathway drawn up using local characteristics and NELA data.
audits.r2: 139 CTs, no discrepancies; 7 EL patients (5%); 134 (96%) changed management; 66 (54%) admissions avoided; 11% new cancers; 10-12 STT CTs per day needed (1/30,000 population/day).

audits.t: SP 10.14 Oncological Outcomes of Emergency Versus Elective Colonic Resection for Colon Cancer: A Retrospective Audit Based on Guideline Compliance
audits.tp: Oncological quality of emergency colon cancer resection
audits.st: ESMO and RCPath standards: R0 resection, lymph node yield >15, no conversion
audits.f: Emergency vs elective: R0 96.97% vs 100%; lymph node yield >15 94.74% vs 98.99% (p = 0.2973); no conversion 89.47% vs 97.98% (p = 0.1211); overall compliance 84.21% vs 94.95%.

audits.t: TPT 1.12 Closing The ERAS Compliance Gap in Colorectal Surgery: A Completed Audit Cycle Highlighting Persistent Intra-Operative Variation
audits.st: ERAS protocol elements (pre-, intra- and post-operative)
audits.f: Counselling documentation 6.25%; pre-operative documentation 93.75%; fasting 87.5%; carbohydrate drink 75%; regional anaesthesia and normothermia 100%; NG tubes 25%; drains 14/16; opioids 100%; POD1 mobilisation 75%.
audits.r2: All pre-operative measures 100%; mobilisation within 24 hours 85%; liquids by POD1 95%; solids by POD3 85%; median LOS 5 days; drains 85%, NG tubes 80%, opioids 100%.

audits.t: TPT 1.13 Assessment of Compliance with ACPGI Guidelines for Patients Undergoing Endoscopy Post Diverticulitis: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: ACPGBI 2021: endoscopy at 6 weeks for complicated diverticulitis, age >50, rectal bleeding or concerning imaging
audits.f: 25 met criteria; 15 (60%) had endoscopy booked.

audits.t: TPT 2.02 The Right Tool for the Job: A Completed Audit Cycle of Trainee Surgical Equipment Knowledge with A Novel Educational Intervention
audits.st: RACS MCQ pass grade of 60%
audits.f: Mean MCQ score 46.4% (median 35.7%, range 28.6-85.7%); standard not met.
audits.c: Practical multidisciplinary teaching session with scrub nurse educators demonstrating a general surgical set and draping.
audits.r2: Mean MCQ score 80.4% (median 71.4%, range 71.4-100%); standard met (p<0.001).

audits.t: TPT 3.04 Acute Diverticulitis: An Audit of Management Against NICE Guidelines
audits.st: NICE NG147 for antibiotic prescribing and surgical management of diverticular disease
audits.f: Blood tests and CT imaging in 100%; antibiotic prescribing compliant with NICE in 38% (10/26); antibiotic duration 3–42 days, median 8 days.

audits.t: TPT 3.11 Evaluating Emergency Appendicectomy Practice in a District General Hospital: A Retrospective Audit
audits.st: National guidance on timely surgery, preoperative imaging and postoperative antibiotic prescribing for emergency appendicectomy
audits.f: Surgery within 24 hours of decision in 73.4%; 45.0% of delays justified, 41.0% due to theatre capacity; preoperative imaging 61.3%; acute pathology on histology 79.0%; postoperative antibiotics 67.2%.

audits.t: TPT 5.03 Closed-Loop Audit of Failed Day-Case Discharges following Inguinal Hernia Repair
audits.st: BADS and GIRFT day-case guidance
audits.f: 44% failed same-day discharge; most common cause was failure to discharge by nursing staff (42%) despite medical fitness.
audits.c: Standardised day-case discharge checklist; doctors, nurses and ward managers briefed on its use.

audits.t: TPT 5.07 Improving Postoperative Discharge Documentation for Inguinal Hernia Repair: An Audit of Compliance with British Hernia Society Guidelines and the Impact of Standardised Patient Leaflets
audits.st: British Hernia Society guidance on postoperative information after inguinal hernia repair
audits.f: Analgesia 0%, bruising/swelling 45%, heavy lifting 75%, DVT/mobility 63%, numbness/pain 0%, closure type 36%, safety-netting 45%, exercise 45%, dressing changes 16%, mesh 90%, postoperative bleeding 50%, showering/bathing 50%.
audits.c: Standardised patient information leaflet on analgesia, exercise and lifting, wound care, closure type and red-flag symptoms given to all patients.
audits.r2: GP and ED attendances for postoperative concerns decreased substantially; 98% of patients reported improved understanding of postoperative instructions.

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: TPT 6.09 Enhancing Patient Safety through Standardised Operative Note Documentation- A Closed-Loop Audit on Laparoscopic Appendicectomy Operative Note

audits.t: TPW 2.08 Post-Colonoscopy Colorectal Cancer (PCCRC): Two-Year Audit Using the WEO Framework to Target Preventable Harm

audits.t: TPW 3.07 Closed Loop Audit: Acute Kidney Injury Management in General Surgical Patients in a Busy Teaching Hospital

audits.tp: Lower GI bleeding risk stratification (Oakland score)

audits.t: TPW 5.04 Introduction of Post-Operative Antibiotic Guidelines Leads to Reduced Length of Post-Operative Stay and Improved Antimicrobial Stewardship in Uncomplicated Appendicectomy: A Single Centre Closed-Loop Audit

audits.st: GIRFT and Royal College of Surgeons benchmarks for operative approach, length of stay, complications and readmission

audits.st: National and WSES recommendations for laparoscopic appendicectomy

audits.t: TPW 6.13 Timing of Cholecystectomy for Gallstone Disease in a District General Hospital: A Retrospective Audit of Guideline Compliance, Readmissions and Service Burden

audits.t: TPW 7.03 Shared Decision-Making and Documentation before ERCP for Choledocholithiasis: A GMC-Aligned Audit Using Prespecified Operative-Risk Strata
audits.st: UK legal and professional (GMC) standards: documentation of material risks and reasonable alternatives (options-based shared decision-making) before ERCP

audits.t: TPW 7.13 Audit into the Management of Gallstone Pancreatitis at A Tertiary Care NHS Trust
audits.st: NICE: cholecystectomy during index admission or within two weeks of discharge for non-severe gallstone pancreatitis
audits.f: Of 30 mild or moderate cases, 2 (6.6%) had cholecystectomy during index admission; of 14 (45%) with elective surgery within five months, 2 (14%) were within two weeks.

audits.t: TPW 7.16 Improving Compliance with Severity Scoring in Acute Pancreatitis: A Two-Cycle Audit
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology: severity scoring within 48 hours of admission

audits.t: TPW 7.20 Closed Loop Audit: Assessing Parenteral Nutrition in General Surgical Patients in A Busy Teaching Hospital
audits.st: Local nutrition standards

audits.t: TPW 9.08 Establishing and Evaluating a Laparoscopic Peritoneal Dialysis Catheter Insertion Service in NHS Lanarkshire: A Two-Cohort Comparative Audit
audits.tp: Laparoscopic peritoneal dialysis catheter insertion outcomes

audits.t: TPW 9.16 Comparative Re-Audit of Unplanned Delays in Emergency General Surgery Theatre Lists

audits.t: TPTh 1.09 Improving Prescribing of Regular Medications in Nil-by-Mouth Surgical Patients: A Closed-Loop Audit at a District General Hospital

audits.t: TPTh 2.12 Regional Adherence to National GIRFT Surgical Guidelines on Post-Operative Antibiotic Prescribing in Paediatric Appendicitis: Multi-Centre Multi-Cycle Audit of Clinical Practice
audits.st: GIRFT guidelines on post-operative antibiotic prescribing in paediatric appendicitis

audits.t: TPTh 2.14 Enhancing Guideline Adherence in Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding Through Structured Risk Stratification: A Two-Cycle Audit

audits.f: 67/70 (96%) met hospital abdominal pain CT pathway criteria at triage; 10/70 (14%) met RCEM criteria; mean time to CT from ED arrival 11 hr 36 min.

audits.t: TPTh 3.09 Audit of Diagnosis and Management of Acute Lower Gastrointestinal Tract Bleeding (LGIB) in a Rural General Hospital, can we reduce hospital admissions?

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: TPTh 4.12 Utilisation of Risk Scoring and Imaging in Acute Appendicitis Diagnosis: A Retrospective Audit of Appendicitis Diagnostic Pathways

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: EP 687 Are we Overscoping?: An Audit of Colonoscopic Follow-up in Acute Diverticulitis Management

audits.f: Only 17% of requests met the standards; 41% inappropriate; 42% had insufficient details.
audits.c: Local ANA testing guidelines devised from Choosing Wisely standards.

audits.t: P15 An audit of the management of Behçet's disease in a tertiary referral centre against guidelines from EULAR and the National Centres of Excellence
audits.st: EULAR guidelines and National Centres of Excellence guidelines for Behçet's disease (escalation and de-escalation of treatment)
audits.f: 26/50 had used anti-TNFalpha therapy and 9/50 IV cyclophosphamide; EULAR guideline followed least well by rheumatology; low adherence to the national guideline due to methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine use in less severe disease and failure to switch from IV to subcutaneous anti-TNFalpha (adherence figures given in a table only).

audits.t: P167 Pulmonary hypertension in patients with systemic sclerosis: an audit of screening practices, incidence and cost over 10 years
audits.tp: Pulmonary hypertension screening in systemic sclerosis
audits.st: Every SSc patient screened annually with echocardiography or NT pro-BNP (European Society of Cardiology)
audits.f: 65% screened, all by echocardiography.
audits.c: NT pro-BNP introduced as an adjunct to echocardiography in 2014.
audits.r2: 88% screened; 25% had echocardiogram and 83% NT pro-BNP; 63% screened by NT pro-BNP only.

audits.t: BSR guideline on the management of adults with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) 2018: baseline multi-centre audit in the UK
audits.st: BSR 2018 guideline for management of adults with SLE, NICE technology appraisal for belimumab and NHS England commissioning policy for rituximab
audits.f: 1021 episodes of care audited; low documented compliance (<60% of visits) for formal disease-activity assessment, reduction of drug toxicity and protection against comorbidities; prednisolone recorded in 497 (49%) visits, including 28.5% of visits with inactive disease.

audits.t: P003 An audit of the uptake of vaccinations against influenza, pneumonia and varicella zoster among rheumatology outpatients
audits.tp: Vaccination uptake in immunosuppressed rheumatology patients
audits.st: Public Health England, BSR and EULAR vaccination guidance; target 90% uptake; departmental vaccination advice in standard letter template
audits.f: Influenza 63/87 (72%); pneumococcus 61/87 (70%); zoster 7/12 (64%); vaccination advice in 24/126 (19%) clinic letters.

audits.t: P007 Service evaluation of the nurse-led telephone advice line in the wake of COVID-19: a report of audit and staff satisfaction
audits.tp: Rheumatology nurse advice line response times
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Multiple attempts needed to return the call in 19/97 (19.6%), of which 13/19 (68.4%) needed ≥2 nurses; first return attempt average 7.6 hours (range 0.1–27.7); time to conclude call average 12.7 hours (range 0.1–142.6); doctor advice needed in 18/97 (18.5%).

audits.t: P010 Management of fibromyalgia patients in secondary care: a retrospective audit
audits.st: 2017 EULAR recommendations for the management of fibromyalgia
audits.f: Before referral: pharmacological treatment 34/50 (68%), physiotherapy 5/50 (10%), psychological input 3/50 (6%); referred to multidisciplinary pain management programme 4/50 (8%).
audits.r2: Before referral: pharmacological treatment 71/82 (87%, p=0.008), physiotherapy 28/82 (34%, p=0.002), psychological input 16/82 (20%, p=0.03); referred to pain management programme 64/82 (78%, p<0.0001); all had pain and function assessed; psychosocial context assessed in 64/82 (78%); information given to 53 (65%).

audits.t: P013 Driving improvement through audit: impact of 2017 regional audit and survey upon giant cell arteritis services in 2020
audits.st: BSR guidance on giant cell arteritis (revised)
audits.f: 14/16 sites responded; 2 sites had a GCA pathway; routine steroid leaflets 6/14 (43%); 1 site had a GCA database; 8 had a steroid taper protocol.
audits.c: 2017 audit and survey results fed back to sites and regionally; sites introduced GCA pathways, temporal artery ultrasound, steroid leaflets and local QI.
audits.r2: 15/16 sites responded; 6 sites had a GCA pathway; temporal artery ultrasound 6/15 (40%); routine steroid leaflets 12/15 (80%); GCA database 4 (27%); steroid taper protocol 7.

audits.t: P016 When and how to deliver advice about self-management: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.tp: Self-management advice in early inflammatory arthritis
audits.st: NICE QS33 QS4: RA patients offered educational and self-management activities within 1 month of diagnosis
audits.f: All RA patients received written information at baseline; only 39 (71%) documented as given self-management advice at 3-month follow-up; 41 (56%) started DMARD within 6 weeks of referral.
audits.c: Driver diagrams with patient group input identified changes: agreed definition of self-management, patient activation measure, different delivery formats and expert patients.

audits.t: P017 Out of outlier status: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.tp: Early inflammatory arthritis time to assessment and DMARD start
audits.st: NICE QS33: QS2 seen within 3 weeks of referral; QS3 RA started on DMARDs within 6 weeks of referral
audits.f: 10% of all patients seen within 3 weeks; 7% of RA cohort (n=77) started DMARD within 6 weeks.
audits.c: Primary care referral guidelines, prompts for RF/CCP requests and changed antibody report wording, more triage and new appointment capacity (extra consultant, upskilled ESP), simpler booking, more drug education and monitoring clinic capacity, signposting to NRAS.
audits.r2: 54% seen within 3 weeks; 56% of RA cohort (n=73) started DMARD within 6 weeks.

audits.t: P019 Audit of prostanoid use in severe Raynaud’s and adherence to treatment of digital ulcers in patients with SSc NHSE pathway: commissioning policy cost analysis and alternative therapeutic pathway proposed
audits.tp: Digital ulcer treatment in systemic sclerosis
audits.st: NHS England 2015 commissioning policy pathway for digital ulcers in systemic sclerosis
audits.f: Prior trials: CCB 77.4%, ACEi/ARB 41.1%, fluoxetine 9.59%, sildenafil 87.1%, tadalafil 25.8%; 22.6% of SSc patients had tried bosentan; only 2 SSc patients (6.45%) had trialled all pathway drugs before prostanoid.

audits.t: P177 Management of patients with axSpA: an audit against the NICE diagnosis and management of adults with spondyloarthritis quality standard, QS170, and clinical practice guidelines
audits.st: NICE QS170 (MRI if no radiographic evidence, structured exercise programme, patient information) and clinical practice guidelines
audits.f: MRI in 18/19 (94.7%) with X-rays showing no sacroiliitis; education in 228/267 (85.4%); referral to structured exercise 217/259 (83.8%); first-line NSAIDs 246/248 (99.2%); 6-monthly renal monitoring on NSAIDs 80.3%; 12-week bDMARD response assessment 198/233 (85.0%).

audits.t: OA41 Audit of the rheumatology PIFU pathway at the UHMB Trust
audits.st: BSR draft guidance on patient-initiated follow-up
audits.f: 9/100 triggered a review; 8 received a nurse call-back within 48 hours; 1 needed urgent consultant review and was seen within 7 days; all 9 reverted to regular follow-up.

audits.t: P001 Audit on giant cell arteritis fast track clinic in Tayside
audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) GCA standards
audits.f: 70.8% seen by rheumatology within 24 hours; 50% with visual symptoms seen by ophthalmology within 24 hours; 89% given steroids within 24 hours; 80.8% had ultrasound or biopsy; written information, recurrence advice, CRP and bone protection documentation 100%.

audits.t: P011 Audit and Outcomes of Hydroxychloroquine Screening for Retinopathy in a Cohort of Patients with Rheumatological Conditions
audits.st: Royal College of Ophthalmologists 2018 guidelines on hydroxychloroquine dosing and retinopathy screening
audits.f: Of 86 eligible patients, 23% were prescribed a dose of >5mg/kg/day; 10% had eGFR <60; none on tamoxifen. 29 patients attended screening and none had HCQ retinopathy.

audits.t: P012 Cross-specialty audit of Infliximab prescribing at the Great North Children’s Hospital (GNCH)
audits.st: Local trust guidelines based on BSPAR guidance (rheumatology) and ESPGHAN guidelines (gastroenterology)
audits.f: 17 rheumatology and 17 age-matched Crohn's gastroenterology patients audited; specialties were not following all guidelines perfectly, particularly pre-treatment viral screening (detailed results in a table not supplied).
audits.c: Recommended development of cross-specialty infliximab guidance.

audits.t: P016 Steroid prescribing and risk of adrenal insufficiency: an audit of giant cell arteritis cases
audits.tp: Steroid emergency card and adrenal insufficiency advice
audits.st: National Patient Safety Alert (August 2020) on steroid emergency cards and adrenal insufficiency risk
audits.f: No patients given steroid emergency cards at first visit (4 during follow-up); 5/90 given written information on adrenal insufficiency risk at first visit; 1/90 given information on symptoms; none given sick day rules at first visit (9 during follow-up).
audits.c: Dedicated GCA clinics and improved follow-up, standardised written steroid information and personalised reduction plans, education sessions for medical and nursing teams, and electronic prescribing of emergency cards (being incorporated).

audits.t: P020 The impact of COVID-19: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.tp: Early inflammatory arthritis time to assessment and DMARD start
audits.st: NICE quality standard QS33 (QS2 and QS3), measured as being seen within 3 weeks of referral and starting DMARD within 6 weeks of referral
audits.f: 41% of all patients seen within 3 weeks of referral and 58% of RA patients started DMARD within 6 weeks, compared with 54% and 56% in year 2 (268 patients).

audits.t: P022 Audit of vitamin D and calcium level monitoring in sarcoidosis patients taking calcium and/or vitamin D supplements
audits.tp: Calcium and vitamin D monitoring in sarcoidosis
audits.st: Monitoring of serum calcium and vitamin D in sarcoidosis patients on calcium and/or vitamin D supplementation
audits.f: 46/102 (45%) had serum calcium and vitamin D measured in the community in the last 12 months.

audits.t: P026 Sugar rush: single-centre audit of screening and counselling for steroid-induced hyperglycaemia, based on the British Society for Rheumatology giant cell arteritis guideline
audits.tp: Glycaemic monitoring on glucocorticoids in giant cell arteritis
audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology GCA guideline: HbA1c monitoring and documented counselling on steroid-induced hyperglycaemia
audits.f: Baseline HbA1c checked in 32/60 (53%); counselling documented 7/60 (12%); hyperglycaemia detected 8/60 (13%).
audits.c: Results presented at a regional meeting to raise awareness and a GCA clinic was set up.
audits.r2: Baseline HbA1c checked in 28/30 (93%); counselling documented 9/30 (30%); hyperglycaemia detected 11/30 (36%).

audits.t: P138 Real-world incidence and management of hypocalcaemia after denosumab administration in patients with chronic kidney disease: a UK secondary-care based audit
audits.tp: Calcium monitoring after denosumab in renal impairment
audits.st: Local protocol: weekly calcium and renal function for 4 weeks after each denosumab injection if CrCl <35 ml/min
audits.f: 29/52 (56%) missed one or more post-injection blood tests, most often the 1st and 4th weekly checks. 18/54 (33%) developed hypocalcaemia; only 3 had adjusted calcium <2.0 mmol/l.

audits.t: P293 Tocilizumab for refractory or relapsing giant cell arteritis: audit data from the Bristol and Bath regional multidisciplinary meetings 2018-2021
audits.tp: Tocilizumab approval criteria in giant cell arteritis
audits.st: NHS England criteria (Blueteq) for tocilizumab in refractory or relapsing GCA; MDT discussion required before starting
audits.f: 38 cases discussed, 31 approved for tocilizumab; 100% of approved cases met criteria for refractory (n = 11) or relapsing (n = 20) disease.

audits.t: P009 Navigating giant cell arteritis (GCA) service during and post COVID-19 pandemic: an audit of GCA care at North Bristol NHS Trust against the BSR quality standards
audits.st: BSR quality standards for GCA
audits.f: Mean referral to specialist review 2.7 days; temporal artery biopsy 41%.
audits.c: Twice-weekly registrar-led hot clinics, ad hoc slots in on-call consultant clinics for GCA referrals, and increased vascular ultrasound capacity during the pandemic.
audits.r2: Mean referral to specialist review 1.6 days; all had vascular ultrasound; temporal artery biopsy 7.5%. 33% diagnosed and treated as GCA.

audits.t: P012 Using the BSR Lupus audit as a springboard to improve management of SLE in the outpatient clinic
audits.st: BSR national Lupus audit standards (11 standards) based on BSR Lupus guidelines
audits.f: 5/11 audit standards met.
audits.c: Nurse education and urine testing added to the clinic observation form; electronic SLE review form and electronic SLEDAI score introduced.
audits.r2: 4/11 standards met across all clinics; 9/11 in the specialist clinic. Urine testing rose from 22% (2020) to 90%. When the SLE review form was used, all standards were met apart from lipid testing and pregnancy discussion (79% vs standard 80%).

audits.t: P013 A three-year audit of dose tapering biologic medications in a rheumatology service
audits.st: ACR and EULAR guidance supporting biologic tapering; locally agreed eligibility criteria
audits.f: Patients tapered increased from 24 in 2019 to 51 in 2021; tapering failed in 7/116 (6%); estimated saving up to £170,000 per annum
audits.c: EHR records flagged to prompt shared decision-making discussion at routine appointments

audits.t: P020 Audit of bosentan use in Rapid Access to Digital Ulcer Clinic (RADUC) in systemic sclerosis: a single-centre experience
audits.tp: Digital ulcer treatment in systemic sclerosis
audits.st: NHS England clinical commissioning policy for sildenafil and bosentan in SSc digital ulceration (bosentan for severe vasculopathy or ≥3 digital ulcers; oral agents before IV prostanoids)
audits.f: All 21 had severe/≥3 digital ulcers; 20/21 started bosentan after inadequate response or intolerance to both sildenafil and iloprost. At 6 months (11/21), total ulcers fell from 5±2.2 to 2.7±2.2 (p < 0.05); 8/11 (72.7%) had fewer ulcers.

audits.t: P023 National care of patients with Polymyalgia Rheumatica: Audit of steroid usage from UK GP data - a cause for concern?
audits.st: BSR PMR guidelines: glucocorticoids for one to two years with taper; cumulative thresholds 0-6 months >2100mg, 7-12 months >1400mg, 13-18 and 19-24 months >910mg
audits.f: A considerable number of patients were prescribed glucocorticoids above recommended levels (figures given in a table not supplied).

audits.t: P110 Challenges of meeting NICE guidance for rheumatoid arthritis in the modern era: a service audit
audits.st: NICE NG100 rheumatoid arthritis annual review standards
audits.f: DAS28 documented 74.4% (253/340); erosions 42% (144/340); blood pressure 33% (113/340); mental health screen 7.9% (27/340); neck pain 14%; respiratory 21%; eye 21%; bone health 27.9% (95/340); AHP referral considered 38%; HAQ 22%.
audits.c: Planned digital RA annual review tool incorporating PROMs.

audits.t: P154 Real-world audit of patients with idiopathic inflammatory myositis-related interstitial lung disease in a European population
audits.tp: Interstitial lung disease screening in myositis
audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology guidelines for managing idiopathic inflammatory myositis (no target stated)
audits.f: 65% (46/70) of adult IIM patients screened for pulmonary involvement. 31% (22/70) had IIM-ILD; 21/22 had PFTs; 76.2% (16/22) had ILD changes on imaging.

audits.t: E002 Management of adults with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in 2021: a multi-centre audit within Wales as part of an ongoing quality improvement exercise
audits.st: 2018 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for the management of adults with SLE
audits.f: No widespread significant changes in care compared with 2019; blood pressure and urinalysis not consistently measured; 48% of consultations were virtual.

audits.t: E005 An audit of demographics, symptoms & investigations: Part of the survey of GCA in the SEHSCT during the COVID-19 pandemic
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: All had ESR and CRP; ANCA in 43 (3 positive); CT brain in 40; TA ultrasound once; CT-PET in 6; 70 TAB with 12 positive and 4 suggestive.
audits.c: Rapid access GCA pathway being designed

audits.t: E006 An audit showing the successful operation of a nurse-led gout clinic during the COVID-19 pandemic
audits.st: Clinic protocol based on BSR guidance; serum urate <360 µmol/L (<300 µmol/L with erosions or tophi)
audits.f: Mean serum urate 509 µmol/L at referral and 322 µmol/L at discharge; all offered and took prophylaxis (85.8% for 3–6 months); 95% had ≤2 flares; no ED attendances for gout.

audits.t: P004 Empowering the reproductive choices of patients with rheumatic disease: using the BSR 2022 pregnancy guidelines audit tool to evaluate pre-conception medication advice
audits.st: BSR 2022 guideline on prescribing drugs in pregnancy and breastfeeding (linked BSR audit tool)
audits.f: Antibody screening 70%; asked about wish to conceive 26%; contraception asked in 21% of those not wishing to conceive; referred to obstetric-rheumatology clinic 17%; appropriate pre-pregnancy drug counselling 22.8% of 35 on medication; none signposted to further information.

audits.t: P008 High response rate to Janus Kinase inhibitors after multiple biologic drug failures, across disease indications, in a District General Hospital: results from an audit of the prescribing, safety and efficacy of Janus Kinase inhibitor
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Side-effect discussion documented at baseline in <10%; 2% MACE and 3% herpes zoster; 36% discontinued; remission or significant reduction in disease activity in 64%.
audits.c: Recommended better patient education before starting treatment.

audits.t: P010 To establish compliance with British Society for paediatric and adolescent rheumatology (BSPAR) and the Royal College of Ophthalmology (RCOphth) guidelines for screening for uveitis in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) at a District General Hospital: a retrospective audit
audits.tp: Uveitis screening in juvenile idiopathic arthritis
audits.st: BSPAR/RCOphth 2006 uveitis screening guidelines
audits.f: Initial screen within 6 weeks 40/42 (95%); symptomatic seen within 1 week 4/13 (30%); screening after stopping DMARDs 9/13 (70%); ongoing screening 15/20 (75%).

audits.t: P081 Out-patient management of gout in secondary care: Results from the North West regional audit
audits.st: NICE, EULAR, BSR and MHRA gout guidelines
audits.f: Treat-to-target levels agreed in 49 (57%); cardiovascular risk tool used in 3 (3%); no patient with major cardiovascular disease on febuxostat; 16 (17%) no planned follow-up; 18 (78%) new patients appropriately referred; 15 (75%) started on first-line ULT; 11 (79%) allopurinol started at low dose; 10 (67%) given colchicine prophylaxis.

audits.t: E009 An audit looking into bisphosphonate co-prescription and compliance in patients with giant cell arteritis
audits.st: BSR giant cell arteritis guideline: consider pharmacological bone protection at presentation
audits.f: Bisphosphonate consideration documented at diagnosis in 96% overall (TOC 94%, MTX 91%, MONO 100%); compliance for recommended duration 88% overall

audits.t: E016 An audit on patient initiated follow up in rheumatology in Manchester Royal Infirmary
audits.st: NHS England PIFU guidance: stable inflammatory arthritis, face-to-face review within 2–4 weeks of contact, around 5% of patients on PIFU
audits.f: Only 22 (17%) met NHS England criteria; 0% seen within the recommended time after contact; 1.5% of department patients on PIFU (target 5%).

audits.t: E019 Management of idiopathic inflammatory myositis - a Northamptonshire audit of British Society for Rheumatology guidelines
audits.st: BSR guideline on idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (March 2022), 26 recommendations
audits.f: Steroids tapered 100%; DMARDs for muscle inflammation 91%; treatment for active skin disease 100%; ILD screening 100%; therapist-led exercise for active muscle disease 56%; psychological well-being formally considered 45%.

audits.t: E021 Patient initiated follow-up long term condition pathway audit
audits.st: Departmental PIFU-LTC standard operating procedure based on GIRFT guidance (entry and exclusion criteria, documentation standards, response to contacts)
audits.f: 81% (n = 42) met diagnostic entry criteria; 92% joined ≥12 months after diagnosis; 40% (n = 21) had no record of an information leaflet; 33% (n = 17) had no documented flare plan; contact to telephone review 1-3 days.

audits.t: E022 Audit on the baricitinib dose in elderly and patients with chronic kidney disease among a cohort of rheumatoid arthritis patients
audits.st: NICE guidance (2 mg daily if 75 years or older) and BNF (avoid if creatinine clearance <30 ml/min; reduce dose if 30–60 ml/min)
audits.f: Of 13 aged 75+ still on baricitinib, 10 on 2 mg and 3 on 4 mg; 4 of 7 started after 75 began on 4 mg; 14 of 16 with creatinine clearance 30–60 ml/min were at some point on 4 mg, 6 still on 4 mg

audits.t: OA13 Preliminary results from the National Axial Spondyloarthritis Society time to diagnosis audit: two years on
audits.tp: Time to diagnosis in axial spondyloarthritis
audits.st: NASS 'Act on Axial SpA' campaign target to reduce time to diagnosis to 12 months
audits.f: Mean total time to diagnosis 8 years (SD 8.91); median 4.7 years (IQR 9.25).

audits.t: P016 Audit on the use of avacopan in ANCA-associated vasculitis at a tertiary rheumatology centre
audits.tp: Glucocorticoid tapering with avacopan in ANCA vasculitis
audits.st: PEXIVAS glucocorticoid tapering protocol and local guideline (twice the PEXIVAS tapering rate)
audits.f: 50% tapered glucocorticoids in line with PEXIVAS; none followed the accelerated local guideline rate.

audits.t: P026 Enhancing care for giant cell arteritis: a closed-loop audit on adherence to Chelsea and Westminster Trust pathway guidelines
audits.st: Ambulatory Care Giant Cell Arteritis Fast Track Pathway Guidelines (Chelsea and Westminster Trust)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Staff education on the GCA pathway, results presented at trust ambulatory emergency care governance meeting, and streamlined documentation
audits.r2: GCA probability score calculated in 69% (21% improvement); TAUS within 72 h 85% (9% improvement); appropriate steroid dose 100% (29% improvement); appropriate bone protection 46% (41% increase).

audits.t: P128 Implications of newly established malignancy screening guidelines for idiopathic inflammatory myopathies: a multi-centre, international evaluation of clinical and economic impact by the Myositis Audit and Research Collaborative group
audits.st: IMACS guidelines for malignancy screening in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies
audits.f: Full IMACS screening panel received by 7.5% of high-risk, 6.6% of intermediate-risk and 27.5% of standard-risk patients; 9.1% of high-risk patients had annual screening for 3 years as recommended.
audits.co: Multinational (Australia, Brazil, Hong Kong and others)

audits.t: E012 Giant cell arteritis: single-centre, four-year audit of baseline and follow up glycaemic assessment in patients on corticosteroid treatment
audits.tp: Glycaemic monitoring on glucocorticoids in giant cell arteritis
audits.st: BSR GCA guideline: baseline HbA1c within two weeks of steroid start; wean steroids within 18 months
audits.f: Baseline HbA1c 32 (69.57%); HbA1c at least 3 months after starting steroids 36 (78.26%); both baseline and follow-up by rheumatology 17/46 (36.96%); steroids weaned within 18 months 31 (67.39%).

audits.t: E014 Audit on outpatient referrals done by primary care providers to the Rheumatology assessment at Airedale Hospital NHS Trust: are the new clinical prioritisation criteria required?
audits.st: GIRFT (Getting It Right First Time) guidance on rheumatology referrals
audits.f: 134 of 674 referrals rejected; 101/134 (75.3%) rejected as more appropriate for MSK/pain services or atypical for RMD; 52/134 (37.9%) advised further assessment or investigations in primary care.

audits.t: Current UK practice in pulmonary screening in paediatric connective tissue disease: UK multi-centre audit and proposed standards
audits.tp: Pulmonary screening in paediatric connective tissue disease
audits.st: Audit standards derived from national and international guidelines on pulmonary screening in juvenile CTD (proposed standards)
audits.f: Pulmonary involvement identified in 27/68 (39.7%) jSLE, 5/41 (12.2%) jDM, 4/7 (57.1%) jSSc and 3/12 (25.0%) jMCTD; 50% or fewer had regular assessment of pulmonary symptoms and signs during follow-up.

audits.t: OA24 Annual prescribing of biologic agents: a six-month audit of implementation and safety at Guy’s and St Thomas’ Rheumatology
audits.st: BSR guidance (at least 6-monthly review) and a local guideline for annual bDMARD prescribing
audits.f: 233/644 (36.2%) eligible patients switched to annual prescribing; 6/233 (2.6%) flared and 1/233 (0.43%) had a significant blood abnormality; 177 (43.1%) met criteria but were not switched.
audits.c: Local guideline moving suitable patients from 6-monthly to annual bDMARD prescriptions.

audits.t: P001 An audit on the management of Familial Mediterranean Fever in Malta
audits.st: EULAR 2016 recommendations for FMF management
audits.f: Initial follow-up within 6 months 54.1% (33); 3-monthly SAA/CRP with dose escalation 8.3% (2/24); 6-monthly monitoring 31.2% (19); SAA and CK on yearly bloods 20.9% and 12.5%; no 3-monthly SAA/CRP during dose reduction.

audits.t: P039 Audit into multi-disciplinary team care of haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
audits.st: GIRFT guidance on broad MDT input (rheumatology, haematology, infectious diseases, critical care) and local HLH guidelines
audits.f: MDT discussion in 26/34; 1/26 (4%) met guideline standards; 13/26 (50%) single-specialty discussions; median 10 days admission to MDT, 19/26 (73%) within 14 days.

audits.t: P040 An Audit of Menopause Assessment and Hormone Replacement Therapy Use in Rheumatology Patients
audits.tp: Menopause and HRT documentation in rheumatology
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Menopause status documented in 10/90 (11.1%) clinic letters; menopause discussed in 4/16 (25%) new patient appointments; HRT documentation accurate and concordant in 83/90 (92.2%); rheumatological diagnosis accurately coded in primary care record in 68/90 (75.6%).

audits.t: P078 Tertiary care centre audit of measles, mumps, rubella and varicella vaccination in children on immunomodulating therapy
audits.tp: Live vaccination in children on immunosuppression
audits.st: 2017 Public Health England / Green Book guidance supporting MMR and varicella vaccination on methotrexate and case-by-case after MDT assessment
audits.f: 81 vaccinations (38 VZV, 43 MMR) recommended by the vaccine MDT; 34/81 (42%) administered (20/38 VZV and 14/43 MMR).
audits.c: Recommended strengthening follow-up pathways, standardising communication and reinforcing primary care engagement.

audits.t: P099 National audit of England shows suboptimal compliance with ophthalmology recommendations for hydroxychloroquine retinopathy screening
audits.st: Royal College of Ophthalmologists guideline: annual retinopathy screening after 5 years of HCQ, or after 1 year if tamoxifen, eGFR <60 or dose >5 mg/kg/day
audits.f: Of 13,298 meeting screening criteria, 2,808 (21.1%) seen in ophthalmology in the previous 365 days; range 0% to 45.9% by ICB.

audits.t: P100 Ethnic disparities in NICE rheumatoid arthritis quality standard 33 attainment: data from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.tp: Early inflammatory arthritis time to assessment and DMARD start
audits.st: NICE RA quality standard 33: QS1 referral within 3 working days of primary care presentation; QS2 conventional DMARD within 6 weeks of referral
audits.f: QEHB QS1: 79% (115/146) White vs 21% (31/146) BAME referred within 3 days; QS2: 26.5% (27/102) BAME vs 73.5% (75/102) White. Nationally QS1 43% (12,561/29,417) White vs 47% (2,333/4,964) BAME; QS2 60% (723/1,204) BAME vs 57% (4,919/8,695) White.

audits.t: P101 Sustaining rehabilitation gains in rheumatoid arthritis: a six-month functional status audit guided by EULAR treat-to-target standards
audits.tp: Functional status follow-up after rheumatoid arthritis rehabilitation
audits.st: EULAR treat-to-target: disease activity and functional status monitored every six months
audits.f: 33/36 (92%) completed six-month functional follow-up; median EQ-5D 46 at admission, 65 at discharge, 62.5 at six months; median self-efficacy 3.4, 7.0 and 5.5.

audits.t: P141 Assessing the appropriateness and outcomes of antinuclear antibody testing requests in primary care: a retrospective audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 605 (19.67%) positive; 190 (31.57%) of positives referred; new CTD diagnosed in 38 patients; 314 (51.9%) of positives were 1/80 homogeneous.
audits.c: Recommended clearer testing guidelines and targeted education for primary care clinicians.

audits.t: P189 Giant cell arteritis: audit of a fast-track assessment pathway including the use of positron emission tomography-computed tomography as an early diagnostic tool
audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology audit tool standards for suspected GCA
audits.f: All reviewed within 3 days (95% by next day); all started on corticosteroids with FBC and ESR; all with visual symptoms given high-dose steroids and ophthalmology review (60% same day); 95% had baseline glucose, 75% vitamin D checked, 70% DEXA; of confirmed GCA, 54% had documented written information and 77% safety-netting advice.

audits.t: E019 Rheum for Improvement: an audit of the electronic referral system and referral quality of the rheumatology department, Glasgow Royal Infirmary, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde from 7th August 2024-31st October 2024
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 30.89% lacked examination findings; 69.10% no further investigations documented beyond haematological/radiological; 53.65% had no differential diagnosis documented.

audits.t: E056 Treat-to-target gout management: a full cycle audit of allopurinol therapy in primary care
audits.st: NICE gout guideline: titrate allopurinol to serum urate below 360 µmol/L with annual monitoring
audits.f: 68/141 had a urate level in the past 12 months; of these 40 (58.8%) had urate below 360 µmol/L or allopurinol increased. 6 had never had a urate level on EMIS.
audits.c: Clinician education on NICE treat-to-target guidance
audits.r2: 65/142 had a yearly urate; 57 (87.7%) managed in line with NICE. Six-fold decrease in patients with no urate ever recorded.

audits.t: E136 MRI requesting and reporting in axial spondyloarthritis: an audit against the ASAS guidance
audits.tp: MRI requesting and reporting in axial spondyloarthritis
audits.st: ASAS guidance on requesting and reporting MRI in suspected axial spondyloarthritis
audits.f: Requests: age in 11 (11.4%), sex in 6 (3.8%), HLA-B27 in 35 (22.2%), back pain duration in 30 (18.9%), suspected diagnosis in 149 (94.3%). Reports: bone marrow oedema mentioned in 128 (81.0%), fat metaplasia in 10 (6.3%), statement on whether 'in keeping with axSpA' in 98 (62.0%).

audits.t: E137 Obesity, comorbidity burden and weight management discussions in psoriatic arthritis patients referred for occupational therapy: a service audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean BMI 33.5 kg/m²; 38% BMI >35; only around half of letters for BMI >30 recorded weight, and none discussed weight management plans or referrals.
audits.c: Recommended training for rheumatology staff on raising weight and better BMI recording.

audits.t: E158 A closed cycle audit of assessment of suspected giant cell arteritis at North Middlesex University Hospital
audits.st: BSR and GIRFT guidelines for GCA assessment and management
audits.f: Steroids 34%; rheumatology referral 55%; temporal artery ultrasound 15%; CRP 92%; median time to eye clinic 2 days.
audits.c: Trust SDEC GCA pathway guideline, streamlined temporal artery ultrasound order on IT system, local teaching, pathway poster in clinic rooms and Southend GCA probability score.
audits.r2: Steroids 54%; rheumatology referral 77%; temporal artery ultrasound 77% (p < 0.001); CRP 100%; median time to eye clinic 1 day.

audits.t: P18 Audit on pre-methotrexate screening in a paediatric rheumatology centre
audits.st: BSPAR consensus guidance: check varicella immunity before methotrexate and immunise if non-immune; consider measles status and TB testing in high-risk patients
audits.f: Varicella status checked before methotrexate in 91 (89%), after starting in 7 and not checked in 4; 20 non-immune, of whom 16 were vaccinated; measles serology checked in 57 (31 before methotrexate); TB Quantiferon checked in 35 before and 39 after starting.

audits.t: P32 Kawasaki disease: learning points from 6 years of audit data from a large university teaching hospital
audits.st: RCPCH guidelines
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: P57 Ensuring safe and efficient prescribing: an audit of external prescription requests from the National Centre of Paediatric Rheumatology, Ireland
audits.tp: External prescription requests between clinic visits
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Parents gave a dose in 10/36 requests; charts available for 27; 21 had blood tests on hospital database in the last 3 months; 27 had clinic appointments in the preceding 6 months.
audits.c: Planned: prescription request form for parents detailing dose, route and latest blood results

audits.t: P58 A re-audit on the adherence to blood monitoring guidelines in paediatric rheumatology patients on methotrexate, etanercept and adalimumab after the introduction of a blood clerk in the team
audits.st: Blood monitoring guidelines for methotrexate, etanercept and adalimumab: starters must meet 6 criteria (frequency, FBC, LFTs, renal function, varicella and measles immunity); maintenance patients 4 criteria
audits.f: Over 60% of patients on methotrexate not monitored according to guidelines.
audits.c: A blood clerk was introduced to the team to chase patients for blood results.
audits.r2: 76/216 (35%) appropriately monitored, similar to the previous audit. Main failure was delayed blood timing (50% methotrexate, 65% maintenance biologics); missing varicella/measles immunity documentation in 42% of biologic starters.

audits.t:
Transfusion in critical care – a
                    <scp>UK</scp>
                    regional audit of current practice
audits.st: UK best practice: restrictive transfusion threshold of haemoglobin below 70 g/l in stable non-bleeding patients
audits.f: Median pre-transfusion Hb 73 (68-77 [53-106]) g/l; only 34% of episodes used a threshold below 70 g/l.

audits.t: Five‐year audit of adherence to an anaesthesia pre‐induction checklist
audits.st: Institutional airway (anaesthesia pre-induction) checklist; primary outcome proportion of wholly performed checklists
audits.f: Checklist completed in 57.3% overall; adherence improved from 48.3% in the first year to 66.7% by the fifth year (p < 0.001).

audits.t: Peri‐operative decisions about cardiopulmonary resuscitation among adults as reported to the 7th National Audit Project of the Royal College of Anaesthetists
audits.st: Current guidance: CPR should usually be attempted for cardiac arrest during anaesthesia and pre-existing DNACPR recommendations should be suspended
audits.f: 595 (3%) of 20,717 adults had a pre-operative DNACPR recommendation, of which 175 (29%) were suspended. Of 881 peri-operative cardiac arrests, 54 (6%) had a pre-operative DNACPR; 25 (46%) of these were formally suspended.

audits.st: Association of Anaesthetists' 2020 consensus guideline on peri-operative glucocorticoid management
audits.f: Of 219 on ≥5 mg prednisolone equivalents, 67 (31%) pre-operatively and 43 (20%) postoperatively supplemented according to guideline; overall compliance 19/219 (9%); 30/219 (14%) no supplementation; 28/58 (48%) on <5 mg received inappropriate supplementation.

audits.t:
Time critical diagnoses and transfers of patients with acute type A aortic dissection in the
                    <scp>UK</scp>
                    : national audit of current practice*
audits.tp: Type A aortic dissection diagnosis and transfer times
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median symptom onset to ED arrival 2.3 h (IQR 1.4–4.7); median ED arrival to start of surgery 9.5 h (IQR 6.1–18.2); delays in diagnosis and transfer in 158 (47.3%); initial misdiagnosis in 52 (15.6%).

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF PAEDIATRIC VANCOMYCIN DOSING
audits.st: Local paediatric vancomycin guideline: 100% correct starting dose, 90% levels at correct time, 80% third-dose troughs in range (10–15 mg/L), 90% appropriate action for out-of-range levels
audits.f: 100% correct starting dose; 90% of levels taken at the correct time; 33% of initial levels in range (a further 31% after dose change); 93% appropriate actions; three of six standards met.
audits.c: Suggested changing dosing frequency to four times a day or continuous infusion.

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF THE MANAGEMENT OF ACUTE PAIN IN CHILDREN
audits.st: Locally developed MDT standards: 80% of severe pain scores to get analgesia within 20 minutes and mild/moderate within 30 minutes with timely reassessment; 80% on regular analgesia to have pain scored at least 4-hourly; 90% on strong opioids co-prescribed naloxone
audits.f: Analgesia given in the same hour for 58% (34/59) severe and 30% (28/92) mild/moderate pain scores; pain reassessed within 60 minutes after 52% (37/71) and 34% (31/92) of administrations; 15/18 (83%) on regular analgesia assessed at least 4-hourly; of 11 on strong opioids 45% had no naloxone, 27% fully prescribed and 27% for respiratory depression only.
audits.c: Planned: specific timing guidance added to the revised guideline, with medical and nursing training sessions.

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF THE PAEDIATRIC EMPIRIC ANTI-INFECTIVE GUIDELINES AND ANTI-INFECTIVE DRUG DOSE TABLE FOR CHILDREN
audits.st: 90% adherence to empirical anti-infective guidelines; 90% indication recorded; 90% duration or review date recorded; 95% initial doses per children's dose table
audits.f: Guideline adherence 40/41 (98%); indication recorded 40/42 (95%); duration or review date recorded 26/42 (62%); initial doses per dose table 67/69 (97%).

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF WHETHER PRESCRIBED DOSES ARE MEASURABLE ON THE GRADUATIONS OF ONE ORAL SYRINGE
audits.tp: Measurable oral liquid doses in children
audits.st: Local dispensing standard: prescribed volumes measurable on the printed graduations of one oral syringe
audits.f: Electronic prescriptions: 61/257 (24%) not measurable; paper charts: 57/303 (19%) not measurable (p=0.19). 77 of 457 liquid doses needed up to 4% adjustment and 10 up to 9%; 19/560 (3.4%) needed measuring to two decimal places.
audits.c: Recommended dose rounding at prescribing and adding liquid strength information to local guidelines.

audits.t: AUDIT OF OXYGEN PRESCRIBING IN A CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL
audits.st: Local guidelines, 100%: all patients on oxygen have a prescription, target saturations, administration device and nurse signature within last 12 hours
audits.f: 0/14 had an oxygen prescription (13 patients receiving oxygen reported).
audits.c: New paediatric medication chart with an oxygen prescription section and a training package for doctors, nurses and pharmacists; awareness of initial audit results.
audits.r2: 4/18 had an oxygen prescription (22%), all medical patients; of these target saturations 100%, device 25%, nurse signature within 12 hours 100%.

audits.t: AUDIT OF PARACETAMOL PRESCRIPTIONS IN PAEDIATRIC SURGICAL PATIENTS
audits.st: Local 2012 perioperative pain guideline (dosing by ideal body weight) and BNFC; 100% compliance with weight and height documentation, ideal-weight dosing, separate IV prescribing and 48-hour IV-to-oral review
audits.f: Weight recorded on 84% of inpatient and 94% of discharge prescriptions; height never documented; IV/PO prescribed together in 32 inpatients; 20 of 52 on IV paracetamol not reviewed at 48 hours (only 3 appropriate).
audits.c: Feedback led to amended local guidelines in 2015 (dosing by lean body mass and ideal weight; maximum 75 mg/kg/day).

audits.t: THE DEVELOPMENT OF A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT SYSTEM TO MONITOR, ASSESS AND FEEDBACK PRESCRIBING ERRORS IN PAEDIATRIC INTENSIVE CARE
audits.st: Local Zero Tolerance prescribing standards
audits.f: Unit mean error rate 12.5%.
audits.c: Automated Excel spreadsheet producing individual prescriber feedback forms, plus posters and discussion at clinical governance meetings
audits.r2: Unit mean error rate 13.0%; in 7 prescribers with at least 5 items in both cycles, mean error rate fell from 15.3 (SD 14.6) to 9.4 (SD 7.3), p=0.29.

audits.t: CHILDREN'S WARFARIN CLINIC-AN AUDIT OF THE NEW PHARMACIST-LED TELEPHONE SERVICE BASED ON A UNIQUE COMPUTERISED SYSTEM COMPARED TO THE WARD BASED PAPER SYSTEM
audits.st: NPSA safety standards for warfarin dosing
audits.f: Original ward-based paper system: 44 patients, 1289 INRs; 11 patients (25%) lost to follow-up.
audits.c: Pharmacist-led telephone warfarin service using a computerised documentation system.
audits.r2: Pharmacist-led service: 73 patients, 1547 INRs; fully compliant with NPSA standards; none lost to follow-up; safety indicators not significantly different.

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF VANCOMYCIN PLASMA CONCENTRATIONS WHEN VANCOMYCIN IS ADMINISTERED BY CONTINUOUS INTRAVENOUS INFUSION IN NEONATES
audits.st: Desired vancomycin plasma concentration 15-25 mg/L
audits.f: 28% of concentrations within the therapeutic range.
audits.c: Switch to continuous intravenous vancomycin infusion (loading dose 15 mg/kg then 20-50 mg/kg/day by creatinine and corrected gestational age), based on another hospital's regimen.
audits.r2: 62% of 115 concentrations within range (60.8% first, 60% second, 65.6% subsequent); 71.3% within a 10% widened range.

audits.t: AN AUDIT TO ASSESS THE TIMINGS OF TTAS AND INPATIENT ORDERS IN PAEDIATRICS; FROM WRITING, TO SCREENING, TO DISPENSING, AND TO LEAVING DISPENSARY
audits.st: Trust KPIs: 85% of urgent items (TTAs) dispensed within 1 hour; 85% of non-urgent items (inpatient orders) within 3 hours
audits.f: TTAs (n=12): average 2 hours from logging in to checking (standard 1 hour); writing to screening averaged 1 hour 34 minutes. Inpatient orders (n=22): average 5 hours 51 minutes to leave dispensary (standard 3 hours). Standards not met.
audits.c: Proposed: additional labelling staff at peak times, IT review of dispensing system, induction teaching on sending TTAs to pharmacy

audits.t: P02 An audit of vancomycin dosing in the neonatal units
audits.st: Local neonatal vancomycin guideline; 100% adherence
audits.f: Correct initial dose 28/28 (100%); level taken at correct time 13/15 (87%); 19/31 levels (62%) within 10–20 mg/L; all 6 levels >20 mg/L had next dose held, but follow-up adjustment often suboptimal; 3 of 4 low levels not acted on.
audits.c: Guideline amended (single safe range 10–20 mg/L, doses adjusted on levels not age) and teaching sessions with worked examples planned for prescribers and nurses.

audits.t: P26 An audit of the use of amikacin for early onset sepsis in premature neonates in an inpatient neonatal unit
audits.st: Trust Neonatal Infection Guideline: 100% adherence to criteria, amikacin 15 mg/kg, level at 24 hours before second dose, further doses only if level <5 mg/L or on pharmacist advice
audits.f: 100% adhered to guideline criteria and 100% prescribed 15 mg/kg; 12 (24%) had no level at 24 hours; of 38 with 24-hour levels only 6 (16%) were <5 mg/L; 17/23 (74%) in range at 36 hours; 2 patients received doses despite levels >5 mg/L.
audits.c: Recommended change from 24-hourly to 36-hourly dosing; re-audit planned in one year.

audits.t: P34 Quality improvement project aimed at reducing gentamicin errors in neonates
audits.st: National Patient Safety Agency (NPSA) recommendations on gentamicin
audits.f: 18 gentamicin errors reported; 84% at prescribing and 16% at administration; 67% due to complexity of calculating a 36-hourly dosing interval.
audits.c: PDSA cycles from July 2017: simplified standardised dosing interval, updated local monograph with example prescription, posters in prescribing areas, MDT feedback session, guideline promotion and error monitoring, lower-risk alternative antibiotic in low-risk babies, and gentamicin prescribing exercise at new doctor induction.

audits.t: P37 Audit on the quality of documentation of paediatric prescriptions using electronic prescription charts
audits.st: Legal prescribing requirements (Medicines Act 1968), trust Medicines Management Policy; ten standards based on RCP Generic Medical Record Keeping Standards 2017
audits.f: 100% compliance for most demographics and prescription items and all fluid standards; allergy status 95% (severity 93%); weight 73%; antimicrobial indication 81% and duration 46%.
audits.c: Results presented locally and emailed to staff; recommended e-prescribing training and compulsory weight and allergy entry.

audits.t: P38 An audit to assess influenza vaccination uptake amongst asthmatic children in a city in the northwest of england
audits.tp: Influenza vaccination and asthma prescribing in children
audits.st: BTS/SIGN British guideline on the management of asthma 2016 for prescribing; influenza vaccine uptake
audits.f: 148 (31.2%) had flu vaccination; 194/297 (65.3%) prescriptions followed BTS guidelines.

audits.t: P39 Continuous vancomycin dosing: an audit and evaluation
audits.st: Local vancomycin prescribing and therapeutic drug monitoring guidance
