audits.f: Only 7/30 (23.33%) tested within the last year; 2 (6.667%) new hyperprolactinaemia diagnoses, both reviewed and treated within one month. No audit standards were met.
audits.c: New risk-stratified hyperprolactinaemia guidance developed; re-audit planned for 2020.

audits.t: An audit: fitness to drive assessment in inpatients of general adult and old age psychiatry
audits.st: Fitness to drive assessed and documented on admission and discharge, with patient education on DVLA duty
audits.f: 18/49 patients had physical health screening before medication initiation (fitness to drive figures not given).

audits.t: Assessment and Management of Eating Disorders at Community CAMHS in South Lanarkshire: A Quality Improvement Project

audits.t: Substance Misuse History Documentation at Admission to Secure Rehabilitation Ward Audit

audits.st: Electronic admission documentation of substance use history

audits.r2: ACE-III scores more accurate (figures not reported).

audits.st: NICE oral health quality standards: mouth care needs assessed on admission, recorded in care plan, and support for twice-daily tooth cleaning and denture care

audits.t: Audit Review of GP Referrals to Perinatal Mental Health Team – Emphasis on Medication
audits.tp: GP referrals to perinatal mental health
audits.st: not reported

audits.st: Best practice recommendations for initiation and monitoring of naltrexone

audits.t: Audit on Management of Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms Among Dementia Patients in Humber Older People's Mental Health Services
audits.st: NICE: non-pharmacological before pharmacological management; antipsychotics started low and slow; follow-up at least 6 weeks after starting

audits.t: Audit on PRN Prescriptions in Adult Inpatient Female Ward

audits.f: PRN reviewed in last 7 days 25%; oral and IM grouped 7.2%; minimum dose documented 10.7%; maximum 24-hour dose 100%; indication 100%.

audits.st: Mental Health Act guidance on CTO paperwork completion and renewal hearings
audits.f: CTO3 paperwork missing in 2 cases; one tribunal hearing missed; one CTO lapsed; remaining patients had regular timely hearings.

audits.t: Audit of Psychotropic Polypharmacy Amongst Inpatients in East Suffolk
audits.st: not reported

audits.st: BNF and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines antipsychotic dosage; HDAT monitoring form for each patient on HDAT
audits.f: 166 (64.6%) on antipsychotics; 2 (1.2%) discharged on HDAT, of whom one did not have the monitoring form completed.

audits.t: Audit of Annual Blood Tests for Patients on Antipsychotic Medications in the Recovery Team
audits.st: NICE and Maudsley guidelines: annual FBC, U&E, eGFR, lipids, LFT, HbA1c/glucose and prolactin where required; compliance 80% or above recommended

audits.c: Recommendations to existing monitoring services and liaison to set up a dedicated physical health clinic (recruitment under way); re-audit planned.

audits.st: NICE PH56: test and replace vitamin D in adults at high risk of deficiency
audits.f: No patient had vitamin D tested (0%).

audits.r2: Compliance maintained at 90% in the third round.

audits.t: Compliance With a Biopsychosocial Assessment Template When Assessing Presentations of Self-Harm or Suicidal Ideation by Liaison Psychiatry Practitioners in Dorset Healthcare: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: NICE NG225: comprehensive biopsychosocial assessment for self-harm or suicidal ideation, using standardised template headings
audits.f: Presenting Situation 100%; Mental State Examination 98%; Risk Summary 98%; Psychiatric Formulation 92%; Social Situation 81%; Physical Health History 75%; Safeguarding Concerns 71%; Carer/Parent's Understanding 40%.

audits.t: A Clinical Audit of ECT Documentation in NHS Grampian
audits.st: NICE guidance on ECT: documented risk/benefit assessment including anaesthetic risk and cognitive impairment, patient information leaflet, consultation of advocate
audits.f: Indication documented 100%; RCPsych leaflet received 50%; risk/benefit discussion documented 50%; specific side effects discussed 50%

audits.t: An Initial Audit of Delirium Detection and Management in an Intensive Care Setting
audits.st: Trust guidance on delirium screening (CAM-ICU), documentation and management
audits.f: 20/81 had delirium. CAM-ICU documentation incorrect in 25% of these; behaviour monitored in 15%; 0% had a complete This is me document; sensory aids unavailable for 50%. Delirium formally diagnosed in 40%, type documented in 15%; 8 had a specific management plan; non-pharmacological management not documented.

audits.t: Audit of the Completion Rate of BPD Admission Checklist for the Hospital Admitted Service Users With EUPD
audits.st: Trust BPD admission checklist completed at admission
audits.f: 0/60 admissions had a completed BPD checklist.

audits.t: An Audit to Assess Nicotine Management on a Mental Health Rehabilitation Unit in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.tp: Smoking cessation in mental health inpatients
audits.st: Mersey Care Nicotine Management Guidelines (SA20)
audits.f: Smoking status recorded 47 (92%); 26/28 (93%) smokers offered support on admission; 24/31 (77%) offered support at regular intervals; 20/28 (71%) offered NRT; 5/31 referred to Nicotine Dependence Treatment Advisor.
audits.c: Action plan: reminders via team meetings and emails, completion of physical health nursing proforma, and posters on the referral pathway

audits.t: Audit of the Use of Outcome Measures Within Child and Adolescent Mental Health Outpatient Services in Rotherham, Doncaster and South Humber NHS Foundation Trust
audits.st: Trust Promise 16: collate and compare outcomes; audit standards on use of outcome measures

audits.c: Planned: use SystmOne to send outcome measures to patients' mobile devices and inform staff of expected use; re-audit in 2024.

audits.t: An Audit on Telephone Referrals to Beechcroft, a Step 5 Regional Child and Adolescent Mental Health Inpatient Unit
audits.st: 7 criteria of necessary referral information (identifiers, referrer, location, legal status, presenting symptoms, working diagnosis, risks warranting admission)
audits.f: Overall 75.2% of criteria met. Identifiers and referrer 100%, presenting symptoms 95%, risks 79%, legal status 74%, location 68%, working diagnosis 11% (2/19).
audits.c: Planned: in-hours bed manager appointed and a standardised referral proforma to be developed; re-audit planned.

audits.t: Audit on Discharge Summaries From General Adult Inpatient Units to Primary Care at Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
audits.st: Professional Record Standards Body and RCPsych guidelines on discharge summary availability, timeliness and content
audits.f: 28/148 (18.9%) had no completed discharge summary, 14 (9.4%) of whom were out-of-locality patients. Mean time from discharge to summary availability 12.7 days. Most summaries contained all relevant information.
audits.c: None reported yet; recommendations: bed management to notify parent teams promptly, medical secretaries to monitor admissions register and prompt juniors, and business intelligence monthly reports of missing summaries. Re-audit planned.

audits.t: Audit of Documentation of Lifestyle Medicine Factors in the Leicestershire Early Intervention Psychosis Team Clinic Letters
audits.tp: Lifestyle advice in mental health care
audits.st: Gold standard: all seven pillars of lifestyle medicine explored at each medical review
audits.f: For all domains 'not mentioned' was most common, ranging from 48.6% to 70.8%.
audits.c: Findings shared with team, educational poster created and electronic system being adapted to record lifestyle factors (re-audit planned in 12 months).

audits.t: Psychiatric Emergency Bleep Documentation Enhancement Audit
audits.st: 90% documentation compliance using a new checklist
audits.f: Psychiatric team documentation 44%; ward nursing documentation 65%; medical ward doctor documentation 39%; appropriate calls 65%.

audits.r2: Documentation 90%; ward nursing documentation 83%; medical ward doctor documentation 57%; appropriate calls 74%.

audits.t: An Audit of the Prescribing and Monitoring of Antipsychotic Medication in an Older Adult Inpatient Psychiatric Ward Using NICE Guidance [CG178] Psychosis and Schizophrenia in Adults: Prevention and Management
audits.st: NICE CG178 (1.3.5.1, 1.3.6.1–1.3.6.4): shared choice of antipsychotic, baseline investigations, ECG, therapeutic trial, systematic monitoring
audits.f: Benefits discussed 9/19 (47%); side effects discussed 5/21 (23%). Baseline HbA1c, weight, pulse and BP 100%; lipids 86%; prolactin 77%; fasting glucose 38%; movement disorder assessment 22%; waist circumference 0%. ECG offered 94%. Rationale recorded 86%. Monitoring: glycaemic control 57%, movement disorders 14%, side effects 13%.

audits.t: An Audit of the Consistency and Quality of Letters From Choice Appointments in CAMHS South Edinburgh
audits.st: Standards derived from the CAPA Book and CAMHS South Choice Handbook (12 letter content and process standards, including maximum two sides of A4 and sent within two weeks)
audits.f: Current concerns 92%, background 96%, patient goals 40%, clinician impression 62%, choices discussed 22%, choices made 100%, self-help agreed 52%, services required 100%, maximum two sides of A4 50%, copy to patient 88%, copy to referrer 100%, sent within two weeks 72%.

audits.t: Audit on Antidepressant Prescribing; Documentation of Indication; and Compliance With EIPN Standards in Medication Review, at Hailsham Early Intervention in Psychosis Service
audits.st: Diagnosis recorded alongside each antidepressant prescription; EIPN guidance that psychotropic medication is reviewed every 6 months
audits.f: 33 patients (37%) prescribed an antidepressant; 25 (76%) had a recorded indication; 67 patients (84%) had a medical review within 6 months

audits.t: Keeping Up Standards: An Audit of Adherence to Admission Standards on Acute Mental Health Wards in NHS Lanarkshire

audits.r2: Admission statement completed in 90%; MSE 91%; risk assessment 59%; where the proforma was used (57%) all components present in 97-100%.

audits.t: Quality of Adult Inpatient Discharge Planning and 3 Day Follow Up – a Regional Audit

audits.t: A Complete Audit Cycle of the Recording of the Baby's and Their Siblings' Age, Date of Births and Due Dates of Pregnant Mothers During the Initial Assessment Process for Patients Presenting to a Community Perinatal Mental Health Services
audits.st: RCPsych Standards for Community Perinatal Mental Health Services 5th Edition (2020), Section 5: record baby's age, date of birth and mother's due date at initial assessment

audits.t: Evaluation of the Clinical Significance of Assessing Previous Gambling Problems Before Initiating Antipsychotic Treatment: An Audit
audits.tp: Gambling risk and dopaminergic medication screening
audits.st: NICE: 100% of patients started on antipsychotics asked about previous gambling history

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Dementia Diagnosis and Management – According to Disease Severity

audits.f: Severity documented in only 7% (all moderate), 93% generic diagnosis; 46/60 on medication, all on monotherapy; 46 completed the diagnostic pathway.

audits.t: A Re-Audit of Physical Health Monitoring of Day-Care Patients in the Adult Eating Disorder Service at Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
audits.st: NICE guidelines and MEED guidance: weight, height, BMI, pulse, sitting/standing BP and temperature every attendance; bloods and ECG by BMI schedule

audits.t: Evaluating Adherence to Rapid Tranquilization Protocols in Psychiatric Emergencies: An Audit of a Tertiary Care Facility in Pakistan

audits.t: Identifying Perimenopausal Symptoms in Women Diagnosed With Depression: A Focused Audit at a Tertiary Care Hospital

audits.t: Monitoring Initiation and Administration of Covert Medication(s) for Service Users in Amber Ward of Millbrook Mental Health Unit, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust: A Re-Audit of Compliance With Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines in Psychiatry

audits.t: Driving in Home Treatment Teams: Are We Talking About It Enough? An Audit Covering Kingston and Richmond Boroughs in South West London and St George's NHS Trust
audits.st: DVLA advice on driving and notification during changes in mental health condition
audits.f: 17.7% had documented driving discussion.

audits.t: A Re-Audit of the Assessment of the Nutritional Status of Patients Admitted to the General Adult Inpatient Wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.st: Mersey Care Nutrition and Hydration Policy: MUST within 72 hours of admission and Nutrition Screening Tool Care Plan completed

audits.t: An Audit of Baseline Physical Health Monitoring in Patients Under the Care of Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust Who Are Commenced on Lithium
audits.st: National guidance on pre-lithium checks (weight/BMI/waist, TFTs, calcium, eGFR), POMH lithium audit

audits.t: An Audit of Whether Patients on the General Adult Inpatient Wards and the PICU in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust Who Are Prescribed High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy Are Being Monitored as per Trust Policy
audits.st: Trust HDAT policy: 13 baseline physical health assessments and cardiovascular assessment before starting HDAT; NICE advice that doses above BNF range are justified and recorded
audits.f: Baseline assessments completed on 226 (81%) of eligible occasions and not on 54 (19%), excluding 98 refusals; cardiovascular assessment before HDAT in 12/29 (41%).

audits.t: An Audit of Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Risk Assessment in an NHS Trust Mental Health Inpatient Setting
audits.tp: VTE risk assessment in psychiatric inpatients
audits.st: NICE NG89: VTE risk assessment on admission or first consultant review, reassessment, and prophylaxis where indicated

audits.t: Supported Employment Programmes for People With Psychosis or Schizophrenia – Full Cycle Audit
audits.st: NICE CG178 1.5.8 (offer supported employment to people with psychosis or schizophrenia who wish to work) and NG181 1.8.9 (facilitate alternative educational or occupational activities)
audits.f: Supported employment offered to 35% of the non-working sample; alternative educational or occupational options offered to 26%.
audits.r2: Employment status documented in 97%; supported employment offered to 38%; alternative educational or employment options offered to 47%.

audits.t: Re-Audit of the Monitoring of National Early Warning Scores 2 (NEWS2) in Old Age Patients
audits.st: Trust Standard Operating Procedure and Physical Health Policy for NEWS2 assessment, recording and escalation, aligned with NICE standards

audits.r2: NEWS2 chart completed on admission for 33/35; demographics, date, time and assessor name 100%; all observations and NEWS scores correct; weekly NEWS in 31/35 (rest had documented justification); NEWS 1–4 reviewed by nursing staff in 20/21; all scores >4 escalated to medical staff.

audits.t: Prescribing Practice of Citalopram and Escitalopram in Older Adults Following the 2014 MHRA Guidance of Associated QTc Prolongation: A Clinical Audit
audits.tp: Citalopram and escitalopram dosing and QTc in older adults

audits.t: Improving Health System Engagement in Patients With Substance Use Disorders: Audit of Care Plans in the National Drug Treatment Centre

audits.r2: GP registration on care plan 93%; up-to-date medical card 45%; status unknown 44%; medical card number displayed 55%.

audits.t: A Clinical Re-Audit (Cycle 1) on the Monitoring and Management of Antipsychotic-Induced Hyperprolactinaemia
audits.st: SWYPFT Trust standards, NICE guidelines and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition); target 100% prolactin monitoring
audits.f: Prolactin monitored in 41%.

audits.t: Audit of Resuscitation Equipment in a Mental Health Setting – Resulting in Trust-Wide Action
audits.tp: Resuscitation and physical health equipment on psychiatric wards

audits.f: 7/10 locations did not meet standards (missing or expired adrenaline, suction, oxygen masks); 4/10 wards had not completed the weekly checklist; 70% of staff-completed checklists were incorrect.

audits.t: Prolactin Monitoring for Inpatients on Antipsychotic Drugs: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: NICE: prolactin checked 6 months after starting then every 12 months, with enquiry about symptoms (not required for aripiprazole, clozapine, quetiapine, olanzapine under 20 mg)

audits.t: Audit of Non-Pharmacological and Rapid Tranquilisation Practices in Managing Distress Among Older Adults: A Comparative Study in Inverness Hospitals
audits.st: Local protocols for managing distress in older adults (non-pharmacological approaches and rapid tranquilisation)
audits.f: Nurses consistently used non-pharmacological de-escalation before RT, in line with the local protocol; physical restraint only used where there was risk, by trained staff; junior doctors, especially in AMU, had limited understanding of the RT protocol.

audits.t: Audit of Compliance With Stopping the Overprescribing of People With Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC) and Intellectual Disability (STOMP) Within the Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) in Warrington, Mersey Care NHS

audits.t: Audit of Electroconvulsive Therapy Service Provision in Lincolnshire Partnership Foundation Trust: Current Standards and Adherence to National Guidance

audits.t: Monitoring of Blood Clozapine Levels After a Change in Smoking Status for Patients Treated With Clozapine: A Clinical Audit From Hull Community Mental Health Team

audits.t: Are We Monitoring Our Lithium Patients as Well as We Should be? A Two-Cycle Audit Evaluating Lithium Clinic Documentation in a District General Hospital in Wales

audits.t: Assessing Adherence to Antipsychotic Prescribing and Monitoring Guidelines in a Psychiatric Unit for Older Adult Females in Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust (KMPT): A Retrospective Audit

audits.t: Re-Audit of Physical Health Equipment Available at the Mount Old Age Psychiatric Hospital
audits.tp: Resuscitation and physical health equipment on psychiatric wards

audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An Audit of Patients Who Did Not Attend Appointments in the East Lancashire Memory Assessment Service
audits.st: Estimated NHS outpatient non-attendance rate of 7.6% (comparator)
audits.f: 4 DNAs among 3 patients out of 99 appointments offered; DNA rate 4%. No DNAs for medication monitoring appointments.

audits.t: Assessment and Management of Substance Misuse Among Patients With Psychosis at a Mental Health Inpatient Unit in CNTW NHS Foundation Trust: An Audit
audits.tp: Substance misuse screening in mental health patients
audits.st: NICE CG120 Coexisting severe mental illness (psychosis) and substance misuse

audits.t: Initial Audit Investigating Physical Health Screening and Management of Neuropsychiatric Manifestations in Parkinson’s Disease (PD), Parkinson’s Disease Dementia (PDD) and Dementia With Lewy Bodies (DLB) on the Mental Health Services for Older Persons (MHSOP) Wards
audits.tp: Physical health screening in Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Antipsychotics considered in 11/11 (100%) with psychosis; bloods in 20/24 (83%); ECG before antipsychotic or cholinesterase inhibitor in 21/24 (88%); cholinesterase inhibitors considered in 13/17 (76%); dopaminergic therapy optimised in 8/18 (44%); PD specialist advice sought in 5/24 (21%).

audits.t: Re-Audit of Discontinuation Plans on Discharge for Prescribed Hypnotics in General Adult Inpatient Services
audits.st: Discharge summaries to include hypnotic medication review and specific discontinuation plan for the GP; target 100% compliance
audits.f: 0% compliance on two wards: no discharge summaries had a hypnotic medication review or discontinuation plan.
audits.c: Implementation of previous audit recommendations (details not reported).
audits.r2: Across six wards, 56.25% included a medication review for hypnotics and 18.75% a specific discontinuation plan.

audits.t: Audit of Local Clinical Governance in London & South Region – 2025
audits.st: NHS England Clinical Governance Framework (2022) and local STEELL agenda standards
audits.f: Qualitative findings only: progress in safety, patient experience and activities; improvement needed in digital tracking of engagement and MDT participation in governance meetings (no figures given).

audits.t: DNACPR Documentation Audit on Old Age Psychiatry Wards in Aneurin Bevan University Health Board (ABUHB) in South Wales
audits.tp: DNACPR and ceilings of care documentation
audits.st: All-Wales DNACPR policy for adults (2015, revised 2024)
audits.f: Decision date missing in 2 forms; not signed with date and time in 1; not documented in clinical notes in 10; discussion with patient in 9; discussion with IMCA/attorney or family in 20; appropriate signatures in 17; 7 not countersigned in section 6.

audits.t: Audit of the Ward Environment in an Inpatient Autism Unit
audits.st: Gold Standard Environmental Standards for LD and ASD inpatient hospitals and QNLD standards (22 parameters)
audits.f: Both wards met 15/22 parameters and failed 7, including no consultation with autistic people on sensory spaces, no patient/family feedback, insufficient autism training for all staff, no soft furnishings, no odour control and no unscented products.

audits.t: Audit on Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Assessment in Adult Inpatient Wards on Admission
audits.st: Local Trust VTE assessment policy (standard 100%)
audits.f: VTE assessment on admission 68%; questionnaire completed correctly 66.6%; examination findings documented 63.4%; reassessed at consultant review 1.8%; at-risk patients reassessed within 24 hours 33.3%; thromboprophylaxis offered when indicated 100%.

audits.t: Ensuring Comprehensive Care: An Audit on Physical Parameter Monitoring in Children and Adolescents With ADHD on Medication
audits.st: Established standards for monitoring weight, height, blood pressure and heart rate on ADHD medication
audits.f: 46/50 had blood pressure, pulse, height and weight measured at every appointment; 1 had no height checks; 1 had no blood pressure or pulse at follow-up; 2 referred for shared care.

audits.t: Evaluating PRN Medication Prescribing Practices in Mental Health Services: A Comparative Audit Following a Serious Incident
audits.st: 13 predefined PRN prescribing standards including generic naming, dose intervals, BNF limits and regular reviews
audits.f: Minimum dose interval 64.5%; maximum dose 96.7%; ward round reviews 3.2%; discontinuation of unused PRN 0%; review of regularly used PRN 0%; regular vs PRN use documented 33.3%.
audits.r2: Minimum dose interval 93.5%; maximum dose 100%; ward round reviews 64.5%; discontinuation of unused PRN 22.2%; review of regularly used PRN 28.5%; regular vs PRN use documented 44.4%.

audits.t: Audit of Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT) Service Provision: Current Practices and Adherence to Guidelines at Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore, Pakistan
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists ECT guidelines (consent, vital signs, monitoring of clinical response and cognitive side effects)
audits.f: Consent forms completed 100% and ongoing consent checked for all; right to withdraw consent explained to none; vital signs robustly documented; no validated rating scale used; response between sessions assessed in 45%; no documentation of cognitive side-effect assessment.
audits.c: Recommended updating consent forms to include right to withdraw, culturally validated assessment tools and re-audit in one year.

audits.t: ADHD in Intellectual Disability Audit: Diagnosis, Medication and Monitoring
audits.st: NICE guidance on ADHD medication monitoring in the past 6 months
audits.f: Weight measured in last 6 months 83%; pulse 76.5%; blood pressure 64%.

audits.t: Audit on Blood Tests Performed by Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team North East Kent (NEKCRHTT): Clinical Indications, Current Practice and Recommendations
audits.tp: Blood test requesting appropriateness in mental health
audits.st: Trust protocol for requesting blood tests, with documented clinical indication when deviating
audits.f: Trust policy not followed in 33.3% of cases, mostly TFT, folate and B12 requested without documented indication.
audits.c: Trust policy poster made accessible in clinical areas, prescriber awareness of the policy, and documentation of indication when deviating from policy.
audits.r2: Only 13.3% of cases did not follow the policy; documentation of rationale improved.

audits.t: Shots in Practice: An Audit of Depot Antipsychotics in Pakistan’s Outpatient Psychiatry Department
audits.st: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition) for long-acting injectable antipsychotics
audits.f: All patients on fluphenazine decanoate with a concurrent second antipsychotic (100% polypharmacy); 78% informed of side effects; none had post-injection observation; no test doses given; no baseline ECG or physical health assessment; fluphenazine used in rapid tranquillisation.

audits.t: An Audit of Metabolic Monitoring Compliance in Patients Initiated on Antipsychotics Across General Adult Wards in the East Midlands
audits.st: Lester Tool: baseline BP, HbA1c/glucose, lipids, lifestyle review and weight within one week of initiation, then weekly weight for six weeks
audits.f: Baseline BP 89.5%, HbA1c/glucose 65.8%, lipids 57.9%, lifestyle review 55.3%, weight 36.8%; 5.9% had full weekly weight follow-up and 41.2% none within six weeks.
audits.c: Recommended awareness of baseline bloods, electronic record alerts for weekly weights and a refusal drop-down, and re-audit.

audits.t: Tower Hamlets Community Learning Disability Service: Sodium Valproate Audit for Male Patients With Learning Disabilities
audits.st: Latest guidance: valproate not recommended for men under 55 unless no alternative, with completed Risk Acknowledgement Form
audits.f: 25 men on valproate (16 under 40); 10/25 had completed the risk acknowledgement form; 11 received valproate from other services and 4 were pending; 2 took over 2000 mg per day.

audits.t: Section 17 Leave Utilisation and Outcomes in Acute Adult Psychiatric Inpatients: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.st: HPFT Section 17 Leave of Absence Policy
audits.f: 157 leave episodes; incidents during leave 8.8%.
audits.c: Leave feedback template completed by the safety nurse at the end of each shift to record leave outcomes.
audits.r2: 137 leave episodes; documented leave outcomes up by 13.2% and documentation of what went well up by 50.3%; incidents during leave 0%.

audits.t: An Audit of the Use of a Ligature Assessment Tool in the Reporting of Ligature Incidents in a Regional Women’s Medium Secure Unit
audits.st: Recording of the 15 criteria of the Ligature Assessment Tool in ligature incident reports
audits.f: 19% of reports recorded 11 or more criteria.
audits.c: No specific intervention (such as education or promotion) between the third and fourth cycles; the Ligature Assessment Tool had been introduced in 2020.
audits.r2: 37% of reports recorded 11 or more criteria; 19 (35%) recorded all 15 criteria.

audits.t: AUDIT^2 – A Clinical Audit of the Alcohol Assessment and Management in the Southern Gambling Service – First Round Results
audits.st: NICE CG115, Department of Health and Social Care and Royal College of Physicians guidance: full AUDIT if AUDIT-C at least 5, brief intervention for scores 5–10, advice and signposting for 11 or more
audits.f: AUDIT-C and EWAC completed 100%; full AUDIT 0%; brief intervention documented in 7% of higher-risk; 1 (25%) possibly dependent patient signposted; none given advice on avoiding abrupt cessation
audits.c: Recommended: full AUDIT for AUDIT-C 5 or more, staff upskilling in brief intervention, regional alcohol services directory, psychoeducation materials

audits.t: Delays in the Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Pathway: An Audit of Wait Times for Initial Assessment and Post-Diagnosis Support in Greater Preston
audits.st: NICE: first appointment within 13 weeks of referral; follow-up within 6 weeks of diagnosis
audits.f: Seen within 13 weeks: 18.9% of school-age and 16.7% of preschool children; follow-up within 6 weeks: 18.9% of school-age and 20.8% of preschool children.

audits.t: Audit of Rapid Tranquillisation Prescribing and Monitoring Practices at Rohallion Medium and Low Secure Forensic Psychiatry Unit, Murray Royal Hospital, NHS Tayside
audits.st: Local and national guidance: 100% documented plan for oral and IM as-required medication; 100% offered oral before IM; 100% side-effect monitoring within 1 hour of rapid tranquillisation
audits.f: 38 (81%) had as-required medicines prescribed; 24 (63%) of these had a documented plan; reasons for IM medication and side-effect monitoring documented 25.42% of the time. Standards 1, 2 and 3 not met.
audits.c: Action plan: work with clinical team and pharmacist to improve documentation, and add headers to online assessment templates. Re-audit planned.

audits.t: ‘At Risk Mental State’: An Audit of Tier 3 Clinical Standards
audits.tp: At-risk mental state recognition and management
audits.st: NICE recommendations and NHS England guidance on ARMS management in children and young people
audits.f: Significant variation in clinicians' confidence and knowledge of ARMS identification criteria and management.
audits.c: 30-minute teaching seminar on ARMS criteria, CAARMS, psychological and family interventions and guidance against antipsychotic use, delivered in CPD slots.
audits.r2: Improved clinician confidence in ARMS identification and management; all participants wanted further support.

audits.t: Genetic Testing in Psychiatry for Individuals With Intellectual Disabilities: An Audit of Current Practice
audits.st: Established criteria for genetic testing in unexplained moderate, severe or profound intellectual disability
audits.f: 39 had moderate to profound ID; 20.5% had a confirmed genetic diagnosis; genetic testing mentioned in 25.6% of those with moderate or severe ID; only one patient referred for testing by this team.
audits.c: Planned: targeted education for the team, sharing the Clinical Genetics referral protocol and a prompt in initial assessments.

audits.t: Audit of Discharge Summary Completion: Identifying Barriers and Implementing Solutions to Improve Timeliness
audits.st: Discharge summary completed within 7 days of discharge
audits.f: Ward 3: 0 of 11 completed within 7 days; Ward 4: 23% of 13 met the target.
audits.c: Proposed dedicated 4-hour weekly slot for junior doctors, assigning a responsible doctor at discharge and a quiet onsite workspace.

audits.t: Audit to Assess the Availability of Electrocardiogram (ECG) Machines on the Inpatient Units at Leeds and York Partnership Foundation Trust (LYPFT)
audits.tp: Resuscitation and physical health equipment on psychiatric wards
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 28 reports of unavailable ECG machines; 490 minutes spent searching (median 10 minutes, longest 120); 4 ECGs not done; 46% missing and 54% faulty machines.
audits.c: Escalation to senior leadership and more ECG machines sourced during the audit period.

audits.t: Audit of Antipsychotic Monitoring in an Old Age Community Mental Health Team in Accordance With NICE Guidelines
audits.st: NICE guidance on routine antipsychotic monitoring (BMI, ECG, bloods, lipids, HbA1c, pulse and BP, LFT, EPSE) over 12 months
audits.f: All offered monitoring (1 declined); blood monitoring 94%; pulse and BP 100%; 29% (5) lacked an ECG despite needing one; 65% (11) not asked about EPSE/movement disorders.

audits.t: Clinical Audit : Supporting Post Detox Abstinence: Discussion of Relapse Prevention Medications by Community Addiction Services Prior to Referral for Inpatient Detoxification

audits.t: From Guidelines to Practice: A Lithium Monitoring Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: NICE guidance and local shared-care protocols for lithium monitoring
audits.f: Urine ACR absent in all patients; serum calcium and thyroid function missed in about 60%; over 10% of results supratherapeutic; renal function not consistently rechecked after high levels.

audits.t: Improving Adherence to the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) Guidance on Documented Driving Advice for Psychiatric Patients Managed by a Home Treatment Team (HTT): A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: DVLA 'Assessing fitness to drive: a guide for medical professionals' – driving advice given and documented
audits.f: Driving advice documented in 25/86 (29.1%); not documented in 61/86 (70.9%).
audits.c: MDT checklist prompt on driving status and advice, patient information leaflet on DVLA advice, presentation at a Learning-From-Excellence meeting, and staff education leaflet and teaching.
audits.r2: Driving advice documented in 76/93 (81.7%); absolute improvement of 52.6%.

audits.t: Audit of SMI Physical Health Checks and Associated Monitoring for Patients Prescribed Antipsychotics Under the Care of the Peterborough Adult Locality Team (PALT)

audits.f: 59% had an SMI physical health check in the preceding 12 months despite 98% engaging with PALT. Core 6 components 78–84%. Antipsychotic blood monitoring 79–84%. Annual ECG 63%. Metabolic monitoring for moderate-high risk antipsychotics 46%; prolactin monitoring 27%.

audits.t: Ethnicity Recording and Equity of Access in Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services: A Re-Audit of East Lancashire CAMHS
audits.st: Original 2020 audit standards: complete ethnicity recording and service users' ethnic composition reflecting the local under-18 population
audits.f: Ethnicity recording completeness approximately 78%; Asian service users significantly under-represented.
audits.r2: Ethnicity recording completeness approximately 88%. Access rates for Asian children about 2-5 vs 12-18 per 1,000 for non-Asian children; observed Asian numbers significantly lower than expected (p < 0.001).

audits.t: Evaluating Adherence to National Standards: A Two-Year Audit of Consent, Clinical Efficacy, and Longitudinal Monitoring in Electroconvulsive Therapy
audits.st: ECT Accreditation Service (ECTAS) standards for consent, capacity and monitoring of target symptoms and cognitive side effects
audits.f: Legal framework and consent documentation met standards; baseline monitoring 100% for all measures, falling below 75% by course completion and declining further at months two and three of follow-up.

audits.t: AUDIT^2 – Identification and Management of Alcohol Use Problems in the Southern Gambling Service: A Full Audit Cycle
audits.st: NICE CG115, Department of Health and Social Care guidance and Royal College of Physicians guidance on alcohol assessment and management by risk bracket
audits.f: Full AUDIT completion 0%, brief interventions 7%, advice on safe alcohol reduction 0%.

audits.t: Improving Admission Clerking and Physical Health Checks in Acute Psychiatric Inpatients. A Quality Improvement Project (QIP)
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: Local and NHS trust admission protocol: clerking, mental state examination, physical examination, ECG and routine bloods all completed within 72 hours of admission
audits.f: All five criteria completed within 72 hours in 27 patients (62.8%); delayed in 14 (33.6%); 2 (4.7%) refused blood tests.
audits.c: Active physical health handover to the physical health nurse and junior doctors, with emphasis on patient rapport.
audits.r2: Overall compliance for physical health checks increased from 62.4% to 96.6% after intervention; reported 1.76-fold increase in timely protocol completion, 1.39-fold reduction in delays and 4-fold drop in patient refusal.

audits.t: Improving Documentation of Driving Status and DVLA Advice in Liaison Psychiatry: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: GMC and DVLA guidance: assess driving status, advise and document
audits.f: Driving status documented in 5%; no documented DVLA advice when indicated.
audits.c: Driving status and DVLA advice prompt added to the assessment template, verbal and email reminders, sharing case learning and visual prompts in the team office (PDSA cycles)
audits.r2: Driving status documented in 50% by week three; DVLA advice provided in 13.6%.

audits.t: Audit of Psychiatric History Taking and Mental State Examination Clerking by Psychiatric Trainee Doctors in North Wales
audits.st: 60 essential criteria derived from the Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry on history taking and mental state examination; 100% target
audits.f: Aggregate compliance 50.6%; administrative tasks 84.3%; objective MSE 68.5%; HOPC 26.4%; past psychiatric history 22.9%; risk assessment 58.1% but risk management plan 8.6%.
audits.c: Planned: training sessions for trainee doctors before re-audit.

audits.t: Monitoring Prescribing for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in Child & Adolescent Mental Health Service (CAMHS): A Clinical Audit
audits.st: NICE: height, weight, blood pressure, heart rate with centiles and growth charts for children on ADHD medication
audits.f: Height and weight 97%; BP and HR 100%; height/weight centiles and growth charts 85%; BP centiles 10%; HR centiles 0%.
audits.c: Results presented at local department meeting and posters of NICE guidelines distributed
audits.r2: Height, weight, their centiles, HR, BP and growth charts 100%; BP centiles 2%; HR centiles 0%.

audits.t: A Mental Health Liaison Core-24 Quality Improvement Project (QIP): Improving Recording of Causes of One-Hour Target Breaches of Referrals to a Mental Health Liaison Team by an A&E Department
audits.st: Core-24 one-hour response target with documented reasons for breaches
audits.f: 32 of 97 referrals breached the one-hour target (33%); 10 recorded a breach reason (30%).
audits.c: Team agreed breach codes; the A&E assessment proforma was amended and emailed to all staff, with posters in the office as reminders.
audits.r2: 20 of 44 referrals breached (45.5%); 9 recorded reasons (45%): staffing 6 (67%), multiple referrals 1 (11%), patient left 1 (11%), other 1 (11%).

audits.t: ADHD Treatment in a Community Mental Health Team: Report of a Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: NICE standards for clinical review and physical health monitoring of ADHD drug treatment
audits.f: 17.2% waiting for initiation and 12.7% in initiation phase; annual blood pressure monitoring 62.0%, annual weight 56.7%; longest wait for initiation 330 days; median initiation phase 92 days.
audits.c: Staff resources reallocated to create a dedicated ADHD clinic with a new process for initiation and shared-care monitoring.
audits.r2: Keyworker allocated 99.7%, diagnosis recorded 99.1%; 12.5% waiting and 20.8% in initiation phase; annual blood pressure 90.4%, annual weight 80.3%; longest wait 125 days; median initiation phase 62 days.

audits.t: Documentation of Driving Status and Driving Advice for Adult Mental Health Inpatients: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Project aim of 10% improvement in documentation of driving status and driving advice within 8 weeks
audits.f: Driving status documented in 48 patients (median 60%); driving advice documented for 10 of 20 drivers (median 50%).
audits.c: Education session for resident doctors on driving regulations; poster prompt in the resident workspace; mandatory driving status field in the discharge meeting template.
audits.r2: Driving status documented in 53 patients (median 83%) with a run chart shift; driving advice documented for 17 of 27 drivers (median 80%).

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project (QIP) to Review Treatment Forms (T2B/T3B) for NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde Community Mental Health Teams (CMHT) Patients
audits.tp: Mental Health Act consent to treatment documentation
audits.st: Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003 and Mental Welfare Commission guidance on T2B/T3B forms
audits.f: Forms and consent uploaded to EMIS 99.8%; clinic letters mentioning treatment orders 85%; referencing treatment forms 14%; medication matching forms 90%; GP Emergency Care Summary correspondence 80%.

audits.t: Optimising Procyclidine Prescribing and Monitoring in Patients on Long-Acting Injectable Antipsychotics: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Trust guidelines: starting dose 2.5mg, review every 3–4 months, attempted withdrawal after 3 months
audits.f: 14/36 (39%) on regular procyclidine; 93% had recorded reviews; 0% on recommended starting regimen; no withdrawal plans documented.
audits.c: Team-wide dissemination of findings and standardised prompts for dose-reduction discussions at reviews.
audits.r2: 18/100 (18%) on procyclidine; dose reduced in 3/18 (17%) and reduction discussed in 4/18 (22%); 44% received active de-prescribing intervention or discussion.

audits.t: Improving the Quality, Accuracy and Consistency of Capacity Assessments Across Inpatient Psychiatric Wards at the Harbour (FC Locality)
audits.st: Mental Capacity Act (2005), MCA Code of Practice, Trust MCA policy and NICE NG97; target ≥80% of assessments meeting all components
audits.f: Decision and time specificity 100%; diagnostic test 77.5%; functional components 70% each; clinical reasoning 60%; correct template use 67.5%; decision-specific framing 60%; outcome stated 92.5%.
audits.c: 30-minute targeted teaching for resident doctors on MCA principles and the capacity template, reinforced through MDT discussions, handovers and optional quick-reference guidance.
audits.r2: Diagnostic test 95%; understand 92.5%, retain 90%, use/weigh 90%, communicate 100%; clinical reasoning, template use and decision-specific framing 92.5%; outcome 97.5%.

audits.t: Embedding Equity Across the Autism Diagnostic Pathway: A Diversity, Inclusion, and Equality Audit
audits.tp: Equality and inclusion in adult autism assessment
audits.st: NHS inclusion health principles, NICE guidelines and inclusive communication principles
audits.f: Strong representation of women, gender-diverse and LGBTQIA+ patients; lower than expected representation of some ethnic minority and religious groups; some inconsistent inclusive language in documentation (no figures given).

audits.t: Improving T3 Medication Authorisation Compliance on an Old Age Psychiatry Ward: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Mental Health Act consent to treatment documentation
audits.st: Mental Health Act medication authorisation (T3) forms: zero administrations outside authorised route or frequency
audits.f: Four off-T3 medication incidents; mean staff knowledge score 58%; confidence 3.7/5.
audits.c: Visual whiteboard above the drug trolley identifying patients with active T3 forms, plus targeted teaching using real incidents.
audits.r2: Zero off-T3 incidents for four consecutive months; knowledge score 71%; confidence 4.3/5.

audits.t: Optimising Referrals: A Closed Loop Quality Improvement on Blood Test Compliance in Memory Clinic Referrals
audits.tp: Memory service referral quality and dementia screening bloods
audits.st: NICE recommended dementia blood tests (FBC, U&Es, LFTs, TFTs, HbA1c, calcium, ESR or CRP, B12/folate) within two months of referral
audits.f: 11.9% of referrals had all recommended blood tests; 27.1% had none.
audits.c: Focus groups with the memory clinic team, information update letter and updated referral proforma distributed to primary care clinicians.
audits.r2: 85.7% of referrals used the proforma; all recommended blood tests in 23.8% overall and in 80% of proforma referrals.

audits.t: Re-Audit of Documentation Practices in the Blossomwood Electroconvulsive Therapy Suite Using a Quality Improvement Approach
audits.st: 20-item ECT documentation checklist; target 100% compliance
audits.f: 100% compliance in 15 of 20 criteria; MADRS 71.4%, MINI-ACE 85.7%, previous treatment failure 85.7%.

audits.t: Audit: Anticholinergic Burden in Patients Newly Referred to the Central Aberdeenshire CMHT (Feb 2024–Feb 2025)
audits.st: Documented intervention to review or mitigate anticholinergic medication when ACB score is 3 or more
audits.f: 73% on at least one anticholinergic; 32.7% (N=69) had ACB 3 or more. 75.4% of these had no documented intervention; deprescribing 8.7%, dose reduction 8.7%, medical review suggested 4.4%, switch 2.9%.
audits.c: None reported yet; recommended routine ACB calculation at assessment, prompted medication review for ACB 3 or more and targeted education. Re-audit planned.

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project on Benzodiazepine Prescribing on Discharge and Compliance with Trust Guidelines
audits.st: SPFT guidelines: 100% with date of initiation and indication recorded, consultant support for continuation, and indication, duration, dose and reducing regimen communicated to GP
audits.f: 12.5% regular and 15% PRN benzodiazepines on discharge; of these 80% on long-term treatment and 40% had documented indication and reducing regimen.
audits.c: Teaching on benzodiazepine prescribing for residents at the start of rotation.
audits.r2: 9% regular and 0% PRN on discharge; 100% consultant supported with indication, duration and reducing regimen documented.

audits.t: Improving Carer Experience and Engagement in a Community Rehabilitation Team: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists standards for community rehabilitation services
audits.f: Only 3/50 (6%) service users had formally recorded carers; survey response 24% (14/58); 93% had emergency contact information, 78% felt supported, 64% felt involved, 50% aware of carers groups, 14% given written information.
audits.c: Bimonthly family, friends and carers support group set up, written carers pack reviewed and definition of carer broadened

audits.t: Audit of Mental Health Assessment in Leicester's Paediatric Emergency Department
audits.tp: Mental health risk assessment in paediatric emergency department

audits.t: Are We Setting Doctors Up to Succeed? A Benchmarking Audit and Quality Improvement Project of Psychiatry Induction Identifying and Addressing MDT Working and Referral Confidence in Intellectual Disability Psychiatry
audits.st: Induction provides new trainees with timely IT access and clear understanding of MDT roles and referral confidence

audits.t: Improving the Interface Between Resident Doctors and the Quality Improvement and Innovation Team at South West London and St George’s Mental Health NHS Trust– A Quality Improvement Informed Approach

audits.r2: 40% not involved in QI projects; of those involved, 100% had QII oversight. QII caseload had 8 active resident doctor projects and 9 enrolled in Streamline QI.

audits.t: Improving Multidisciplinary Team Documentation and Handover in a Long-Stay Dementia Psychiatry Unit: A Quality Improvement Project

audits.c: Co-designed structured MDT template (current issues, better/same/worse progress, named actions with review dates), closed-loop communication and weekly MDT summary sheets for nursing handover, through PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: 100% completion across all measured domains by the second cycle; responsible team 100% and review dates 100%.

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project on the Use of Zopiclone on Elm Ward, West Park Hospital
audits.st: NICE TA77: zopiclone not exceeding four weeks including tapering

audits.c: Practice changes introduced after the initial audit (not described).
audits.r2: Mean duration 3.42 weeks, median 1.29 weeks; 83.3% (10/12) within ≤4 weeks; 30% of evaluable cases met indication-specific NICE durations.

audits.t: Improving Documentation of Side-Effects Discussions by Doctors for Psychotropic Medications in Community Settings: A Single Centre Quality Improvement Project Under the Early Intervention Service, EIS Limbrick Centre
audits.st: Documentation of at least one specific side effect discussed for newly prescribed psychotropic medication; target 100% within 12 months

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Improving Access to Menopause Healthcare for Women with Intellectual Disabilities: A Quality Improvement Project in Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project on Uned Gobaith, the Mother and Baby Unit: Improving Monitoring and Records of Response to Psychotropic Medication on the MBU

audits.t: Safe Prescribing: A Quality Improvement Initiative Promoting Anti-Cholinergic Burden Scoring and Medication Review in a Community Mental Health Team for Older People
audits.st: Local QI target: 90% of eligible patients with documented anticholinergic burden score by January 2026
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Carer Involvement in Liaison Emergency Assessments at Devon Partnership Trust: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: PLAN standards, NICE suicide and safety planning guidance and Triangle of Care; target 90% carer contact and information-sharing form completion
audits.f: Carers not routinely contacted and information-sharing form infrequently completed.
audits.c: QI team including a carer representative; staff survey, driver diagram and change ideas focused on workplace culture, with monthly rolling audit of 5 patients per team.
audits.r2: SPC data initially within normal variability, particularly for documentation; recent positive trend without figures.

audits.t: Audit of Compliance With Section 3 Mental Health Act Capacity Assessment and Three-Month Reassessment in a Psychiatric Inpatient Unit
audits.st: Mental Health Act 1983: capacity to consent assessed on admission and at three months for Section 3 patients
audits.f: Capacity assessment at admission documented in 46.2% (6/13); three-month reassessment in 7.7% (1/13).
audits.c: Planned: automated RiO reminders, targeted staff education and patient information leaflets; re-audit planned.

audits.t: A Quality Improvement (QI) Project to Improve Adherence to Alcohol Dependence Guidelines in an Acute Adult Inpatient Setting
audits.st: Trust Alcohol Dependence Guidelines for assessment and management of alcohol withdrawal
audits.f: SADQ/weekly alcohol intake documented in 44.4%; regular chlordiazepoxide prescribed per guideline in 55.6% (lower for as-required); escalation for clinical review documented in 25%; CIWA-Ar completed in 23.97%.

audits.r2: Authors report improved clinician confidence, recognition and documentation of withdrawal symptoms; no figures given.

audits.t: Improving the Quality of SHO Seclusion Review Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Mental Health Units (Use of Force) Act 2018; target 80% compliance with all domains
audits.f: 75% of reviews met all required criteria.

audits.r2: 83% of reviews met all required criteria; minimal change in overall compliance on SPC chart.

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project for Menstrual Health on Inpatient Psychiatric Wards
audits.tp: Menstrual health screening on psychiatric wards

audits.f: 3/44 (7%) actively screened; 8/44 (18%) had appropriate menstrual health intervention.
audits.c: Staff training, patient information materials and updated clerking prompts.
audits.r2: 28/45 (62%) actively screened; 33/45 (73%) had appropriate menstrual health intervention.

audits.t: Unveiling the Hidden Burden: An Audit Examining Whether National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines Are Followed in the Management of Depression in Primary Care
audits.st: NICE (2022): review within 2–4 weeks of diagnosis, or 1 week if suicide risk; QOF review within 10–56 days
audits.f: 41% (n=23) had a documented review; 25% (n=14) reviewed within 2–4 weeks; 39% met the QOF 10–56 day target. Suicide risk assessment documented in 91%.

audits.t: Improving the Accuracy of Clozapine Documentation in Primary Care Records: A Completed Audit Cycle Within a Community Mental Health Team
audits.tp: Clozapine documentation in primary care records

audits.f: Clozapine on GP repeat prescription 93%; accurate dose and frequency documented 33%.

audits.t: Audit of Sleep Assessment and Management in Older Adults Across Mental Health Services: Impact of a Targeted Educational Intervention
audits.st: NICE NG97 and NG222, NHS and RCPsych guidance on sleep assessment and management
audits.f: Records: 23.3% detailed assessment aligned with guidance, 70% brief mention, 6.7% no documentation; pharmacological management 88.2%. Clinician survey (n=20): 45–50% routinely assessed sleep, 80% no structured tools, 10% sleep diaries, 80% unfamiliar with guidance.
audits.c: Targeted teaching on sleep assessment in older adults and dissemination of guidance on non-pharmacological approaches
audits.r2: Clinician survey only: 90% reported routine sleep assessment, structured tools 81%, sleep diaries 72%, 72% familiar with guidance, 90% offering sleep hygiene advice.

audits.t: Sexual History Taking in Acute Psychiatric Inpatient Admissions: An Audit of Documentation and Clinician Practice

audits.f: Documentation of sexual health and sexual safety below expected Trust standards (figures not reported). 50% of surveyed doctors aware of the policy.

audits.t: Adherence to Smoking Cessation Policy in Inpatient Psychiatric Services at Hamad Hospital: A Retrospective Clinical Audit
audits.tp: Smoking cessation in mental health inpatients
audits.st: Institutional Smoking Cessation Policy (smoking status, dependence severity, NRT initiation and monitoring, education, referral, discharge planning)

audits.t: Trust-Wide Re-Audit on Prescription of Medications in Children Under 18 With Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) at Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust (BCHFT)

audits.t: Evaluating EEG Utilisation and Diagnostic Yield in a Psychiatry-Led Service: An Audit From a Low- and Middle-Income Country

audits.t: Clinical Audit on ECG Monitoring in Patients Undergoing Amphetamine Withdrawal
audits.st: American Heart Association recommendations for ECG monitoring during withdrawal

audits.t: Audit Report on Leave and Observation Documentation in Admission Plans for Out-of-Hours Admissions
audits.tp: Care plan documentation in mental health

audits.t: Shared Care Uptake for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder Medication in Hull and East Riding of Yorkshire: An Exploratory Audit
audits.st: NICE and local prescribing guidance: shared care with primary care after titration and dose stabilisation
audits.f: 62 (55%) had shared care requests; of these 43 (69%) accepted, 13 (21%) no response, 6 (10%) declined.

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Driving Advice on Discharge: An Audit of Compliance With DVLA and GMC Standards in Psychiatric Care

audits.t: Adherence to BNF Prescribing Standards and PRN Governance in an Early Intervention in Psychosis Service: TwoCycle Clinical Audit

audits.t: An Audit on Medical Seclusion Reviews in a Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit

audits.t: Monitoring Compliance With Local Policy: A Re-Audit of Senior Psychiatrist Review of New Admissions Within 48 Hours at Mental Health Unit, Forth Valley Royal Hospital
audits.st: NHS Forth Valley Psychiatry Emergency plan 2023: senior review (ST4-6 or consultant) within 48 hours of admission

audits.t: Goal-Focused Admissions for EUPD: An Audit of the NHFT Complex Emotional Needs Inpatient Pathway

audits.t: A Cross-Sectional Audit of Body Mass Index in the Northamptonshire Early Intervention Psychosis Service

audits.t: Strains on Resident Doctors’ Workloads: An Audit of On-Call Room Conditions and Driving Distances
audits.st: BMA guidance on rest facilities

audits.t: Prescribing Pathways Following Private ADHD Diagnosis: An Audit in Peterborough Adult Locality Team
audits.st: NICE ADHD guideline (2018): prescribing and monitoring after titration under shared care arrangements with primary care

audits.t: Monitoring Oral Hygiene in Inpatient Psychiatric Units: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: Trust inpatient policy: comprehensive physical health assessment including oral health examination on admission, and dental hygiene in ongoing nursing care reviews
audits.f: 'Eating, Drinking and Oral Health' questionnaire partially completed for 61.4% (70/114), fully completed for none. Formal oral health examination recorded for 10.5% (12/114), 0% in forensic unit. No patients had a completed oral health risk assessment.

audits.t: Improving Adult Inpatient Discharge Planning and 72-Hour Follow-Up: A Regional Re-Audit Across Three Mental Health Sites
audits.st: NCISH, NHS CQUIN and Welsh Crisis Care Concordat: follow-up within 72 hours of discharge and discharge documentation of risk, MSE, medication and care plan
audits.f: Previous regional audit found variable compliance and incomplete documentation.

audits.r2: 72-hour follow-up 78.4% (29/37); discharge plan 86.5%; MSE 78.8%; risk assessment 72.7%; medication 63.6%. Modest improvement from baseline.

audits.t: An Audit on the Prevalence of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in the General Adult Community Mental Health Team Caseload and Compliance With the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines on Physical Health monitoring
audits.st: NICE ADHD guidelines: baseline observations, 6-monthly weight, HR and BP, 6-monthly psychiatry review, side-effect assessment

audits.t: Improving Prescribing Documentation in a Community Learning Disability Team: A Clinical Audit and SOP (Standard Operating Procedure) Development
audits.st: Local prescribing documentation standards (upload to Care Director, clinic register entry, case note documentation)

audits.t: Audit Review of Psychotropic Medication of the Caerphilly Psychiatry Community Learning Disability Caseload

audits.t: An Audit Cycle Evaluating Timeliness of Post-Discharge Follow-Up for Patients Discharged From an Adult General Psychiatry Inpatient Ward in Wales

audits.t: Audit of Dna/disengagement Guideline in the North Essex Specialist Community Mental Health Team (Scmht), Essex Partnership University Nhs Foundation Trust (Eput)

audits.t: Timely Completion of Inpatient Discharge Summaries: A Clinical Audit

audits.t: Prolactin Monitoring in Antipsychotic Prescribing: A Trust-Wide Completion of Audit Cycle

audits.t: Sodium Monitoring in Older Inpatients on Antidepressant Therapy, a Clinical Audit and Service Development Project
